News.title: UK hit by fresh wave of asbestos recalls with TWELVE toys pulled from shelves in latest alert
News.content:
TWELVE toys have been included in a fresh wave of asbestos recalls in the UK.

Consumers are urged to stop using the items immediately and keep them out of reach of children.

A number of products have been recalled today by The Office for Product Safety & Standards as the items pose a serious health risk.



All the affected products contain sand that may be contaminated with small quantities of asbestos.



14 items have been recalled today, including 12 toys and doorstops.

The substance is banned in the UK as it poses risks to health, even at low levels of exposure.

Due to the traces of asbestos found in the products, all the affected items do not meet the requirements of the Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011.

Any customers who have bought one of the affected items should stop using the product immediately and keep it out of reach of children.

According to advice given on PMS international, consumers should “place the items in a heavy-duty plastic bag, double tape it securely, label it clearly and store in a secure location out of reach of children”.

If any of the sand has been spilt, the area should be cleaned up using wet cloths to prevent the generation of dust.

Anyone cleaning up the sand should wear gloves and a mask.



Any items worn or used when cleaning up the asbestos-laced sand should also be double-bagged.

Customers who has bought one of the affected items should return the product to the store where it was purchased to receive a refund.

News.title: Is there another heatwave coming in the UK? Latest Met Office forecast and when the hot weather will return
News.content:
BRITS hoping for a return to sunshine won’t have to wait long, with the Met Office dropping hints that another heatwave could be on the way.

While we’ll have to dodge a few showers first – and swap the hosepipe for a watering can – forecasts suggest settled, warm weather is getting ready to make a comeback.

What is a heatwave?

The Met Office uses strict criteria to officially declare a heatwave – it’s not just about a single hot afternoon.



A heatwave is triggered only when a specific temperature threshold is met or exceeded for three consecutive days.



These thresholds vary across the UK to reflect local climates.

For example, London and the Home Counties have a higher bar of 28C, while parts of northern England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland have thresholds set at 25C.

When was the most recent heatwave?

According to the official Met Office criteria, the most recent UK heatwave began on July 4.

While the temperatures obviously varied between regions, some parts of the country remained in official heatwave conditions for a full fortnight.

For example, Bournemouth in Dorset surpassed its threshold temperature of 26C for the 14th consecutive day on Friday July 17.

Temperatures then cooled across the UK over the weekend, bringing the third official heatwave of the summer to an end.

The year’s first heatwave started on May 22, and brought a record-high temperature for the month of 35.1C, recorded in Kew Gardens, London.



This was followed by a further heatwave that began on June 19, which again broke the record for the month’s hottest ever day when the temperature reached 37.7C in Lingwood, Norfolk on June 26.

Is there another heatwave coming in the UK?

According to the Met Office’s long-range forecast, the UK could see a return to “very warm” or even hot spells as we head into August.

Looking ahead from Saturday, 25 July to Monday, 3 August, forecasters say the end of July will feature changeable weather, but high pressure – which could herald a return to higher temperatures – is waiting in the wings.

The Met Office says: “As we approach the turn of the month… there are hints that high pressure could return for a time, which would mean dry conditions resuming, especially in the south.”

It adds that temperatures during this period will be “near or above normal, warmest in the south, and perhaps becoming very warm again by the start of August.”



Moving further into next month, from Tuesday, 4 August to Tuesday, 18 August, the outlook becomes even warmer.

The Met Office says: “Higher pressure is considered generally more likely than lower pressure through August. This means settled and dry weather will likely prevail, especially across the south.”

It highlights that temperatures “will very likely remain above normal, with potential for further hot spells, particularly in the south.”

The average temperatures the Met Office refers to vary significantly across the UK, and you can find your own area using the interactive map here.

Below is a sample of average maximum temperatures around the country for August, alongside each location’s heatwave threshold in brackets:



Kew Gardens, London – 23.37C (28C)

St Austell, Cornwall – 20.36C (25C)

Winterborne, Birmingham – 20.97C (27C)

Rochdale, Greater Manchester – 19.55C (25C)

Durham – 19.87C (25C)

Cardiff, Bute Park – 21.43C (26C)

Edinburgh, Royal Botanic Garden – 19.07C (25C)

Glasgow, Springburn – 18.6C (25C)

Belfast Newforge – 19.4C (25C)

How long will the current changeable weather last?

If you are waiting for uninterrupted sunshine, you’ll need to push through a brief spell of unsettled weather first.

Rain is set to spread southeast across most parts of the UK over the coming weekend, followed by showers and further bands of rain moving through next week.

Winds will remain light to moderate, though occasionally fresh around northern coasts.

But this changeable patch isn’t expected to last deep into August, with the South and South East seeing warmer weather first when temperatures are predicted to rise around the end of the month.

While northern areas may still catch occasional rain or summertime thunderstorms, high pressure building from the south will bring back settled, dry, and warm conditions for the majority of the country.



Where are hosepipe bans in place?

Thames Water has become the latest water supplier to announce a temporary use ban (TUB) covering 10.1 million customers across London, the Thames Valley, and the Home Counties.

Residents will be banned from using hosepipes to water gardens, wash cars, fill paddling pools, or top up hot tubs.

The restriction formally kicks in at 12.01am on Thursday (July 23), but households are being urged to start saving water immediately.

Nevil Muncaster, director of strategic water resources at Thames Water, said: “We would not be taking this step unless it was necessary to protect water supplies for everyone and the environment.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Similar bans are already in place or announced by Southern Water, South East Water, Anglian Water, Affinity Water, and Cambridge Water.



It comes as the Environment Agency revealed large parts of southern, central, and eastern England have moved closer to official drought status following three heatwaves and the driest spring on record.

News.title: US will hit Iran’s nuclear fortress Pickaxe mountain very soon, Trump reveals & says ‘they haven’t seen anything yet’
News.content:
DONALD Trump has threatened to bomb Pickaxe Mountain, where Iran is reported to have moved its nuclear material.

“We’ll be hitting that area very probably pretty soon, and there’s not a not a thing they can do about it,” the US President told reporters in the White House.



Responding to claims by Israel that the Islamic Republic has concealed its stockpiles in a fortified deep-underground complex in the Natanz area, he said the US does not have a record of it.

Trump added: “I think that they may have. We don’t have it on record.



“[But] it doesn’t mean anything unless they have the material.”

Pickaxe is a peak in the mountains surrounding the city of Natanz, and is over 5,000ft high – taller than any mountain in the UK.

Buried 328ft down, the site is heavily fortified, and it is believed that it hosts two tunnel complexes.

Experts assess it as being beyond the reach of the most powerful bunker buster bombs in the USarsenal.

News.title: I rescued my best friend from sinister sex cult where evil leader streamed vile rapes & made his wives have naked fights
News.content:
IDLY scrolling her phone during a quiet weekend away at her parents’, Jenya Reynolds was suddenly stopped in her tracks.

To her horror, she realised she was watching a stomach-churning livestream video of her best friend Jenaé Newell being brutally raped and abused.





Utterly disgusted by what she saw that day in March 2022, Jenya, 35, immediately called the police, but was told said they needed victims to come forward before they could take action.

So Jenya, a support worker from Las Vegas, turned amateur detective and set about gathering as much information as she could about the vile monster she had seen having sex on screen.

In an extraordinary new TV documentary now on Hulu, she reveals how Eligio Bishop was making videos of his supposedly peaceful and healthy life in a Costa Rican paradise, in 2015, which were getting hundreds of thousands of views.

But it quickly emerged that something darker was occurring.

Within his so-called eco-cult, Carbon Nation, he enforced constant nudity, had multiple ‘wives’ who were brainwashed not only into having sex with him on camera but also forced to fight each other on his command.

He is now serving a life sentence for rape, false imprisonment and revenge porn for what he did to Jenaé.

The New Yorker called himself master teacher, then tribal chieftain and ultimately God himself, claiming: “I am the king of the Earth. I’m the Messiah. I’m God returning. I’m Christ.”

Bishop was the only one allowed to use the toilet – his followers had to go outside. He told Rolling Stone magazine: “The human race needs to stop living the way we’re living — for our own survival. I promote living in tune with nature.”





Incredibly, the father-of-four amassed 94,000 subscribers to his YouTube channel, NatureboyTV, and more than 50,000 on Facebook and Instagram.

At times, the cameras were running nearly round-the-clock, turning Carbon Nation into an immersive, nonstop reality show.

In one particularly disturbing video posted from Costa Rica, Bishop said: “I wanted my son to be so pure that he’d never know he was naked. I take baths with my kids.

“I’m naked with my kids. I have sex in front of my kids.

“My son be breastfeeding, I be making love to his mom. That’s how I get down around kids!”

Former followers including a man called Alex Rapaso and another known as Velvet, explain in the four part docuseries how they were made to change their names, hand over credit cards and block all contact with friends and family. They were allowed one vegan meal a day.

“We live away from everything,” Bishop would say in his videos. “We are a cult. I am a cult leader.”

Many followers were recruited from deprived and vulnerable backgrounds.

It has been widely reported how Bishop began to prey on young black people who were feeling marginalised by the first Trump administration, the killing of George Floyd and the Black Lives Matter movement.

Bishop managed to convince them that melanin, which produces skin, hair, and eye pigmentation, has supernatural powers enhanced by the sun.



From 2016 until 2022, he preached the benefits of leaving America to live in idyllic tropical locations, and had a rotating core of between 10 and 20 followers who moved between Costa Rica, Mexico, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, California, Nevada, and Texas, before settling in Atlanta.

Former follower Velvet explained in her TV interview: “People in the minority, we experience extreme poverty, we do not have access to adequate housing, adequate food sources.

“I just didn’t want to be depressed anymore. I didn’t want to feel lonely anymore. I didn’t want to feel invisible. This could be where my life changes for the better.”

And in an exclusive interview with The Sun, Jenya recalled how troubling it was watching the footage of her unsuspecting pal.

She told us: “He livestreamed two girls fighting naked on the beach – he just gave the order, and they started. One bit the other one’s boobs and banged her head against the rocks. I was convinced they would both drown.

“It was unacceptable.”



“He spoke to them in a demeaning way, like they were trash. He told the women they were nothing without him. He told them serving him was their privilege.

“It was a cesspool, everyone was sleeping with everyone else, and they were all convinced Eligio was their best friend.

“I saw him slap a man across the room who tried to feed him a strawberry.

“It was a crazy environment.

“He was recording porn and posting it online, saying it was sex education – it was horrendous to watch.”

After Jenya saw the video of Bishop raping Jenaé, she immediately tried to reach out to her but discovered she had deactivated her phone and social media accounts.

Eventually, Jenya managed to get a message to her via Facebook Messenger. After an agonising two-week wait, Jenaé finally made contact.

“She knew she was being filmed but thought it was for education videos; she had no idea they were being posted online,” Jenya said in our interview. “That was not educational; it was revenge porn.



“When I finally explained to her what had been happening, she screamed.

“I will never forget that scream. For two more weeks, she tried to protect him, but finally, we got him arrested.”

Fellow cult members reveal Jenaé was attacked and raped as she tried to leave.

Aaron tells the documentary: “Jenaé wanted to leave. She was hit that night because she was supposedly disrespecting Nature Boy.”

Another man called Courtney adds: “We were hearing her getting slapped over and over again. The next thing you know they’re having sex.”

Now Jenaé and Jenya are closer than ever, and Jenaé is writing a book about her five-year ordeal.

Bishop, 42, is serving life in prison without the possibility of parole after being found guilty last year of rape, false imprisonment, and revenge porn in respect of Jenaé .

Several of Bishop’s former cult members spoke during his sentencing:

One woman said: “He said my soul belonged to him and there was absolutely no saying no to him.”

Another added: “You were our guy, but now you’re a prisoner as you imprisoned us.”



Bishop still claims he’s innocent and when he spoke to Rolling Stone magazine from prison in 2025 he insisted: “I’m a controversial figure because what I stand for goes against the power structure.”

News.title: Fresh agony for mum as migrant who mowed down daughter, 14, is freed… and riddle over body ‘left in a ditch like animal’
News.content:
HORRIFIED by the “injustice” she was hearing, Trijntje Boes hurried out of the courtroom – after coming face to face with the migrant who mowed down and killed her beloved teenage daughter Tamar.

Last week, asylum seeker Jamal T. – who was behind the wheel when Tamar, 14, died in a hit-and-run in the Netherlands – walked free. But for the Dutch teen’s devastated family, unanswered questions still plague the case.



Why was the Dutch teen’s body found in a ditch? Why were her arms and legs stretched out straight? And if she had rolled into the ditch after being hit – why had the grass not been flattened?

Tragic Tamar left her house at 1am, on July 25, 2020, after a row with her parents over late night use of her laptop.

The sporty teen was struggling with lockdown and, when Trijntje turned the Wifi off so she couldn’t spend all night on TikTok and other sites, Tamar snuck out.



“Tamar hoped to be an air stew­ard­ess. She loved sport, she was very act­ive and always wanted to be busy,” Trijntje said. “The Covid lock­down meant she could not go to school from 8am to 4pm as nor­mal” .

Her frantic parents heard the front door close and immediately went out looking for her but tragically, they didn’t find her.

Tamar was three miles from home when a car ploughed into her – leaving her for dead. Trijntje believes she may have been sitting at the side of the road hoping her dad, who was out looking for her, would pick her up.

Police discovered Tamar’s body at 4am on the verge of a ditch between Marken and Monnickendam, north of Amsterdam.

Shockingly, at the start of the investigation in 2020, Tamar’s mother Trijntje said she was told by the authorities that the driver was German, and not an Iraqi asylum seeker.



She told The Sun: “They knew the driver was an asylum seeker from Iraq and travelling with a group of Iraqi friends – but they were afraid of the public reaction. So they withheld the truth.”

Jamal T., 33, an Iraqi migrant living in central Germany, was driving a Mazda with three other men in the car on the fateful night six years ago.

Trijntje says she was told his nationality and political status was concealed amid fears it could stir up fury within supporters of the anti-immigration Geert Wilders, leader of the Dutch Party for Freedom (PVV).

The prosecution sought just a mere eight week prison sentence for the Iraqi driver, on the basis that he negligently caused a fatal accident, and subsequently fled the scene.



But appearing before the Harlem court, Jamal T. claimed he believed he had driven over “an animal” rather than a person.

Devastated Trijntje, however, blasted his defence as “outrageous” and said the verdict issued made her lose faith in the Dutch legal system.

“At the moment it happened in 2020, the family liaison officer could only tell us what the prosecution allowed them to say. So we were told the perpetrator was a German,” she said.

“But the prosecution knew who it was of course. This later came out.



“They said didn’t want a ‘Wilder’s effect’ in Holland, because they were afraid of the public reaction. This is why we were not told there were four men in the car and they were asylum seekers.

“And now today in court, six years later, everything from the judge was just ‘not guilty, not guilty, not guilty’.

“In court [Jamal T.] claimed he thought that he had run over an animal, then the judge even said: ‘Yeah, I can imagine he thought it was an animal.’

“That’s how it goes here in Holland. After that, my husband and I left the courtroom. We were devastated.”



Trijntje and her lawyer have long maintained that the driver and his three passengers – none of whom were recalled from Germany and made to appear in court – did not just knock Tamar down.

They fear the men physically moved Tamar’s body from the road into a nearby ditch, where it was later found.

After investigating, experts from the Netherlands’ military police force also concluded that Tamar had not just been knocked over by a car, but that her body had been moved.

The family’s lawyer Sébas Diekstra previously said: “There is no other possibility. There was no other person there, no other car. Only those people were there.



“Tamar was lying in the ditch with her legs straight and her hands above her head. Even the grass underneath her wasn’t flattened.

“If she had rolled into the ditch, the grass would have been crushed. So she must have been placed there straight away.”

Police officers who found Tamar on the road said her arms were positioned upward and her legs were extended straight together.

One officer said: “As if she had been laid out.”

Another cop reported seeing what appeared to be a straight-line mark on the tarmac consistent with something having been dragged.



And several of the first officers on the scene also questioned whether the physical evidence fitted the scenario of a straightforward collision.

Lawyer Sébas later concluded: “The traces found and expert findings show that the final position in which Tamar was found cannot be explained by the collision itself.”

“Concrete indications for an alternative scenario are lacking. One must assume that her body was dragged or moved after the collision.”

Trijntje said she believes the men in the car knew they had hit a person – not an animal.

“They hit Tamar, then they drove to the parking place in Marken,” she claimed.



“Two hours later they went back to the dyke close to where Tamar had been hit, and found the police already there.

“And it was here that officers told them to turn left because there was an investigation going on. So they knew exactly what had happened.

“They knew it was never just a small animal they hit. And yet they got away with that.”

The group of Iraqi men had driven to the Netherlands from Germany, where they had applied for asylum.

They had been camping in the Netherlands and later told police the reason they were driving along the country roads in the early hours of the morning, was that they were looking for an open camp site.



Trijntje and her remaining family has always questioned this – especially as there are no camp sites open at that time.

Within a few hours of the crash, however, the group suddenly decided to drive back 450km to Marburg in central Germany, where the car was washed and put up for sale two months later.

But it was not the authorities who revealed any of this to the Boes family. They only became aware of it after doing a search for the vehicle themselves.

Police then found the driver’s Mazda 3 in Germany, and forensic experts recovered Tamar’s DNA from underneath the vehicle.

In June 2021, the public prosecution office initially said the driver would face zero criminal charges and be handed a mere 1,500 euros fine for “careless driving”.



But Trijntje and her family refused to accept this, and lobbied the support of a lawyer.

An ‘Article 12 procedure’ was then triggered – compelling a judge to review the decision of the Public Prosecution Service not to prosecute the suspect for leaving the scene of an accident.

This time the prosecution sought a prison sentence of eight weeks and compensation of 48,000 euros for the bereaved family.

In court last week, only driver Jamal T. had to appear in court, while the fellow passengers remain in Germany.

“They’re just carrying on, living their lives “ Trijntje said.



“The only time they said sorry was during the hearing on June 13.

“They said, ‘Sorry it took so long,’ but they never explained why it took so long. It wasn’t an apology for what happened.”

She recently told the Dutch Times: “My daugh­ter was left in a road­side ditch like a dead animal. You wouldn’t wish that on any­one.’

The prosecution now has two weeks to appeal the acquittal verdict and take it to a higher court.

“We have to keep fighting,” Trijntje said.



“This is about injustice. It’s about lying. It’s about getting away with lies.

“It all sends out a terrible message to the next person who hits someone on the road. They will now think that you can just move the body, keep lying, run away, and you’ll just get away with it.

“Things are going crazy. This isn’t only happening in Holland. It’s happening right across Europe. There is no justice anymore. Good is bad and bad is good.”

News.title: Shocking moment driver boards ferry with a PONY crammed into her tiny Citroen C1 for hour-long crossing
News.content:
THIS is the cruel moment a driver boards a ferry with a pony stuffed in the back of her tiny Citroen C1.

A Swiss motorist took horsepower a bit too literally when she was spotted transporting an actual pony in the back of her car on an Italian ferry.



Dumbfounded tourists on the Pozzuoli to Ischia ferry managed to capture the wild encounter on July 5.

Footage shows the animal enduring the hour-long crossing squeezed into just a few cubic metres of space.



Despite the Swiss woman claiming to have alerted the crew about the pony, no ferry personnel intervened even when witnessing the poor animal squashed in the back.

The video has caused outrage online with one animal activist, Enrico Rizzi calling for the driver to be investigated for alleged animal cruelty.

He said: “How is it possible that nobody stopped that vehicle before it was loaded onto the ferry?

“Is it possible that no employee of the ferry company Medmar Navi Spa saw a pony crammed inside a small car?

“Is it possible that nobody thought it necessary to call the Carabinieri [police]?

“And, if staff really were already aware of the animal’s presence, why was the journey allowed to go ahead anyway, given that we are dealing with a crime?”



Rizzi has reported the incident to the local police in Pozzuoli.

He said only a fool could behave in such an inhumane way towards an animal.

A local MP, Francesco Emilio Borrelli, has called for the animal’s owner to be identified and for the pony to be taken away from them “to protect its well-being”.

Following the shocking discovery, the ferry provider, Medmar Navi, has condemned the incident calling it an “extremely serious and shameful incident.”

They say it is entirely incompatible with their principles, values, and rules.



The company has launched an internal investigation to determine if there was any liability on the part of their staff.

According to the company, initial investigations have already revealed a series of serious operational anomalies, Ansa it reports.

It is understood the Citroen may have boarded the ferry without a ticket.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Medmar Navi said: “No tolerance will be shown to anyone who violates the rules or fails to carry out required checks.”

The company say the incident reflects on the driver’s behaviour and not company policies, which are based on compliance with regulations, safety, and animal welfare.

News.title: Mystery as mummified remains of victim known as ‘Croft Man’ found in multiple bin bags in river after ‘violent assault’
News.content:
GRISLY END Mystery as mummified remains of victim known as ‘Croft Man’ found in multiple bin bags in river after ‘violent assault’

A MAN discovered mummified in multiple bin bags in a river was the victim of a “violent assault”, a coroner ruled today.

Two mummified legs and feet and two mummified arms without hands were found by a dog walker in the River Stour in Suffolk on August 27, 2020.



Police divers later discovered skull fragments, facial bones and two loose teeth in a thin blue plastic bag 150 metres further along the river.

The mystery victim later became known as the “Croft Man” due to where his severed remains were found but his true identity remains unknown.



Suffolk’s senior coroner Nigel Parsley today recorded he died as the result of a “violent assault”.

He said checks had been run against national and international databases for missing people and for criminal activity but there had been no matches.



The coroner also told the court radiocarbon dating indicated he was born before the early 1950s and died in about 2008 to 2012 – so was likely aged in his late 60s to 70s.

Mr Parsley said the removal of the man’s hands and the injuries to his head and face “appear to have been an attempt to hamper his identification”.

He concluded it was “more likely than not the Croft Man was unlawfully killed”.

“We must remember that the Croft Man was somebody’s son,” the coroner continued.



“He lived for 60 to 70 years. He may well have had family, he almost certainly had friends.

“It’s a tragedy we cannot identify him as there must be some loved ones somewhere wondering where their loved one is.”

Dogwalker Julie Dunn-Beechin said she was on a stretch of the River Stour by water meadows when she saw two black bin bags in the water.



She said her attention was drawn to them when her dogs started sniffing in the area and it “didn’t seem right to me”.

Park ranger Samuel Morgan, who was called to the water, said: “[Julie] said she didn’t know if she had been watching too many Midsomer Murders and had a concern about what could be in the bags.”

He told the court the bags had rocks and bricks in and “what looked like a Toilet Duck soap that had partly dissolved”.

Samuel said he saw “through a small hole in the bag what I thought looked like mummified skin and bone” and what appeared to be the ball joint of an arm so he called police.

Superintendent Mike Brown, of Suffolk Police, told the inquest it was estimated the bags were deposited between August 13 and August 19.



A fingertip search of the riverbed was carried out and a dive team found further human remains in a thin blue bag on August 29.

He told the inquest there were bags within bags, filled with shingle, rocks, bricks and soap and air freshener products.

Supt Brown confirmed DNA testing indicated the person was a white northern European male, likely to have been born with blonde or light hair which may have darkened naturally, and blue or green eyes.

“The most likely and preferred hypothesis is that there’s a criminal element,” he said, adding that the injuries inflicted on the skull supported this.

Supt Brown also revealed the manner of dismemberment of the body could suggest someone with “skill in butchery”.



“Our victim has likely met a violent and unnatural death,” he said.

He continued: “Because of the length of storage the individual could have been found in a state by somebody who doesn’t want to come to the attention of police and has tried to dispose of them by throwing them away.”

A pathologist was unable to give a cause of death but found there had been “multiple blows to the head”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dr Ginni Fitzpatrick-Swallow also said the man could have been bludgeoned with a heavy weapon, like a meat cleaver, axe or machete.

She added: “To completely destroy a skull like that seems from a dismemberment point of view unnecessary.”

News.title: Iran hangs two brave young men who offered help to fleeing anti-regime protesters amid brutal crackdown
News.content:
BARBARIC REGIME Iran hangs two brave young men who offered help to fleeing anti-regime protesters amid brutal crackdown

TWO young Iranians have been hanged for opening their doors to anti-regime protesters as Tehran’s tyrants crack down on dissenters.

Erfan Esfandiari, 18, and Gol Mohammad Mohammadi, 23, were executed for helping terrified demonstrators flee the regime’s brutal security forces.



The two men were found guilty of “tying police officers to a road sign with ropes, injuring them with stones, dousing them with gasoline, and setting them on fire”, the regime’s court said.

The Iranian court’s indictment claimed they had “filmed the scene of the killing and transmitted the footage to television channels” abroad.



But local reports from human rights activists said their only crime was sheltering demonstrators during mass protests against the bloodthirsty Ayatollah in January.

Donald Trump share a post with a photo of Erfan, that said: “He did not kill anyone. He did not carry a weapon.



“This is a government that is so terrified of a generation that refuses to be silent, that that it executes teenagers for the act of compassion.”

The US president said: “Young kids – they kill them like they’re nothing, like they’re candy. It’s crazy what they do.”

“They’re just killing people at random.”

The pair were arrested with 57 others during mass protests in January, during which the late Ayatollah presided over the massacre of more than 30,000 of his own people.



Neither reportedly had an independent lawyer during trial.

Iranian Human Rights (IHRNGO) said the pair were hanged at Isfahan (Dastgerd) Central Prison.

The statement did not specify the dates of their arrest or trial, and did not give the men’s ages.

In 2025, the regime executed at least 1,639 people, around four a day.

It was the largest number of executions for any year since 1989, according to the NGOs Iran Human Rights and Together Against the Death Penalty (ECPM).



Iran is responsible for the second most executions of any country, after China, according to Amnesty International.

In 2025, around four people were killed every day.

Most were executed after being accused of drug crimes or murder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But some dissidents were killed on charges such as “waging war against God” and “corruption on Earth,” according to a report by two human rights watch charities.

The brutal executions, mostly hangings, were carried out “after grossly unfair trials and without due process”, according to the report.

News.title: Andy Burnham live: New Prime Minister sets challenge to ministers during his first Cabinet meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham has thrown down the gauntlet, asking MPs to "take that little bit of pressure off people's shoulders" as he sets sights to help ease families facing the cost-of-living crisis

Andy Burnham today chaired his first Cabinet meeting and told his appointed ministers to examine “all possible ways” to help families struggling with high costs.

In a challenge to his top team one their applause had died down, the new Prime Minister said their task was to "take that little bit of pressure off people's shoulders" and show them help was coming so they could have some hope things were improving.

He told the meeting: "That’s the mission that we’ve got to set ourselves together” and asked his colleagues to look into what their department could do to ease cost-of-living pressures, “big and small,” saying: “We need to be a cost-of-living Government, getting that cost of living down, looking at all possible ways of doing that.”

Burnham started today by making good on his promise for “breathing space” for struggling households, a key plinth of his economic plans unveiled in his maiden speech outside No 10 on Monday. The move will see VAT removed from domestic electricity bills from October 1.

Burnham said: “Westminster has not been working for people for too long, with families struggling with the cost of living. That needs to change. I said I wanted to give people breathing space, and that’s what I’m announcing on my second day as Prime Minister. We’re taking immediate action to cut taxes on energy bills, put more money in people’s pockets and bring back hope.”

It is estimated that the change will reduce the annual Ofgem price cap by around £45 from October, with companies expected to pass the reduction onto customers.

Chancellor John Healey said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living. Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter". He continued: “This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”

The fully priced plan from Mr Healey comes as Burnham continues to pad out his cabinet, with a number of key appointments made since yesterday, including Ed Miliband receiving the FCDO brief, Angela Rayner returning as Housing Secretary, and Shabana Mahmood staying on as Home Secretary.

News.title: Andy Burnham might have a Donald Trump problem - but it's not his old online taunts
News.content:
Andy Burnham might have a Donald Trump problem - but it's not his old online taunts

Whether Andy Burnham has a cordial relationship with Donald Trump won't be down to whether he's criticised him in the past. But being chummy with him probably won't help Britain much either.

View 3 Images Donald Trump has been criticised by Andy Burnham in the past (Image: AARON SCHWARTZ/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

Does Andy Burnham have a Trump problem? Well, kind of. Maybe. But it's probably not going to be the problem you think.

‌



We all know Donald Trump loved Keir Starmer. To start with, at least. In fact, European leaders were so surprised at how well Trump and Starmer got on in the early days, given their different political leanings, that Starmer was made kind of an unofficial Trump whisperer.

‌



Anyway, Andy Burnham and Keir Starmer are very much not the same person, and Burnham will be starting from scratch. Until this week, all Trump knew about Burnham was that he was mayor of "some English town."

‌



And after Starmer kinda sorta stood up to him over the Iran war, Trump seems to have soured on the special relationship altogether. I mean, we're not alone in that - there's not many of America's traditional allies that Trump is on particularly good terms at this point. But still, despite the British public really, really hating him - we're frequently told by Number 10, there are valid national security reasons Andy Burnham should pursue a cordial relationship with Trump. For now, at least.

Now, a lot of people bring up the things Burnham has said about Trump before. As recently as 2021, after the January 6th attempted coup, Burnham said: "Any UK politician who gave Trump the time of day should be ashamed right now." Before that, he said he'd refuse to meet with him on principle, and accused him of "sharing extremist material online."

‌



View 3 Images Until this week, Trump only knew that Burnham was mayor of 'some English town' (Image: Chris Ratcliffe/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

But I don't think any of that is a problem. Trump is pretty used to people slagging him off in public, and doesn't really hold grudges like that. If he did, he'd have very quickly run out of people in Washington he could do business with. Keir Starmer should perhaps have worked out slightly sooner that the opposite is also true - having a chummy relationship with Trump didn't mean the US didn't slap us with the same tariffs as everyone else.

People say Trump is transactional, and that he'll make nice with anyone he can do a deal with. That's not exactly true either. 'Transactional' implies both parties get something out of it, and Trump has no interest in giving anything away. Anyway, the bigger problem for Burnham is not Trump himself - it's the people around him.

‌



For example, someone in the administration is not pleased about Burnham picking Ed Miliband for Foreign Secretary. Now, to be clear, Donald Trump has no idea what an Ed Miliband is. And the President doesn't actually have much to do with Foreign ministers - he's in a different orbit. But as Secretary of State, Marco Rubio will have quite a lot to do with Miliband - and it seems like this displeasure with his appointment, anonymously whispered to a right wing newspaper - has probably come from his side of the administration.

View 3 Images Trump soured on the Special Releationship after Starmer stood up to him over Iran (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

This could also pose a problem for Burnham in the unlikely event that Trump leaves office in 2029 like he's supposed to, and Rubio gets elected to replace him. Which is a lot of 'what ifs'...but worth bearing in mind.

Article continues below

Burnham has said he wants to "meet Trump where he's at" - a delightfully meaningless phrase. But people read quite a lot into that and Burnham signalling he'd be "pragmatic" about North Sea drilling - about which Trump has a bee in his bonnet, for various reasons, many of them to do with windmills next to his golf club in Aberdeen.

For now, with Trump not really paying attention to anything west of Turkey, that seems to have been enough to keep him calm. They'll probably meet for the first time in person in September at the UN General Assembly. But 'calm' is the most you can hope for. And if Burnham wants to keep Trump calm going forward, that's the time for him to flutter his eyelashes at him.

News.title: 'We were told our baby boy was dead before he started moving inside body bag'
News.content:
'We were told our baby boy was dead before he started moving inside body bag'

Letícia Cristina da Cruz Santos was told, hours after her baby Noah had been declared dead, that he was actually alive following an incredible discovery by a funeral worker

View 3 Images A baby was found alive hours after being declared dead (Image: Family handout)

A mother who was told her baby had died was informed just hours later that in fact her son was actually alive. On June 15, Letícia Cristina da Cruz Santos had a son called Noah Gabriel da Cruz Santos in Sao Paolo, Brazil.

‌



Noah, who was one month premature, was later transferred to the Santa Casa hospital's Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. He was waiting transfer to another hospital because he needed surgery when he suffered a cardiac and respiratory event.

‌



In a statement following what was to happen, the hospital confirmed that CPR was immediately administered to Noah for 45 minutes. When all efforts to save his life proved unsuccessful, Noah was pronounced dead that afternoon.

‌



The hospital further maintained that all proper protocols were adhered to throughout Noah's time in their care, stating: "The Brazilian protocol for confirming death is recognised for its high standards of rigour and safety."

Letícia, who witnessed the event, later took to social media to speak about what had happened while praising the hospital's care of Noah during his lengthy stay there.

View 3 Images Noah was born earlier this year (Image: Family handout)

‌



She said: "We are contemplating God's greatness and admiring our little warrior, who continues to fight to get well. We fully believe in our miracle [...] miracles can't be explained; they must be experienced.

"Sometimes I feel like we're dreaming, not just me; I was talking to my husband just a little while ago inside the hospital, looking at him [Noah] as he moved around, kicking his little legs with his eyes open.

"We're just in awe. I actually witnessed the moment it happened, how the doctor reacted and how hard she fought to try to resuscitate him."

‌



Sadly, Noah was declared dead after attempts to save his life failed. However, hours later, funeral worker Regina Célia Paschoal discovered the infant moving inside the body bag in which he had been placed.

Speaking to EPTV, Regina, who has amassed 17 years of experience in her field, recalled the chilling moment: "I opened it, and the baby started moving even more; he was making a noise, as if trying to breathe."

Mattheus Batagello, Regina's colleague, corroborated her account, revealing that they initially questioned whether something else might be causing the movement: "It was a desperate moment, but also a relief, you know?"

‌



He explained that he alerted fellow nurses to examine Noah after hearing "a sort of hiccupping sound". Once it was confirmed that Noah was alive, he was immediately readmitted to the neonatal unit for intensive care to aid his recovery.

View 3 Images Noah was born premature (Image: Family handout)

Meanwhile, Leticia also addressed the moment she found out her son was alive after previously saying that she and her husband spent roughly an hour with their son following his passing. She also recalled the extraordinary moment she learnt her boy was alive, as reported by G1.

Article continues below

She said: "When we arrived, we went back into the ICU, and they told us about our miracle. All I could do was say 'Glory to God' and weep."

In a remarkable twist of fate, Noah's miraculous revival occurred on the very day he was originally due to be born, having entered the world a full month prematurely.

News.title: 'I'm a professional dog trainer - there's a fascinating reason dogs tilt their heads'
News.content:
'I'm a professional dog trainer - there's a fascinating reason dogs tilt their heads'

A canine behaviourist has shared the science behind dogs tilting their heads, branding it "fascinating" while also explaining its close link to the bonds between a dog and their owner

View Image Many dogs tilt their heads when their owner speaks to them (stock image) (Image: Tatyana Consaul via Getty Images)

Many dog owners will have spotted their pet tilting their heads when speaking to them and, while it's commonly regarded as a cute and endearing habit, there's a "fascinating" reason behind it. A professional dog trainer has shared how it could even offer insight into the depth of a bond between owners and their dogs.

‌



There's lots of popular choices when it comes to pets, from cats, rabbits and guinea pigs to ferrets, snakes and even birds. But dogs are arguable one of the most beloved options, with millions of proud owners across the globe choosing them as the perfect addition to the family.

‌



With a huge variety of breeds and sizes available, dogs are universally celebrated for their loyalty, affection and unwavering companionship.

‌



Many owners are eager to better understand their furry companions, delving into the reasons behind certain quirks and behaviours. Social media has become a go-to resource for guidance and advice, with fellow owners, vets and industry experts all sharing their knowledge online.

Canine behaviourist Will Atherton has built up a devoted following across social media, regularly posting videos that draw on his extensive experience and expertise working with dogs.

In a clip posted to TikTok, Will detailed the reason behind the common behaviour of head tilting.

‌



Will began: "The reason your dog tilts their head when you talk to them is way more fascinating than most people realise."

He then gestured towards his much-loved dog Sully, as the footage cut to scenes of Will alongside his dogs.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The trainer went on: "Take young Sully here. He does it constantly, and every single time someone sees it, they go absolutely mad for it.

"'Oh, isn't that adorable? Isn't he clever?' And yes, he is adorable, but there is real science behind what is happening in that moment - and understanding it will actually make you a better dog owner."

Will then went on to explain what a dog might be attempting to communicate when they tilt their head.

‌



He said: "When your dog hears your voice, they are doing two things simultaneously.

"They are trying to locate the precise source of the sound, and they are trying to read your facial expressions and lip movements to gather as much information about what it is you're trying to communicate.

"The tilt physically adjusts the position of their ears to improve directional hearing, and it also moves the muzzle out of their line of sight so they can see your face more clearly."

‌



What else does it mean when a dog tilts their head?

Will went on: "Now, here is the part that really matters. Dogs that have a stronger bond with their owner tilt their heads more frequently.

"It's not a random quirk. It is a sign that your dog is genuinely engaged with you and that they are trying to understand you, and that they see you as a source of meaningful information."

Will added: "Sully's got a beautiful soul, and that head tilt of his tells me everything that I need to know about where we are in our relationship.

Article continues below

"So the next time your dog does it, do not just melt and move on - recognise it for what it is: your dog working hard to connect with you.

"Lean into that, work with it more, engage with them more and build that relationship through it more. It is the foundation of everything."

News.title: 'My sister was stabbed to death — strangers have given my desperate family solace'
News.content:
'My sister was stabbed to death — strangers have given my desperate family solace'

The grieving family of Kirandeep Kaur say the support shown by strangers following the 24-year-old’s death has brought them comfort during an unimaginable time

View 2 Images Kirandeep Kaur was stabbed to death (Image: Family Handout)

The brother of a woman stabbed to death as she lay beside her husband and baby has spoken of his family’s heartbreak.

Her family, who are thousands of miles away in India, say the vigils held in west London have brought them comfort as they continue to wait for Kirandeep Kaur’s body to be returned home. The 24-year-old woman was killed at her home on Uxbridge Road in Hayes in the early hours of July 12.

Speaking through a translator from the family’s home in Punjab, her eldest brother Paljinder Singh said seeing people come together in Kirandeep’s memory had helped them through their grief. He said: “If we’d known what was going to happen, we would never have let her go."

View 2 Images Tributes have been made to Kirandeep (Image: Family Handout)

The family are now hoping Kirandeep’s body can be returned to India so they can say one final goodbye. He said: “I will never speak to her on the phone again, but I want to see her one last time."

The 24-year-old had moved to Britain two years ago to study at Buckinghamshire New University before later finding work at a grocery store after plans to settle in Canada fell through. Her family, who live in Tarn Taran in Punjab, had never imagined London would become her home.

Speaking through a translator, he said: “We never thought when she left, just two years ago… we never thought she would never come back.” He added: “She was a lovely person. If you asked anyone in the village, they would say that.

“She would never say anything bad about anybody. She never said no to helping anyone. When she was near, everything was lovely. After what has happened, things will never be normal again. All my life, I will never forget her.”

Her death sparked a series of marches and vigils across west London, where members of the community gathered to remember the graduate and stand alongside her loved ones.

Article continues below

Although thousands of miles away, Singh said the support had brought the family comfort. He said: “We were very grateful to hear about the vigils. Everyone got together to raise the case. Hopefully, this will not happen to another family.”

Daniel Sean James, from west London has been charged with murder, attempted murder and possession of a bladed article. Prosecutors allege he attacked Kirandeep inside her home before jumping from a window and breaking both ankles. He was later detained by police nearby.

James appeared at the Old Bailey by videolink from Wormwood Scrubs on Thursday where Judge Nigel Lickley KC remanded him in custody. He is due to enter pleas on October 1.

News.title: M25 traffic live: Major delays anticlockwise after lorry crashes into embankment
News.content:
Delays of over an hour are expected after congestion on J6 of the M25 is reported to stretch back for seven miles.

A large section of the M25 has come to a standstill after a lorry crashed into an embankment, sparking major delays with emergency services rushing to the scene.

The crash happened anticlockwise on Junction 6 at Godstone and Clacket Lane Services at around 10am this morning, resulting in the closure of two of the motorway's four lanes.

Significant queues have been building in the area, with delays of up to 60 minutes and around seven miles of congestion reported in the area.

News.title: Postman reveals unbelievable thing one woman said when she answered the door
News.content:
Postman reveals unbelievable thing one woman said when she answered the door

Postman Reece Petch has gone viral on TikTok after sharing a funny story about what one woman said to him when he turned up at her home with her parcels. "I just had the funniest thing ever," he said.

View Image Ordering a lot of things online can result in you becoming very familiar with your local postie (stock image) (Image: Moment Editorial/Getty Images)

Where would we be without Britain's dedicated army of postal workers? Rain or shine, whether battling a record-breaking heatwave or soaking wet from a downpour, they're always out on their rounds ensuring our important - and sometimes not so important - letters and parcels reach our doors.

‌



Postman Reece Petch, who regularly documents his day-to-day experiences on his rounds via social media, shared a hilarious tale on TikTok, where he boasts more than 15,000 followers. Speaking directly to the camera, Reece said: "I just had the funniest thing ever.

‌



"A woman that I delivered to, she always has a parcel, I knock on the door. Usually when I answer, when people answer the door to me, I'm like 'Oh, hi, you alright?'"

‌



However, the woman's reaction caught Reece completely off guard. He said: "She just went 'shh!'", reports Lancs Live.

"They don't have, like, a baby or anything. So I was like, oh, like, maybe they're looking after a baby or, like, something. someone's sleeping or whatever. I was like 'Oh, sorry, sorry'.

"[She] just looks at me with this sort of look where she's like, she's whispering fully. She's like 'I'm not meant to be getting any parcels'.

‌



"I literally just went 'Oh, okay'. And the funny thing is, I parked up, she came to the door without me knocking. So she actually has been anticipating my arrival, so that I wouldn't knock on the door to get her husband's attention."

As it happens, Reece actually has a personal connection to the woman, which could result in her husband discovering her secret. "Her husband is actually friends with my dad," he said.

"[If] he ends up seeing this somehow, or I don't know how, but, like, that would be really funny. But your missus is buying parcels. Not to bait her out or anything. Unless she's banned herself, but then she won't be whispering to herself. I don't know. I find it quite funny."

‌



Reece went on to say that "so many people" confess to feeling guilty about how much they shop online. "You get the people that you go to all the time, and they look like they feel ashamed of themselves," he said.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"When you're close to your postie, that's when you know you've probably got an addiction to ordering parcels. Hey, I'm here for it. I don't care. I gotta go around this area anyway, so if I gotta deliver it, I gotta deliver it."

‌



Wrapping up, he said: "If you want to be discreet about your parcels, or if you're banned from buying parcels, just wait for my arrival. And 'shh', easier said than done."

Viewers shared their own amusing encounters with postal workers and other delivery staff in the comments. One wrote: "I've got my postie on fb (Facebook), he'll message me when he's on his way to check I'm in."

Another user said: "I ordered everyday when on matt leave then there was one week where I didn't order anything. My post lady actually came to see if I was ok. Knocked on my door and was genuinely concerned."

Article continues below

A further commenter added: "My local Evri driver told my boyfriend before Christmas 'is she done ordering so I can go on holiday now?' I'm embarrassed."

News.title: Donald Trump 'will allow Tate brothers to be extradited to Britain'
News.content:
Donald Trump 'will allow Tate brothers to be extradited to Britain'

A total of 28 new charges with authorised against Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, by the Crown Prosecution Service

View 2 Images Tristan and Andrew Tate (Image: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP via A)

The White House has reportedly refused to intervene to prevent Andrew Tate and his brother from being extradited to Britain.

Donald Trump will not step in to stop the brothers returning following their arrest in Miami, reports The Telegraph. The social media influencer and his younger sibling Tristan Tate were detained by US police on Saturday at the request of British detectives who are seeking their extradition to face trial over allegations of rape and human trafficking.

Their arrest was met with calls from some leading Republican figures and administration individuals for Trump to step in. Their lawyer, Joe McBride has claimed they are victims of a "politically motivated witch hunt".

The Telegraph has now said a US official told the paper that the White House will not get involved in the case. The official reportedly said: "The White House has no involvement and no feelings on the issue."

The pair have "unequivocally" denied wrongdoing, with Andrew Tate describing himself and his brother as "very innocent men".

View 2 Images A courtroom sketch of Andrew and Tristan Tate appearing with their attorneys before judge Lauren Louis in Miami federal court on July 20 (Image: AP)

When the Tate's were first arrested in Florida last year following a period of house arrest in Romania, Andrew Tate suggested in leaked texts that the Trump administration had helped him and his brother to flee the country.

Trump said he knew "nothing about it" when he was asked about this at the time. A total of 38 new charges with authorised against Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, by the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

Andrew Tate was charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Tristan Tate was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.

Charges were previously authorised by the CPS following a file of evidence submitted by officers from Bedfordshire Police into allegations dating back to 2012.

Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Major Crime Unit have been continuing to investigate a number of other alleged offences reported to both Bedfordshire Police and Hertfordshire Constabulary.

Article continues below

The total number of charges against the brothers now totals 59. Of these, 42 charges have been authorised against Andrew Tate, and 17 against Tristan Tate.

The CPS confirmed it had requested the extradition of Andrew and Tristan Tate from the US. Malcolm McHaffie, head of the CPS's Special Crime Division, said: "We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child.

"These charging decisions followed receipt of a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and bring the total number of alleged victims in this case to seven." The offending is alleged to have taken place between July 2010 and August 2017, according to the CPS.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe was hit on head 21 times with hammer, prosecutors say
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times at her home as she ate lunch in an attack that was caught on camera, prosecutors have told Westminster Magistrates' Court.

Prosecutor Kashif Malik said the man charged with her murder, Joshua Kerry, arrived at her house on 8 July in a red Vauxhall Corsa and entered through the front door.

Kerry, who prosecutors say was in the property for two minutes and was wearing black gloves, then allegedly hit Widdecombe repeatedly with a hammer in her kitchen, tipped her from her chair and took her wallet before driving off.

The 28-year-old from South Yorkshire later also appeared at the Old Bailey and was remanded in custody.

At the Old Bailey hearing, prosecutor Alistair Richardson said the attack on Widdecombe had been carried out with a "ferocity of violence".

Malik told the court that Widdecombe did not attend a pre-arranged online interview with Channel 5's Matt Allwright show that had been scheduled for just before 13:00 BST on 8 July.

The show's production team tried to contact Widdecombe through her personal assistant, who then asked Widdecombe's gardener to check on her, the court heard.

Prosecutors said the gardener entered the house via the open front door on 9 July and found Widdecombe lying face down on her kitchen floor with a serious head injury.

News.title: London-based civil servants offered move to No 10 North in Manchester
News.content:
Civil servants working for government departments based in London have been offered relocation packages to encourage them to move to the North of England, the BBC understands.

It comes as the first details are emerging about the new No 10 North, which Downing Street says is already up and running.

The BBC has been told that the Northern branch of Downing Street will be overseen by cabinet minister and ally of Burnham, Louise Haigh.

Haigh, who is the first secretary of state, is thought to have been asked to lead a new Office for the Prime Minister and the Cabinet (OPMC), which will give her control of key decision-making bodies across government.

The OPMC will include No 10, No 10 North and teams within the Cabinet Office.

Addressing his cabinet for the first time, Burnham said No 10 North was "not a gimmick" and that the "time for resisting devolution was over".

A No 10 spokesman said the prime minister was expecting to work from No 10 North "at least one day a week" subject to government business.

Announcing the changes,, external which will also establish a new AI taskforce, Leader of the House of Lords, Baroness Angela Smith said No 10 North would be a "dominant driver of the UK's economy".

It is understood that the initial location of No 10 North will be Heron House in central Manchester, in the same building which houses offices for the intelligence service GCHQ. Specialist police officers have been seen guarding the building.

It is likely that the longer term base for No 10 North will be at a new government "Digital Campus" which is under construction in the Ancoats area of Manchester. It is not due for completion until 2032.

However, a good indication of what it could look like comes from a new report, released on Tuesday.

The blueprint has been authored, external by the Re:State think tank which Burnham was involved with until he stepped down as mayor of Greater Manchester.

News.title: Argentina's Fernandez defends team after ugly scenes in World Cup final loss to Spain
News.content:
Midfielder Enzo Fernandez has claimed Argentina represented their nation "in the best possible way" during the World Cup, despite ugly scenes during and after their final loss to Spain.

Fernandez was sent off late in normal time for two yellow cards and Spain won 1-0 after extra time on Sunday in New Jersey.

His first booking was for showing dissent towards Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic and Fernandez was later dismissed for catching Pau Cubarsi with a challenge that sent the defender cartwheeling in the air.

But, in a statement on social media, the Chelsea midfielder did not mention the red card and said: "As time goes by, you realise there is something much bigger than just a result.

"For years, this group has represented the team in the best possible way. It teaches that competing isn't just about winning; it's about giving your all for the jersey and never giving up.

"It has been a privilege to be part of a group that always stepped up, competed at the highest level, and defended these colours with pride, humility, and commitment."

News.title: Parts of the UK move closer to drought
News.content:
Summer so far has been exceptionally hot and dry across much of the UK, with three widespread heatwaves and the longest run of dry days in central England since 1995. England, Wales and eastern Scotland have been the driest areas over recent weeks, and this follows a very dry spring in similar regions.

England has received only 3% of its long-term average July rainfall with the south and east of England seeing no rain at all. Wisley in Surrey has seen 33 consecutive dry days.

Rainfall so far this summer has been below average across the UK as a whole, but there has been large regional contrast.

Up to the middle of summer - 15 July - parts of eastern and north-eastern England had received just 26% of their total expected summer rainfall. Areas of northern and western Scotland had more than average for the first half of the summer, though.

In Wales, where just 5% of July rainfall has fallen, Natural Resources Wales has moved the worst affected regions in the north and south-east into "prolonged dry weather status", the first step in its drought plan.

Comparisons are being made with last summer, when drought was declared across much of England, Wales and eastern Scotland. It officially ended just four months ago.

This year, drought has not developed as quickly because heavy rainfall recharged our aquifers, rivers and reservoirs during a very wet autumn and winter.

However, the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology says flash droughts, external with a sudden transition between wet and dry conditions are "likely to happen more often, and be more intense".

As the effects of human-induced climate change continue, the Met Office expects our summers to become hotter and drier, external in the future. In fact, by 2070, our summers could be up to 60% drier and 1-6C warmer compared to 1990.

News.title: Thames Water announces hosepipe ban for 10 million
News.content:
Thames Water has announced a hosepipe ban affecting 10.1 million customers after an "exceptionally warm and dry spring".

The restrictions mean, from Thursday, hosepipes should not be used for watering gardens or allotments, cleaning cars, filling paddling pools or swimming pools, or cleaning windows.

The water company said its region had seen 40% of average rainfall, and more days at or above 34C this year than ever recorded before.

Nevil Muncaster, director of strategic water resources, said: "We would not be taking this step unless it was necessary to protect water supplies for everyone and the environment."

The ban applies to all customers that Thames Water supplies with drinking water and comes into effect on Thursday.

The company provides water to customers across parts of Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Surrey, the Thames Valley, Greater London, and the surrounding areas, external.

It provides water and wastewater services to 16 million customers overall.

It said water use was currently 10% above normal in the Thames Valley and Home Counties and 7% above normal in London, which amounted to an extra 100 million litres of water every day.

News.title: Russian warship carried out firing exercise off Plymouth coast
News.content:
The live-fire exercise took place in international waters and lasted for 30 minutes.

The Russian warship requested that the Royal Navy's HMS Tyne reposition to a safer distance, which it did.

The Russian frigate was also being monitored by a French military aircraft which made radio contact with the warship asking it to clarify its intentions, the BBC has been told.

BBC Verify has analysed flight and ship-tracking data which shows the position of HMS Tyne and several British military aircraft operating in and around the Channel near Plymouth on Monday.

Flight data on ADS-B Exchange indicates at least four Royal Air Force and Royal Navy aircraft were flying off the coast of Dorset mostly above the UK's territorial waters, including two Eurofighter Typhoons, a Voyager air refuelling tanker and a Super Lynx helicopter.

A French military H160M GuÃ©pard helicopter also flew out and over the Channel during the afternoon. It is not clear if this is the aircraft which made contact with the Russian warship.

Data on ship-tracking service MarineTraffic shows HMS Tyne began to broadcast its location about 40 miles off Plymouth at 13:57 BST on Monday. It remained in that location for around two hours before departing at 15:56 to return to Plymouth.

HMS Tyne has been tracking Neustrashimy since at least 16 July when both vessels were also captured in the North Sea about 36 miles miles from the port of Felixstowe in Suffolk on a satellite image.

The incident will be a reminder for the new prime minister of increased Russian naval activity near UK waters in recent months.

Last month, Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in a six-hour operation which was the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

Also in June, a British couple in international waters in the English Channel came across a Russian warship - Admiral Grigorovich - 23 miles off the Isle of Wight.

The frigate fired warning shots as Jane and Alan Kelvey sailed their yacht on what Russia's defence ministry said had been a "dangerous approach". However, the couple said they had not been on a "collision course".

Russian warships regularly pass through international waters in the Channel, which are separate from UK and French territorial waters.

Tom Sharpe, a retired Royal Navy commander, told BBC Radio 4's World At One programme it was "very unusual" to conduct a gunnery exercise so close to the south coast.

"It is entirely allowable but in my mind it is a signal," he said.

Apart from the warning to HMS Tyne, the Russian vessel did not put any safety measures in place before firing a 100mm cannon, he said.

"One of the issues with firing a weapon of that calibre is that it can ricochet for miles, perhaps over ten miles beyond its intended landing point," Sharpe added.

"You are in the busiest shipping lane in the world and who knows where it is going?"

Asked how the UK should respond, the retired commander said: "You could argue that this was them responding to us because we've upped the ante in the Channel, we boarded the [MV] Smyrtos, one of their dark fleet ships, which is now at anchor off the south coast.

"So we are in this tit-for-tat, which is kind of Cold War normality. We've just forgotten that this sort of stuff used to happen all the time but we need to acknowledge that it is getting closer and closer to the UK."

Additional reporting by Ella Kipling, Barbara Metzler, Thomas Spencer and Patrick Jackson

News.title: Ryanair boss says 'foreign object' may have caused plane window incident
News.content:
An incident on a Ryanair flight which saw a passenger partially sucked out of a plane window may have been caused by "foreign object damage" to an engine, said the airline's boss.

Michael O'Leary said an initial investigation into the incident on 10 July between Greece and Germany suggests "it looks like a foreign object damage to the engine on takeoff at Thessaloniki but ... we can't say that definitively".

He insisted that the engine on the 18-year-old Boeing 737 plane had been fully serviced and overhauled in the past two years.

Serbian national Ljubisa KaroviÄ's head and right shoulder were sucked out of the plane's window, leaving him "seriously injured and in shock".

His wife Svetlana GrkoviÄ MaksimoviÄ told BBC Serbia that she and two other passengers held on to his legs for several minutes.

She said: "We pulled him back together. His entire face was deformed and blood was pouring from his nose and mouth."

He was taken to hospital after the plane made an emergency landing.

Passengers told local media they heard "some kind of explosion" on board.

The aircraft was operated by Ryanair's subsidiary Malta Air.

Confirmation that the damage was caused by an external object could affect Ryanair or Boeing's liabilities over the incident.

The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating. O'Leary said that a draft report would be issued in about 28 days.

News.title: Lindt's Easter chocolate sales fall after price hike
News.content:
Lindt has partially U-turned on its decision to hike prices after Easter chocolate sales dropped.

The Swiss chocolate maker said a "necessary groupwide" price surge of 11.8% was one of the reasons revenue shrank in the first half of this year, particularly in the UK, Germany, and Switzerland.

It also blamed weaker Easter demand and a drop in tourism from Asia and the Middle East "due to geopolitical uncertainties". In response, it said it has adjusted prices and boosted marketing in certain regions for the second half of the year.

Around Easter, Lindt is known for its chocolate rabbits wrapped in gold-coloured foil and decorated with a red ribbon and bell on their necks.

Overall, the company's sales dipped 0.9%, with European sales down by 2.1%. It added that "performance was impacted by more price-sensitive and mature markets such as Germany, Switzerland and the UK".

By volume, meaning the amount of chocolate sold rather than the money it made, overall sales sank 7.5%. Pre-tax profit fell 1.5%.

Meanwhile, sales of Lindt chocolate in airports decreased "due to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, and therefore declining passenger traffic".

Lindt said it sales picked up in North America, Australia, China, and Japan, though these countries account for a much smaller slice of its sales than Europe, where it makes over half its revenue.

Lindt chief executive Adalbert Lechner said: "The actions we have initiated focus on volume recovery in the second half of 2026 and lay the foundation to regain volume growth momentum in 2027."

Lindt is not the only chocolate firm which has been putting prices up.

Experts say climate change has led to extreme rainfall and droughts which have decreased cocoa farmers' crops.

This pushes up costs of making chocolate, and companies have chosen different ways to react to this, with some reducing chocolate content or sizes rather than raising prices.

According to the latest official data, the annual rate of chocolate and sweet price rises is 7.9%, external â much higher than the general rate of UK inflation at 2.8%, external.

News.title: Family of woman who lay dead in crash for days confronts mechanic who falsified MOT
News.content:
Angry scenes erupted outside court after the family of a woman killed in a car crash confronted a garage owner who falsified an MOT just weeks before.

Neil John Lewis, 47, pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on Tuesday, and admitted he knew the car was "dangerous".

Eve Smith, 21, Darcy Ross, 21, and Rafel Jeanne, 24, died when the car given the false MOT crashed into woodland in Cardiff in March 2023. They lay undiscovered for two days. Two others survived.

As Lewis left court, the family of Ross brandished a framed photograph the dead woman, and shouted at him: "Darcy Ross, remember her name."

News.title: 'Significant hot spots' remain at Cairngorms wildfire
News.content:
Hot spots remain at a wildfire which has burned across 10 square kilometres of land in the Cairngorms over the last week, according to the fire service.

More than 100 firefighters have been involved in the operation to control and extinguish the fire, which started near Ryvoan Bothy, south of Nethy Bridge, last Wednesday.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said on Sunday that they had "surrounded" the large-scale blaze.

However, they say "significant hotspots remain across a large and complex landscape" and crews will stay at the scene until the incident is brought to a safe conclusion.

News.title: Boy, 15, accused of sex attacks on eight girls
News.content:
A 15-year-old boy charged with sexual offences against eight girls, including one who was 10 years old, has appeared in court.

The complainants were aged between 10 and 15 at the time, Wellingborough Youth Court heard.

The teenager, who cannot be named because of his age, faces 22 charges relating to alleged incidents between 2023 and 2025, including rape.

He was not asked to enter any pleas during a 20-minute hearing, before the case was sent to Northampton Crown Court for 18 August.

The defendant, who was accompanied by his mother, was released on bail.

Details of where the offences took place have been withheld to protect the alleged victims' right to anonymity.

The boy has been charged with:

Twelve counts of sexually assaulting a female

Three offences of assaulting a girl under 13 by touching

Two counts of rape and a further two of making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child

Assaulting a female by penetration

Possessing a prohibited image of a child and possessing an extreme pornographic image or images

District Judge Amar Mehta told the boy: "Your case is too serious to be tried in this court."

His bail conditions included not to contact the alleged victims and to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16.

The boy spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address. He also asked the judge to explain what the Youth Justice Service was.

News.title: B&M fined £2m over mice infestations
News.content:
B&M Retail Ltd has been fined Â£2m over mice infestations at three Birmingham stores where inspectors found rodent-gnawed foodstuffs and droppings near children's toys.

The company was prosecuted for food hygiene offences by Birmingham City Council after complaints led to inspections being carried out between November 2024 and October 2025.

Locations included St Andrew's Retail Park where officers found gnawed products on sale, the council said.

Mouse infestations were also found at Priory Square Shopping Centre and The Fort Shopping Park.

The council said complaints included one from a member of the public "who reported seeing a mouse in the shop" at Priory Square.

Other transgressions there included urine contamination from rodents on food packaging and shelving, inadequate cleaning standards and structural defects allowing pest entry.

A Hygiene Emergency Prohibition Notice was served and the store was closed immediately, the council said.

A further inspection took place at B&M's store at The Fort Shopping Park in Erdington on 27 October 2025 following a complaint alleging a mouse infestation.

Officers found widespread evidence of mouse activity throughout the premises, including mouse droppings "in close proximity to children's toys on display", the council said.

The store was also closed due to the risks posed to public health.

News.title: Met investigating fatal balcony fall, coroner told
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has opened a corporate manslaughter investigation after a man died following a fall from the balcony of his flat in central London.

Joshua Robbins, 23, leant on the balcony railings of his home in Holland and Thurston Dwellings, Holborn, when it gave way on 26 January. He had been checking on a pizza delivery for him and his father Will Robbins.

The pre-inquest review at St Pancras Coroner's Court heard that Islington and Shoreditch Housing Association (ISHA) was assisting the police with its requests for material.

Joshua's mother, Fiona Garrett, 46, previously said she was seeking answers about her son's death, as his father was "extremely traumatised" after seeing the fall.

A forensic engineer attended the scene and CCTV footage was gathered following the fatal fall.

Det Insp Mark Paterson said: "It's an ongoing investigation. A lot of the material is held by ISHA, who are fully compliant with requests that are being made at this stage."

He said the court could expect an update by January. Senior coroner Mary Hassell scheduled a further pre-inquest review for 6 January 2027.

Previously, Garrett said she had emailed her son's MP, former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer, requesting a meeting as part of her campaign for answers.

She said she was pleased his office "came back straight away" and began asking for further information.

She said: "I thought, 'Oh well, if I get a reply it would just be your bog-standard, written-by-someone-else response and he just won't even know that it's gone out', but the fact that he wrote it, so he actually signed it himself at the bottom and wrote a little bit extra, it did seem really genuine.

"When I showed Will, he was just like, 'Oh my God, the prime minister knows who our son was'."

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said inquiries remain ongoing and officers continue to liaise with the Crown Prosecution Service and are keeping the family updated.
