News.title: Laos methanol poisoning charges 'slap in face' for families
News.content:
The brother of a British tourist who died in a mass methanol poisoning says the failure to charge anyone over her death is a "slap in the face".

Simone White, 28, was one of six people who died after drinking free shots at the Nana Backpacker Hostel in Vang Vieng, Laos, in November 2024.

Last week authorities in the South-East Asian country said they couldn't determine if the deaths "were caused by the actions of any individual or by any particular cause, because no autopsies were conducted".

Simone's brother, Zak told BBC Newsbeat he found the conclusion "pretty ridiculous", as a death certificate issued in Laos lists "methanol toxicity" as one of her causes of death.

Trainee lawyer Simone and childhood friend Bethany Clarke were among about 100 guests given free shots thought to be tainted with methanol.

They felt unwell the next day and were taken to hospital, where Simone, from Orpington in south-east London, was put on life support before she died.

Two Australians, two Danish citizens and an American also died after drinking the shots.

Medical documents seen by Newsbeat state methanol was found in Bethany's blood in November 2024.

"For them to say there's not really enough evidence, I think for me and my parents, it's a bit of a slap in the face, really," says Zak.

"If you've got a death certificate with that on it, surely there's enough proof?"

Zak previously said his family had braced themselves for an unsatisfying resolution to the case as authorities were "not very forthcoming with trying to speed things along".

The case will remain open for 15 years, but Bethany says she is "not expecting much" from the Laos legal system in future.

"To my mind it's very clear what's happened," she says.

"I don't know why it should take a rocket scientist to come to the conclusion of what's happened here."

News.title: Owners of viral TikTok blue lagoon warn people to stay away
News.content:
Owners of a "blue lagoon" that went viral on TikTok during the Covid pandemic have warned people not to enter the site, particularly during the current hot weather.

Brombil Reservoir in Margam in Neath Port Talbot attracted thousands of visitors, which caused traffic problems and littering.

To reach the 30m-deep (100ft) reservoir, visitors must walk up a steep 900m (2,953ft) public footpath.

Leisure Estate Investments Ltd, which bought the secluded site at auction for Â£20,000 in 2024, are now charging Â£2 a visit as "a temporary deterrent" and have installed barriers on its dam face.

It is concerned about people swimming, paddleboarding, littering and damaging structures around the site.

Although the reservoir can be accessed via public footpaths, the barriers were installed to stop people from walking on the dam face - but these have since been removed by trespassers.

The owners said the Â£2 levy was introduced in an effort to manage unauthorised visits and help fund clean-up operations, as part of its efforts to discourage public access because of "inherent safety risks".

A spokesperson for the company said: "We have strictly banned [people] from going there and walking on the face of the dam.

"Our long-term vision has always been to build a sustainable public-private framework so the community can safely enjoy this asset.

"However, managing a critical piece of infrastructure presents immense structural, environmental, and financial challenges that cannot be indefinitely sustained by a private entity alone."

News.title: UK borrows less than expected in June but public finances remain a challenge
News.content:
The government borrowed slightly less than expected in June, according to figures published as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham began setting out measures to cut living costs for households.

Borrowing - the difference between spending and income from taxes - was Â£16bn, about Â£7.9bn lower than a year earlier, although analysts said challenges remained over the UK's public finances.

Other data showed the unemployment rate was unchanged, with the Office for National Statistics (ONS) saying the labour market was "relatively steady".

However, while the borrowing figure was less than forecast, the ONS said total debt was high by historical standards and close to the annual value of the UK economy.

Borrowing for June was slightly below the Â£16.3bn that had been predicted by the government's official forecaster, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR).

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said June's figure was "a rare piece of good news" for the new prime minister and his new Chancellor, John Healey.

However, she added: "Overall, there's no escaping the fact that the public finances are fragile and that there is limited scope for extra borrowing."

So far in the current financial year, borrowing has reached a total of Â£57.6bn, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). While this is down Â£3.7bn from the same period last year, it is Â£2.7bn above the OBR's forecast.

James Smith, chief UK economist at ING, told the BBC's Today programme the fact that borrowing was still running ahead of the OBR's projections was "a reminder of the challenges that the new chancellor and the new prime minister face".

He added they would face a "difficult picture" at the autumn Budget, with "lots of tough choices to be made".

Burnham and Healey have both pledged to stick to former chancellor Rachel Reeves' fiscal rules on spending and borrowing, although the new prime minister said on Monday he would use "any flexibility within them" to help with policy changes.

Shortly after Burnham's comments were made public, the yield on 10-year government bonds - effectively the interest rate charged to the UK government for a 10-year loan - rose above 5%.

The yield hit 5.03% late on Monday afternoon. However, when trading began on Tuesday the rate slipped back slightly to 5.01%.

In a statement released on Monday, Healey said "fiscal credibility is the bedrock for economic stability and for national security".

Shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said Labour had "maxed out the nation's credit card and sent borrowing soaring".

"If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control," he said.

The new leadership's first major policy announcement was to cut VAT on household electricity bills from 5% to zero from the beginning of October.

Ministers said it would be funded by savings from the cancellation of the digital ID programme, but Labour's Darren Jones, who was sacked as chief secretary to the prime minister on Monday, accused the government of announcing an unfunded tax cut.

News.title: 11 best cylinder vacuums to combat dirty floors, tried and tested
News.content:
Cylinder vacuums remain a popular choice thanks to their strong suction power, lightweight designs and easy manoeuvrability. While they lack the convenience of cordless vacuum or robot vacuums, they often deliver excellent cleaning performance and are available in options to suit everything from small flats to busy family homes.

It’s no surprise that professional cleaners often turn to cylinder vacuums. Cleaning expert and author Laura Mountford says their appeal lies in their versatility and powerful suction. “Cylinder vacuums are lightweight but with heavy duty power, because they focus on pure suction rather than rotating brushes,” says Laura. “Most models come with lots of tools and attachments that can be used to clean all around your home. They are basically the Swiss Army knife of vacuum cleaners – great for vacuuming different surface types, the stairs, getting into tight spaces, sofas, curtains and rugs.”

With years of experience testing vacuum cleaners, I put a range of cylinder models through their paces to find the ones truly worth buying. From bagged and bagless designs to options for allergy sufferers or one of the best pet vacuums, this guide covers the best cylinder vacuums for every type of household.

Remco Evenepoel rode a brilliant time trial to win stage 16 of the Tour de France on a bittersweet day for his Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe squad, as co-leader Florian Lipowitz crashed out of the race.

Lipowitz, who finished third last year and won the best young rider classification, had been in fifth place going into stage 16.

The German misjudged a corner with 6.4km to go on the course and was sent sprawling across the road, before being helped off the course into an ambulance.

Three-time TT world champion and pre-stage favourite Evenepoel safely negotiated the same corner on his way to victory in 32:19.33.

It made for back-to-back stage wins for the reigning Olympic champion, after he won a first ever Tour de France road stage on Sunday on Plateau de Solaison.

“It’s amazing, it was a very nice TT, a lot of people on the side of the road, my whole family from both sides, my wife is here with her parents and siblings as well,” Evenepoel said. “I read this morning it’s been a while since a Belgian won on our national day [Rudy Matthijs, in the 1985 edition] so I’m proud to be the one. It’s unbelievable to take two victories in a row.

“I’ve just been told my teammate Lipowitz crashed, that’s very unfortunate... how do you call it, a bittersweet pill to swallow with this victory. I wish him all the best and hope he’s not too bad. I will really miss him for the last week.”

Evenepoel finished 28 seconds quicker than the next-fastest finisher, yellow jersey Tadej Pogacar, whose lead over the Belgian - second in the overall standings - was cut to four minutes and 32 seconds.

Pogacar nearly slid out on the same corner which put paid to Lipowitz’s Tour in a nervy moment but managed to stay upright.

Still, the Slovenian appears fully in control of this race, barring accident or injury in the last week, and Evenepoel conceded as much. He said: “Honestly not [thinking about winning the Tour], I’m just focused on my own spot. If Tadej is on his way to win a fifth Tour de France, I think it’s just amazing that I can be a bit close to him, it’s an honour to race with him. For me it’s a big step forward that I can be around him and learn from him.”

Lidl-Trek’s Mattias Skjelmose produced the time trial of his life to come third home in 33:23.64 but Evenepoel was head and shoulders above the rest of the field, a minute and four seconds quicker than the Dane in his 26th victory against the clock.

open image in gallery Evenepoel has now won three time trials at the Tour de France ( Reuters )

After Monday’s second and final rest day a difficult final week of the Tour began with the only individual time trial of this edition.

The 26.1km course, on the shores of Lake Geneva, was most suited to the general classification contenders, with the climbing beginning straight out of the gate in Evian-les-Bains and heading towards the category two Cote de Larringes, a 9.7km ascent averaging at 4.3 per cent. The riders then tackled a tricky, technical descent and flat finish in Thonon-les-Bains.

Visma-Lease a Bike’s Bruno Armirail set the quickest time of the earlier starters, beating the Netcompany-Ineos duo of Josh Tarling and Filippo Ganna, while their teammate Thymen Arensman was unlucky to be late to the start gate.

Without that strange mishap the Dutchman would likely have finished quicker than Armirail; as it was he came home a fraction shy of five seconds off his time.

open image in gallery Pogacar now leads Evenepoel by four and a half minutes ( Reuters )

Red Bull Bora-Hansgrohe’s Matteo Cattaneo displaced Armirail in the hot seat with a time of 34:01.28 and held the virtual lead until the top 10 began to arrive in Thonon-Les-Bains, ultimately finishing sixth.

In the battle for the best young rider’s white jersey, and third place on the podium, French wunderkind Paul Seixas stole five seconds over Isaac del Toro, finishing fourth with his rival fifth on the day. Seixas now sits 20 seconds down on the Mexican in fourth overall.

Britain’s Tom Pidcock finished 12th on the day after a strong ride in a discipline which he does not excel in, two minutes and seven seconds off Evenepoel, and is up to eighth in the standings after Lipowitz’s withdrawal.

News.content:

A United Airlines employee was captured on video appearing to threaten to call U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement on a passenger during a ticket counter dispute last week at San Francisco International Airport.

“Maybe we should call ICE on you,” the unidentified staff member is heard saying in the recording.

The altercation began when 54-year-old East Bay resident Julio Varela arrived at the airport with his family to resolve an issue with one of his daughters’ tickets, which had mistakenly listed her middle name as her last name.

According to Varela, the family had spent hours attempting to fix the error when the employee told them she could not assist and that they would miss their flight.

“I say, ‘well, my wife made the mistake, but we’ve been trying to correct it,’” Varela told CBS News. “So that's what we’re here for, so you can help us. She says, ‘well, I don't care if you fly or not.’ So that’s what got me upset. I said, ‘what’s your name?’ She said, ‘I’m not going to give you my name.’”

open image in gallery An unidentified United Airlines employee was captured on video appearing to threaten to call U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement on a passenger during a dispute at San Francisco International Airport ( Julio Varela via Storyful )

When the staff member refused to identify herself, Varela pulled out his mobile phone to record the interaction, prompting the worker to do the same.

Footage posted online shows the employee holding her phone directly in front of her face in an attempt to block her appearance while seemingly recording back.

From behind the camera, Varela responds to the initial statement: “You're going to call ICE on me?”

“Maybe you need to be,” the employee can be heard saying when Varela tells her to repeat herself, “because you don't act like a citizen. Get away."

The video shows the employee repeatedly telling Varela to “get out my face.” Varela responds by telling her, “you got some guts lady,” and threatens legal action, to which she replies, “okay, you sue.”

As the confrontation continues, Varela shouts, “United Airlines has a racist customer service lady,” and tells her, “you're lazy, and you're rude and you are racist.”

open image in gallery Julio Varela began recording the unidentified worker after she refused to provide her name during the ticket counter interaction ( Julio Varela via Storyful )

Varela, who was traveling with his wife and three daughters, noted that all five family members are U.S. citizens.

“I was so shocked, I was angry,” Varela told CBS News. “It’s intimidating, because my kids didn’t know, you know, if when we get back, are we, am I going to be arrested? Is ICE going to be there?”

He added: “My 14-year-old daughter is crying on the side, and she’s screaming. My daughter’s, like, ‘Why would you say you were going to call ICE?’ That's so rude and disrespectful, you know?”

Despite the statement from the employee, Varela said he refused to drop the matter.

“She assumed that I was just gonna be some idiot that was gonna, you know, just be quiet and shut up,” Varela told the outlet. “So I said, ‘No, call ICE.’”

The ticketing issue was eventually resolved minutes after the exchange, allowing the family to board their scheduled flight.

In a statement emailed to The Independent, United Airlines said it was investigating the incident but offered no further details.

Longtime ESPN broadcaster Karl Ravech is expected to be among the latest layoffs at the network, sources told The Athletic Tuesday.

Ravech, a 31-year ESPN veteran, served as the network’s lead baseball play-by-play announcer, also covered college basketball and anchored SportsCenter. He called the Dodgers-Phillies game Monday before reportedly learning his job was at risk.

When contacted by The Athletic Tuesday morning, Ravech said he had not yet been informed of his status.

The cuts follow ESPN’s decision Monday to part ways with NFL analyst Ryan Clark, with additional layoffs expected to hit behind-the-scenes staff. Most of the reductions are reportedly coming at NFL Network, including Tom Pelissero, one of the network’s top insiders, per The Athletic.

A memo from ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro to employees Tuesday morning, obtained by The Independent, did not identify those impacted by the layoffs but said the cuts followed a review of the company’s teams, resources and structure after integrating acquired NFL assets.

open image in gallery Karl Ravech, pictured holding a microphone, is reportedly among those impacted by ESPN’s latest round of layoffs, sources told The Athletic Tuesday ( Getty )

ESPN acquired NFL Network in late January as part of a deal with the league that also gave the NFL a 10 percent stake in ESPN.

“Over the past several months, we've made significant progress integrating the NFL assets that we acquired into ESPN. Throughout this process, we have taken the time to carefully evaluate our collective teams, resources and organizational structure to best position us for the future. As a result, we had to make some difficult decisions about job impacts that we will be communicating today,” Pitaro wrote.

“While most of the job impacts are tied to the acquisition, we will also notify colleagues in other parts of the company today that their positions have been impacted. We are committed to treating employees with compassion and respect and to providing support as they navigate this transition,” the memo continued.

“Even in moments like these, the strength of ESPN comes from our people, our teamwork and our shared mission to serve sports fans.”

open image in gallery NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero is reportedly among those impacted by ESPN’s latest round of layoffs ( Getty )

ESPN declined to provide further comment.

The network reportedly planned to announce Clark’s departure Tuesday but moved up the decision after receiving media inquiries Monday, The Athletic reported.

Clark was removed from Monday’s episode of NFL Live and informed of his dismissal directly by an executive before the news became public, sources claimed.

Clark, a former NFL safety who joined ESPN more than a decade ago, was earning more than $2 million annually, according to The Athletic. He was a prominent voice on shows including Monday Night Countdown, First Take, Get Up and NFL Live.

open image in gallery Ryan Clark’s ESPN exit was reportedly influenced by concerns over his on-air comments and conduct, including a dispute with colleague Peter Schrager ( Getty )

ESPN executives reportedly became concerned over Clark’s conduct, with tensions escalating after a dispute with colleague Peter Schrager during an episode of Get Up last season.

The disagreement followed Clark’s criticism of Schrager’s defense of Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb, with Clark telling Schrager, That's the non-player in you."

Clark addressed his layoff in an Instagram post Tuesday, sharing clips of his workout allegedly before he received the news.

“Proof of Life…Before the madness of yesterday, I woke up, got in my Tundra, drove to Planet Fitness, and got to work,” Clark wrote.

“The rest of the day was eventful, but the journey continues. My peace is with God, and my humility comes from within. I’ll continue to build myself so the world can never strip me of what’s real. Get moving today y’all!”

Clark also showed support for his fellow shuttered colleagues on X. He wrote Tuesday: “Sending prayers and love to all those laid off today by ESPN. So many of you have poured your life into that company, & I know how you’re feeling right now. My hope is as this door closes, another opens for you all. God bless!”

US strikes on Iran are unlikely to impact Tehran or cause it to soften its negotiating demands, according to new American intelligence assessments.

Iran attacked another tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, forcing crew to abandon the ship as both sides traded strikes for a tenth consecutive night.

But Iran’s government is unlikely to be affected by the attacks, current and former US officials told the Washington Post.

Instead, US intelligence officials have briefed the Trump administration that Tehran and Washington are now stuck in limbo, with both sides refusing to deescalate.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has said that it will not give up and vowed to fight to the end, saying on Monday: “[Trump] should know that, by God’s grace, even if this war lasts for several years, until the very last day, our missiles and drones will rain down on American criminals.”

But Trump has likewise threatened that Iran will pay the price “many times over” for the deaths of three US soldiers – including 19-year-old Isabella Gonzalez – in Iranian attacks on a US air base in Jordan on Saturday.

open image in gallery Military equipment targeted at an unknown location, during what U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) says are strikes on Iran, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released on July 20, 2026. ( Reuters )

He wrote on Truth Social: “Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over! This directive has been passed on to Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Daniel Caine, and every Leader in the Military. President DONALD J TRUMP.”

To complicate matters further, reports emerged on Tuesday that Iran had proposed a 10-day ceasefire in a bid to iron out differences regarding the Strait of Hormuz, sources familiar with the talks told The Jerusalem Post.

Iran has accused the US of violating a ceasefire after commercial vessels appeared to bypass Iranian-approved routes and travelled through a southern corridor by the coast of Oman. But America says that Tehran’s attacks break their promise to allow vessels to pass safely through the waterway.

Mediators from Qatar, Egypt, Oman and Pakistan are involved in the discussions, with a potential “middle corridor” being floated as a solution to the deadlock.

open image in gallery Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 21 ( Reuters )

Other reports suggest that negotiations continue to take place behind the scenes, with Iranian spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei telling a news conference on Monday that intermediaries in Qatar have passed messages from Washington to Tehran.

“We have received messages, without going into details, but the main point is that the diplomatic apparatus has been active in recent days and ideas have been conveyed to us by certain mediators,” he said.

Tehran amped up its attacks on Monday and Tuesday with strikes on an Amazon data centre in Bahrain and water desalination and power plants in Kuwait.

Israeli finance minister Bezalel Smotrich said on Tuesday that Israel has “no interest” in joining the ongoing confrontation between the US and Iran, in comments made at a conference organised by the Gush Katif Heritage Center. Israeli troops withdrew from parts of southern Lebanon with the Lebanese army deployed in the areas instead.

President Donald Trump has claimed that states run by Democrats are destined to become tomorrow’s “ghettos,” with “no people, no money, no hope,” if they continue to tax wealthy corporations and individuals.

“Rich people and Companies are pouring out of Dumocrat run Blue States at levels never seen before!” the president wrote on Truth Social Tuesday morning.

“If this trend continues, these States will become the ‘Ghettos’ of the Future – No people, no money, no hope. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN!”

Trump’s post came in response to a Just the News story claiming that a “high-tax exodus” is underway in the Midwest, pointing to True Value Hardware recently announcing that it is moving its corporate headquarters away from Chicago to Fort Wayne, Indiana, echoing the Chicago Bears relocation to Hammond in the same state.

The right-wing outlet argues that Illinois risks becoming as “business-repellent” as California and New York unless it changes its ways.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has attacked blue states like Illinois over their tax policies and warned they could become ‘ghettos’ if the wealthy leave ( Getty )

“True Value joins the ranks of other longtime Illinois companies like Boeing, Tyson Foods, Morton Salt and Caterpillar [in leaving], the latter of which pointedly cautioned that the state’s inability to balance the budget and lower taxes would drive out businesses,” it states.

The president issued a similar warning in a post back in April.

“Job-producing people and companies are being forced to flee at levels never seen before,” Trump wrote at the time. “Remember, once people and companies leave, they are never coming back.”

Just the News also cites the “U-Haul Growth Index” on company relocations, saying its latest data “shows an overwhelming number of entrepreneurs and workers ditching Illinois and California for the greener pastures of Texas and Florida.”

The likes of North Carolina, Tennessee and Arizona are also serving as sanctuaries from “high taxes and regulatory strangulation,” the index suggests.

open image in gallery Trump has had regular run-ins with Democratic governors like Gavin Newsom and JB Pritzker ( AFP/Getty )

The report further notes that Charles Schwab, Hewlett-Packard, Chevron, Public Storage and Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX have all left California in recent years for more favorable tax climates.

Trump has had regular run-ins with the likes of California Gov. Gavin Newsom and his Illinois counterpart JB Pritzker, as well as other Democratic governors, over everything from natural disaster responses and urban crime to the presence of ICE agents taking part in his federal crackdown on undocumented migrants.

Democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani’s surprise triumph in last year’s New York City mayoral election and the subsequent success of leftist candidates in other votes has meanwhile given Republicans fresh cause for concern ahead of this November’s midterms.

That has led to renewed cautions against the dangers of left-wing policymaking from Trump and other influential MAGA voices, as well as an increase in personal attacks on popular progressives like New York Rep. Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez.

However, despite the cost of living remaining high and providing a major source of worry to voters, Pew Research found last year that a majority of the American public nevertheless still believes that asking corporations and higher-income households to contribute more is the right way to deliver improved public services and a fairer society.

Harry Styles is sparking concern after he abruptly canceled a show due to health reasons.

The British singer, 32, is in the middle of the South American leg of his Together, Together Tour. After already performing two concerts in São Paolo on Friday and Saturday, he was scheduled to perform again Tuesday evening.

However, a note sent to ticket holders July 21 announced that the event at Morumbi Stadium was “cancelled due to tour illness.”

“We deeply regret to inform you that the Harry Styles show scheduled for Tuesday, July 21, 2026, at MorumBIS has been canceled due to a health issue on the tour,” Live Nation Brazil said on X in a statement that was translated from Portuguese.

Tickets for the show will be fully refunded, according to concert officials, and people with tickets to Tuesday’s show will have a chance to buy an exclusively discounted batch of tickets for Friday’s show, which is still scheduled to take place.

Harry Styles cancelled his third show in São Paolo, Brazil ( PA Wire )

“We have worked with the event venue to release as many tickets as possible for the Friday show, but please keep in mind that availability is extremely limited,” Live Nation Brazil told fans. Buyers will receive more information in an email from Ticketmaster.

Representatives for Styles did not comment further on the health issue affecting the tour. The former One Direction member did not immediately address the cancellation.

Styles kicked off his world tour in Amsterdam earlier this year after the release of his fourth album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.

Last month, he broke a record by playing 12 nights at London’s Wembley Stadium, which The Independent’s Roisin O’Connor reviewed as a “euphoric, vital show.”

During one of the historic shows, he worried fans by collapsing on stage after appearing to choke while spitting water into the air. He lay on the ground and coughed, which led concertgoers to become worried that he had fainted from the heatwave in the U.K. at the time.

However, Styles then seemed to be fine as he stood up and continued the show, assuring fans: “It’s all good, I’m good.”

After Friday’s show in Brazil, the superstar is scheduled to head to Mexico City for six shows from July 31 to August 10. Later in August, he will begin a 30-night residency at Madison Square Garden in New York City, which wraps up October 31. The tour is set to end in Australia in December.

The police watchdog has launched an investigation after a teenage boy died after falling off a motorbike which was about to be followed by officers.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said Logan Stead, 16, was riding a motorbike along Eastbourne Terrace in Pontefract, West Yorkshire, on 13 July.

Police said he came off the motorbike and died at the scene despite medical assistance from police and paramedics.

A 13-year-old boy who was also on the motorbike was uninjured.

The IOPC said the bike had been spotted by West Yorkshire Police officers shortly before the crash at 5pm.

They “had concerns about the age of the boys” and had turned around to catch up to the motorbike once it had travelled past them in the opposite direction.

The IOPC said there was no pursuit of the vehicle by officers before the crash.

open image in gallery The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said Logan Stead, 16, was riding a motorbike along Eastbourne Terrace in Pontefract, West Yorkshire, on 13 July ( Getty Images )

A spokesperson said: “Our investigation will be looking at the circumstances in the lead up to the collision.

“Our initial inquiries have established that officers had concerns about the age of the boys on the motorbike, although there was no pursuit of the vehicle by officers prior to the collision.

“As soon as WYP notified us of the incident, IOPC investigators went to the collision scene to begin gathering information.

“We declared an independent investigation on the same evening.”

IOPC director of engagement Emily Barry said: “Firstly, my thoughts and condolences are with the family of Logan and all those who have been affected by this tragic incident.

“We have contacted Logan’s family to explain our role and we will continue to update them as our inquiries progress.

“There is a mandatory requirement for forces to refer to us incidents like this, which result in death or serious injury, and our investigation will thoroughly examine the circumstances of the police involvement, including whether appropriate policies and procedures were followed.

“Whilst our investigation is in the early stages, investigators are in the process of obtaining accounts from the officers involved and working with the force to secure all available footage related to the incident.”

Police previously said the 13-year-old boy was arrested after the crash on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

On Tuesday, the force confirmed no further action will be taken against him.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

Sports.title: Argentina hold open-top bus parade after LOSING World Cup final but Lionel Messi snubs it after flying home separately
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI was missing as Argentina held an open-top bus parade – despite being BEATEN in the World Cup final.

The sore losers returned to Buenos Aires after failing to win the tournament back-to-back in New Jersey.



Messi, 39, broke down in tears on the MetLife Stadium pitch after the South Americans were beaten by a single goal.

Meanwhile his team-mates got into scraps after the final whistle – with Nahuel Molina taking a swing at Rodri and Leandro Paredes lashing out at several Spain stars.





The shameful scenes came after Lionel Scaloni’s side failed to muster a single shot on target, instead focusing on gamesmanship rather than playing football.

But their pitiful showing did not stop them receiving a hero’s welcome as they touched back down in Argentina‘s capital.

Thousands of fans took to the streets to applaud the team as they made their way by bus back to their training complex.

Messi was a notable absentee after flying home separately from his team-mates – to his hometown of Rosario.



The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner faces a short turnaround with Inter Miami‘s season resuming this wee.

David Beckham’s side face Chicago Fire in the MLS on Thursday although the Argentina captain is sure to miss that as he spends time with his family.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Like all World Cup stars he is entitled to three weeks off after his exploits at the tournament.

Other Argentina stars who did not fly back with the team include Rodrigo De Paul, Cristian Romero, Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez.



Boss Scaloni and Nicolas Otamendi were the first off the flight before being followed by the likes of Nicolas Tagliafico and Alexis Mac Allister.

Lisandro Martinez was also spotted walking off the plane with his suitcase and a bag.

The defender went off injury the first half of the final after appearing to hurt his leg.



He has opted to take the plane to his homeland rather than fly from New York to Manchester, where he lives.

Other players that were spotted included Leandro Paredes and Valentin Barco.

Barco became infamous in England after Argentina dumped the Three Lions in the semi-final.



He was filmed wildly celebrating in front of the English players and was slapped in the back of the head by Jude Bellingham.

The former Brighton flop could be seen with a fairly vacant expression on his face as he waited to board the team bus.

There was plenty of pageantry for the World Cup final losers with a military band playing them in off the plane.

There was also a long red carpet rolled out for them all the way to the bus.

Sports.title: Everton join transfer race for Norway World Cup star, 35, with Man City and Leeds also considering move
Sports.content:
EVERTON have joined the race for Norway keeper Orjan Nyland.

The free agent, 35, was a smash hit for the World Cup quarter-finalists in North America.



SunSport revealed fellow Prem sides Manchester City and Leeds are tracking Nyland, who is out of contract after leaving Sevilla at the end of last season.

Veteran Nyland was outstanding in Norway‘s run to the last-eight where they lost to England 2-1 in extra-time.



He started five out of the six games in the Norwegians’ impressive World Cup campaign, keeping three clean sheets.

Nyland did not feature in the France clash that saw Stale Solbakken make ten changes.



The keeper saved 70 per cent of the shots he faced during the tournament and has now won more than 60 caps for Norway.

The ex-Aston Villa and Norwich man produced a standout display in the knockout win over five-time world champions Brazil.

England No1 Jordan Pickford is the first-choice for Everton boss David Moyes.

But back-up Mark Travers has been linked with a move away from the Hill Dickinson Stadium and that could free up space in the Toffees squad.

Sports.title: Top Premier League referee, 47, RETIRES from football after 831 matches just days after World Cup exit
Sports.content:
FAIRY TAYL ENDS Top Premier League referee, 47, RETIRES from football after 831 matches just days after World Cup exit

TOP Premier League referee Anthony Taylor has retired just days after the World Cup ended.

Taylor, 47, was one of England’s most accomplished officials and one of two at the tournament alongside Michael Oliver.



Taylor’s final match was the last 16 clash between eventual winners Spain and Portugal in Dallas.

Spain clinched a 1-0 victory in Dallas after Mikel Merino scored a last-minute winner to set up a quarter-final against Belgium.



The referee ends his career after 16 Premier League seasons and 831 games – 668 of which were in England.

Taylor took charge of 432 Prem games and every major domestic cup final, including the 2017 and 2020 FA Cup finals.



He also spent 14 years as a Fifa official, reffing games at the 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and Euro 2020 and 2024.

Taylor was shortlisted to referee the 2022 World Cup final but was removed from consideration due to Argentina’s history with England over the Falklands.

Reflecting on his career, Taylor said: “Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.



“I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants Gary and Adam, my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years.

“Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Howard Webb, Chief Refereeing Officer at Pro Ref, added: “Anthony has been a fantastic servant to the game over many years, both domestically and on the international stage.

“He has been repeatedly trusted to officiate in the biggest games including Portugal against Spain in this summer’s World Cup which ultimately capped off an outstanding career.

“He’s consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it’s not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many.

“The professionalism he’s shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.



“We thank him for his immense contribution to the game and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career.”

Taylor has been at the centre of some memorable Premier League moments – including the infamous confrontation between Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel after the match between Chelsea and Tottenham in 2022.

And in Europe, he received plenty of media attention after Jose Mourinho waited for him in the Puskas Arena VIP car park following Roma’s 2023 Europa League final defeat to Sevilla.

Mourinho called him a “disgrace” and heavily criticised his refereeing performance to reporters.



At the time, the then-Roma boss fumed: “This is a European final and with this kind of refereeing, it is hard to accept.

“If we talk about refereeing situations, it’s not two or three: it is many, quite apart from the big decisions.

“Those of us who have been in football a long time realise immediately what is going on.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mourinho was eventually charged by Uefa for using “insulting/abusive language against a match official” numerous times.

Before becoming one of Europe’s top referees, Taylor served as an assistant at the 2014 Uefa Super Cup, the 2015 Europa League final and the finals of both the 2016 Champions League and European Championships.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson pays heartbreaking tribute to Kevin Keegan and reveals secret meeting after ‘love it if we beat them’
Sports.content:
SIR ALEX FERGUSON has admitted he had the “utmost respect” for old rival Kevin Keegan, who passed away on Monday.

Former Liverpool star, Newcastle boss and two-time Ballon d’Or winner Keegan died aged 75 after battling cancer.



He and Manchester United icon Fergie went toe-to-toe in the Premier League‘s early years, when Keegan was in charge of Toon.

But Ferguson reflected positively on their rivalry and credits the job his rival did on Tyneside.



The Scotsman told Track Radio: “I had the utmost respect for him.

“We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but I have to say the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic.

“He re-energised that club and he brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism that great supporters can give. That’s the job he did.

“I must say, the challenges we had with Newcastle at that time at United were huge.

“Kevin carried the love of the game on his sleeve, there’s no question about that, and that carried right onto the fans, to the players.

“That period at Newcastle was of emotion, it was excitement. They brought great players to the club too and they added to it, and it gave Newcastle – I think – their best ever team.”



The managers’ rivalry peaked in 1996, when Newcastle blew a 12-point lead to hand United the league title.

Weeks before the end of the season, in late April, a fired-up Keegan famously admitted he would “love it” if his Toon side pipped the Red Devils.

He also said Ferguson had “gone down in his estimation” by hinting that teams were trying harder against United than they were against Newcastle.



But they let bygones be bygones in a pub near Wentworth Golf Club, where they spent a night around the piano shortly after the campaign ended.

Sir Alex continued: “The great thing about him, he held no grudges. That was a fantastic quality he had and we had a great night.

“All aside whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten. I really respected him for that.”

But despite the timing, Garnacho is NOT being offered as part of a straight swap.

Instead, Villa see him as the man to fill the void left by Rogers once the England international completes his move to Stamford Bridge.



Villa are hoping to land Garnacho on an initial season-long loan rather than a permanent deal.

The proposal is said to be for an initial loan with a buy clause included with Emery approving the Argentine winger as one of his priority targets.

Discussions are also continuing with the player’s representatives.

Sports.title: Rayan Cherki singles out Didier Deschamps after backlash to England incident and 'snub'
Sports.content:
Rayan Cherki singles out Didier Deschamps after backlash to England incident and 'snub'

Rayan Cherki was one of the France players taken off at half time in the 6-4 third-place play-off loss to England at the 2026 World Cup

View 2 Images Rayan Cherki was substituted at half time of the third-place play-off match vs England (Image: Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Manchester City attacker Rayan Cherki has sent a special message to outgoing France boss Didier Deschamps after what appeared to be a couple of frosty incidents between the pair. Deschamps has ended his 14-year reign in charge of the French team following this summer’s World Cup.

‌



Les Blues were one of the favourites to win the tournament, but a 2-0 loss against eventual winners Spain in the semi-final left them fighting for third place. That’s where they came up against England, who suffered semi-final heartbreak against Argentina.

‌



In what was arguably the game of the tournament, the Three Lions came out as 6-4 winners to claim third place. Thomas Tuchel’s men found themselves 4-0 up at half time, but France almost completed a second-half comeback before a Bukayo Saka penalty and a Jude Bellingham goal put England out of reach.

‌



Both teams have now returned home, with Cherki taking to social media to give his response to the tournament and single out Deschamps. “Naturally, I am saddened by the outcome of a tournament where our mission was to make you all proud and happy,” he wrote on Instagram.

Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next READ MORE :

FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job READ MORE :

“Thank you for the support that stayed with us every day and served as our driving force. I am infinitely grateful to the coach for everything he has achieved for French football and for giving me my first caps for Les Bleus.

“His track record speaks for itself. Thank you to the coaching staff for their dedication, and to all the federation personnel who supported us and ensured we had the best possible conditions, all while looking after our loved ones.

‌



“Thank you to the whole squad for these unforgettable moments of brotherhood. Despite our differences, mistakes, or setbacks, we are one family; it is up to us to remain united so that French football comes back stronger!”

View 2 Images Rayan Cherki has sent a message to outgoing France manager Didier Deschamps (Image: Maddie Meyer - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

The message comes after Cherki appeared to ignore Deschamps, not once, but twice, during the tournament. The first incident came after the team’s round of 32 win over Sweden, where the forward appeared to initially snub the manager before giving him a brief greeting.

‌



The second came during the first half of the game against England. During the first hydration break, with England 2-0 up, an agitated Deschamps appears to try to give Cherki instructions, only for him to wave his hand towards the manager and walk away.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

With England scoring a further two goals before half time, Cherki was one of four France players to be replaced at the break. Speaking about the incident after the match, Deschamps said: “I’m not going to settle scores today.

‌



“The players know perfectly well. I’m not going to point fingers. However, I always tell them, and as Kylian (Mbappe) said, they needed time to process it but it was my mistake, I should have made different choices from the start of the match, you can say that, and perhaps things would have gone better.

“Everyone is judged on their performance. Obviously, some players could have done better. I wish them all the best.”

Cherki’s mention of the French Football Federation in his message is also noticeable, given reports in France around growing tensions between the federation and the team. Issues reportedly include World Cup bonuses, travel and match tickets for families for the World Cup just gone.

Sports.title: Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next
Sports.content:
Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next

Anthony Taylor has retired from refereeing with his final match being at the recent FIFA World Cup

View 2 Images Premier League referee Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement after officiating at the 2026 World Cup (Image: Rico Brouwer/Soccrates/Getty Images)

Premier League referee Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement. The Englishman has hung up his whistle after officiating Spain's 1-0 win over Portugal in the last 16 of this summer's World Cup.

‌



The 47-year-old has called time on his career after over two decades and 831 matches. Taylor officiated in the Premier League for 16 seasons, taking charge of no fewer than 432 top-flight games.

‌



The experienced ref also officiated the 2024 Champions League final between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. But Taylor will no longer referee in the professional game - bowing out after the World Cup.

‌



Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job READ MORE :

The now former top-flight official announced the news in a post on his LinkedIn account on Tuesday. He said: “The final whistle has blown – moving on to the next chapter.

“After 16 unforgettable seasons officiating at the highest level of English and international football, I have decided that the time has come to retire from elite refereeing. Looking back, I do so with immense pride and gratitude. It has been the greatest privilege to officiate in the Premier League, across FIFA and UEFA competitions, and on some of football’s biggest occasions. Every match, every challenge and every experience has shaped not only my career but also the person I have become.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“Elite refereeing is about far more than the ninety minutes on the pitch. It demands commitment, resilience, preparation and sacrifice, but it has given me memories, friendships and experiences that I will cherish for the rest of my life. No referee achieves success alone. I have been incredibly fortunate to work alongside so many outstanding colleagues throughout my career. To each of you, thank you. It has been an honour to share this journey together.

“A special thank you must go to Gary Beswick and Adam Nunn . What “Team Tayls” has achieved together makes me immensely proud, and I could not have wished for better colleagues or better friends. Your professionalism, loyalty and unwavering support have meant more than words can express.

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor was an experienced referee (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“It hasn’t always been easy – the pressure is intense and the scutiny is constant – but it has been an immense privilege to be at the heart of the game I love. Football is built on passion, and whilst decisions will always be debated, it has been an honour to serve the game with integrity and professionalism.

“Most importantly, thank you to my family and friends. Your love, patience and unwavering support have been my foundation throughout this journey. The sacrifices you have made alongside me have never gone unnoticed, and I simply would not have achieved any of this without you.

‌



“To everyone who has been part of this remarkable journey, thank you. It has been the privilege of a lifetime. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.”

Hinting at future plans in the public eye, Taylor confirmed he will now be represented by barristers Trinity Chambers and added: "To follow what comes next, follow me on Instagram… @anthonytaylor.official."

Taylor is one of several officials to have retired from English football this summer. Referee Darren Bond and assistant referees Natalie Aspinall and Marc Perry also hung up their whistles after the 2025/26 season concluded.

Meanwhile, referee Jeremy Simpson and assistant referee Mark Russell called it a day in the Championship, while referee Cristiana Hattersley retired from WSL duty.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino told World Cup decision could have cost him his job

Gianni Infantino has come under fire following a controversial World Cup with the FIFA president told one outcome changing could have resulted in him being dismissed

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been sent a damning World Cup message (Image: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

La Liga president Javier Tebas has admitted Gianni Infantino could have lost his job at FIFA if the USA beat Belgium in the World Cup last-16. The build up to that clash was engulfed in controversy after USA star Folarin Balogun had his red card from the previous knockout round against Bosnia and Herzegovina suspended for 12 months.

‌



U.S. President Donald Trump called Infantino regarding the incident, with FIFA's disciplinary committee later reversing the decision to make him available to manager Mauricio Pochettino again. Despite his inclusion, the co-host nation were comfortably beaten 4-1 and Tebas has stated that result likely saved Infantino his job as president.

‌



During an interview with Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport, Tebas said: "The suspension of the American player's ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky that Belgium eliminated the USA, because otherwise a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job."

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

He could have potentially lost his job regardless with an official complaint made to The International Olympic Committee that his dealings with Trump breached political neutrality. However, he will not face any sanctions from the IOC, of which he has been a member of for the last six years.

Infantino's role as FIFA president is still under increasing pressure though, with Tebas the latest high-profile figure to speak out against the 56-year-old.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up," he said. "There's no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. He shouldn't stay, but the current state of affairs means he won't leave."

Though the next World Cup is not until 2030, it has been in the headlines with Infantino and FIFA'S vice president Alejandro Dominguez open to a 64-team tournament. Tebas, who was in the United States to watch his country lift the trophy this year, has explained why he thinks that is not a good idea.

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas has spoken out against Gianni Infantino

‌



He said: "Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense. The football industry isn't just the World Cup. It's the national competitions that sustain this sport. They are destroying the football industry, which generates tens of thousands of jobs, for an event that lasts 40 days and involves a minority of players.

"Are the best players there? Clearly, but they are also in our leagues. We need fewer international matches and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don't realise they are making irresponsible decisions."

One positive of the proposed format would be that 16 groups of four teams would not see any third-placed teams get through but the round of 32 would remain. A record 104 matches were played across the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer. That would jump up to 128 if FIFA got their wish of expanding the World Cup.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez hints he could quit Argentina duty after World Cup final loss

Argentina suffered a painful defeat in Sunday's World Cup final to Spain and first-choice keeper Emi Martinez has admitted he is now considering his future with the national team

View 2 Images Emi Martinez has indicated he is contemplating international retirement (Image: Juan Mabromata/AFP)

Emi Martinez has revealed that is considering his international future following Argentina's loss in the World Cup final, saying he must decide whether it is now "time to step aside".

‌



The Aston Villa goalkeeper was a colossus in Argentina's triumph in Qatar four years ago during an epic penalty shootout victory over France and again on Sunday, where he kept Spain at bay until extra-time. Ferran Torres eventually beat Martinez to deny Argentina the chance to make history with successive World Cup titles.

‌



Martinez is the latest Argentina star to send a message to supporters on social media after the heartbreaking defeat.

‌



And the 33-year-old, who has won 67 caps for his country, has hinted that Sunday's game in New Jersey could end up being his final international appearance.

FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced READ MORE :

“I dreamt we'd win it again, I dreamt of bringing it back to Argentina and making history once more,” Martinez wrote in a post on Instagram.

“The truth is, the pain is hard to explain. There are many things to reflect on and how to move forward, and if it's time to step aside.

‌



“I'm so sorry, I truly tried my best to help my country and my team-mates.”

Argentina and Martinez were left up against it when the Chelsea midfielder, Enzo Fernandez, was shown a red card in the final minutes of regulation time. They eventually succumbed to Spanish pressure in extra-time but had been under the pump all game, failing to register a single effort on goal until the 116th minute.

View 2 Images Martinez helped Argentina win the World Cup in 2022 with crucial penalty saves against France (Image: Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



The aftermath of the game was marred by ugly scenes as Argentine frustration boiled over, with Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes both lashing out at opponents.

Their behaviour was condemned by Wayne Rooney, who argued that their conduct in previous games hardly made their poor reaction a surprise. The BBC pundit said: “Does it surprise you? It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this with Argentina before.

“It's just not the reaction you want. We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round. That's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's really poor from them.”

Sports.title: Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, set to make first-team debut THIS week as ban lifted
Sports.content:
Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, set to make first-team debut THIS week as ban lifted

Manchester United star JJ Gabriel has been on the verge of a first-team breakthrough for some time and it appears that the teenager could finally be in line to make his senior debut

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has been unable to make a first-team appearance yet (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel is set to make his long-awaited first-team debut in the Red Devils’ clash with Rosenborg. Michael Carrick’s side take on the Norwegian side in their second pre-season friendly of the summer on Friday.

‌



A similar squad is expected to be named to the one that lost 1-0 to Wrexham, albeit with a few differences. Gabriel, 15, took part in United’s latest training session on Monday at Carrington and is under consideration to be included in the squad to fly to Norway.

‌



Taking to Instagram after the defeat to Wrexham, the teenager wrote: “The longer you wait for something the more you appreciate it when you get it because anything worth having is worth waiting for.”

‌



Gabriel has been part of United’s youth system since 2022 and has been working his way up through the ranks. In 2025, he became the youngest-ever player to represent the club’s under-18 side, while he has regularly been handed opportunities to train with the first team.

He also enjoyed a brilliant season last term, having scored 26 goals in 29 appearances for United’s youth team last season as they reached the FA Youth Cup final. Gabriel has yet to make his first-team debut due to a rule about player ages, albeit he can sign a professional deal when he turns 17 in October next year.

Paul Scholes accuses Thomas Tuchel of trying to get sacked after comments on England stars READ MORE :

Speaking about Gabriel last season, Carrick said: "He's not allowed [to make his debut], he's too young. He's doing really well, JJ.

‌



“We've got some really good young players in the academy and we try and get the younger players up [with the first-team] as much as we can. We're always trying to give that exposure to the players to come and train and feel it."

The United boss added: "JJ is a big talent, it's pretty obvious to know that and he's had a really good season for the U18s.

View 2 Images Gabriel trained with Man United's first team ahead of the clash with Rosenborg (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and working with him in development as we do with all the different younger players and picking the right moment to step up.

"What he's done when he's trained, he's done well as you'd expect and it's good to have the younger players come up with us."

Sports.title: FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced
Sports.content:
FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced

Plans to potentially expand the World Cup to 64 teams in the future have been heavily criticised with the chief of La Liga now taking aim at Gianni Infantino after this summer's tournament

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under fire during the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The president of La Liga, Javier Tebas, has accused FIFA and Gianni Infantino of trying to 'destroy football' with their plans to increase the number of teams competing at future World Cups to 64.

‌



Spain won the final of this summer's tournament on Sunday, beating Argentina 1-0 in a forgettable final. 48 teams, rather than the usual 32, competed across matches held in the United States, Canada and Mexico as part of expanded format for the first time, but Infantino has already confirmed that adding a further 16 teams will be discussed.

‌



However, Tebas has torn into the plans, claiming they make 'no sense' and that moving ahead with them would be irresponsible.

‌



“Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense,” Tebas told the Italian outlet, La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final READ MORE :

“The football industry is not just the World Cup, which is the most important event. But not everything can revolve around the World Cup. It is national competitions that support this sport.

“They are destroying the football industry, the one that generates tens of thousands of jobs for an event that lasts 40 days and to which the minority of players go.

‌



“We need fewer national teams and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don’t realise, they decide irresponsibly.”

Tebas went on to question Infantino's position following criticism of political interference at the World Cup from the United States President, Donald Trump.

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas has torn into Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Infantino has been in power for 10 years and is expected to be elected for a fourth term next year. But Tebas wants to see change, even if he believes it is unlikely to happen.

“In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up,” he added. “But he has the support of the system, of the federations, there is not much more to add, right?

“There is no opposition candidate, no one wants to present themselves to lose. This is the system, and it is a system that is sick at the source.

‌



“In these days here in America I have heard many people against Infantino, who do not agree with what he does. They say it, but then they do nothing.

“I don’t know if silence or complicity is worse, because those who are silent are perfectly aware of the damage that football is suffering.”

Sports.title: Premier League referee Taylor retires
Sports.content:
Long-serving Premier League referee Anthony Taylor is standing down after 16 years in England's top flight at the conclusion of the World Cup.

The 47-year-old hangs up his whistle following 831 games in the English, European and international game, with his final match the World Cup last-16 clash between Portugal and tournament winners Spain.

Domestically, Taylor refereed in every major domestic English cup final, officiating the 2017 and 2020 FA Cup finals and the 215 League Cup final, as well as 432 Premier League matches.

He also served for 14 years on the FIFA international list, and was selected to represent England at both the 2022 and 2026 World Cups.

Anthony Taylor's career in numbers 668 professional matches in England

16 seasons in the Premier League

432 top-flight matches

Officiated every major domestic cup final

14 years on FIFA International List

163 international matches

Two World Cups (2022 and 2026), two European Championships (2020 and 2024) and two Club World Cups (2022 and 2025)

Gave 14 yellow cards in a Premier League match - the most ever

In announcing his retirement, Taylor suggested his decision had been fuelled by the "intense" pressure and "constant" scrutiny he faced in the role.

Speaking in a statement through refereeing body Pro Ref, formerly PGMOL, Taylor said: "Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career."

He was publicly targeted by Roma fans at Budapest Airport in 2023 after being criticised by their then-manager Jose Mourinho following the club's Europa League final defeat by Sevilla.

Last year, he revealed his family no longer came to matches he was officiating while criticising the "expectation of perfection" placed on referees and admitted he had repeatedly considered quitting the game.

Commenting on the incident in Hungary, he told BBC Sport: "That's for sure the worst situation I've dealt with in terms of abuse.

"Not only because I was travelling with family members at the time, but it also highlights the impact of people's behaviour on others.

"It makes you reflect back on whether you made a mistake travelling with your family in the first place."

Taylor refereed more Premier League games than anyone else in 2025/26, with his last game West Ham's final-day 3-0 win over Leeds, which was not enough to save the Hammers from relegation to the Championship.

The Premier League has no set limit on retirement age for referees, with a number of officials continuing into their 50s including Neil Swarbrick and Graham Scott, who refereed in the top flight until they were 52 and 56 respectively.
