Sports.title: I used to be team Lionel Messi but after World Cup final I’m team Cristiano Ronaldo
Sports.content:
I used to be team Lionel Messi but after World Cup final I’m team Cristiano Ronaldo

Andy Goldstein has admitted that he is no longer in the Lionel Messi camp after his and Argentina's antics in the World Cup final.

The South American giants lost to Spain at the MetLife stadium in a game that was marred by bad sportmanship and dirty tactics.



5 Messi was in tears after collecting the second World Cup runners-up medal of his career Credit: Getty

And as a result, Goldstein is now back in the Cristiano Ronaldo camp.

During the final, Messi even tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off.

Under new rules introduced by FIFA for the World Cup, a player covering their mouth while confronting an opposition player would receive a red card.

In the aftermath of Enzo Fernandez's second yellow, Cucurella spoke to Messi and half covered his mouth.

Immediately, the response from the Argentine great was to try and get an official to look at it and send Cucurella off.



Speaking on Drive with Ben Foster, Goldstein said: "I've changed my mind now on Messi and Ronaldo. I was team Messi for a long time...

"But the bit where Cucurella sort of covered his mouth but didn't, and Messi went to the headteacher and was grassing, 'oh, he should get detention'. He didn't need to do that."



Foster added: "I am disappointed. I love Messi. He is everything I want from a footballer, but that was horrible.

"I think he's desperate, and he's reaching for everything that he possibly can, but you don't need to do that.



"Don't sink to those levels."

5 Mess attempted to get Cucurella sent off for doing nothing Credit: AFP

5 Ronaldo had a pretty terrible World Cup as Portugal crashed out in the round of 16 to eventual champions Spain Credit: Getty

On Messi and Argentina's performance, he said: "I can imagine it is quite hard work trying to pull a rabbit out of the hat every single game.

"They found a way to just keep getting by. They were winning in extra time and coming from two goals down and did it round after round.



"I think they thought that they were just going to have to keep it going in exactly the same way.

"But as World Cup finals go, it was one of the worst you will ever see.

"I think Argentina outdid themselves on horribleness. What we saw at full time was as bad as it can get.

"Paredes fully lost his head and was trying to punch people in the face, and it was a horrible end to what was a bad game of football."



5 There were very unsavoury scenes at full time with FIFA opening an investigation

On the rest of Argentina's antics, Foster said: "It was about as one-sided a final as you are likely to see.

"It was just Argentina sitting back and Spain were just waiting. If they had scored early doors, it would have been a completely different game.

"But Argentina have got to do what they've got to do because they can't compete with Spain."



Argentina disgrace

Argentina became the first side in World Cup history to play a final and not have a shot after 90 minutes.

They ended the match with a total of two shots and none on target.

There was a huge brawl at the end of the game as Leandro Paredes was sent off but has since had his red card rescinded.

5 It was absolute carnage at the end as Spain's Gavi took the brunt of the hatred from the Argentinians Credit: Getty

They refused to watch the trophy lift and incensed Adrian Durham and Stuart Pearce.



Speaking at the end of the final, Durham said: "They've been absolutely shocking.

"They've been a total disgrace here today. The fans, we think have been brilliant. But even during the trophy lift, also when Rodri went up to get the best player in the tournament trophy, the fans were singing Messi's name and they were singing Argentina as well.

"They simply cannot accept that Argentina were beaten in the World Cup final."

Durham continued and went through the whole tournament, adding: "Argentina are a total embarrassment to the game, an embarrassment to the World Cup.



"In fact, they have been an embarrassment all along really, apart from that 20 minutes against England.

"Drawn in the easiest group in World Cup history, made hard work in the knockouts against Cape Verde, needed Egypt to grab defeat from the jaws of victory to get through to the quarters where Switzerland shot themselves in the foot with a needless red card.

"England in the semis were on top, handed it on a plate to Argentina who came here to the final and totally embarrassed themselves.

"The lack of red for Messi in the group stage was predictably shocking.



"No punishment for a Falklands banner held up by the players after beating England.

"A terrible refereeing decision even gave Argentina a chance at the end of extra time here in the final.

"Argentina are cheats, they're impossible to like. The beautiful game of football is the winner at this World Cup final."

Sports.title: Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires days after World Cup clash
Sports.content:
Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from refereeing after the 2026 World Cup.

The 47-year-old was one of the most experienced officials in the Premier League and featured 433 times in the English top flight.



2 Taylor has called time on his refereeing career Credit: Getty

Taylor hit 831 professional matches across club and world football but now decided to hang up his whistle.

His last match was the World Cup last 16 clash between Portugal and Spain on July 6, which the latter won 1-0.

"Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant," he said.



"The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.

"I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants Gary [Beswick] and Adam [Nunn], my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years.



"Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded."

Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, said: "Anthony has been a fantastic servant to the game over many years, both domestically and on the international stage.



"He has been repeatedly trusted to officiate in the biggest games including Portugal against Spain in this summer's World Cup which ultimately capped off an outstanding career.

"He's consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it’s not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many.

"The professionalism he’s shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.

2 Taylor was one of the most trusted officials in the Premier League Credit: Getty



"We thank him for his immense contribution to the game and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career."

Top job

Taylor was trusted with some of the biggest matches in club football such as two FA Cup finals and a Europa League final.

He officiated five matches across the 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and took charge of six Euro 2020 and 2024 fixtures.

His Premier League debut came in February 2010 when he oversaw a 1-0 home win for Fulham against Portsmouth.



Last season, Taylor refereed 31 different fixtures in the competition, including the opener that saw Liverpool beat Bournemouth 4-2.

He dished out 121 yellow cards during the campaign, the second-most of any referee.

Sports.title: Aston Villa submit surprise bid for Chelsea’s Alejandro Garnacho as potential Morgan Rogers replacement
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho has been the subject of a loan bid by Aston Villa, talkSPORT understands.

It is believed that the deal includes a conditional obligation to buy clause, as the Villans now look to agree personal terms with the winger.

3 Garnacho could be on his way out of Chelsea after just one season in west London Credit: Getty

As it stands, it remains unclear if Chelsea would sanction a temporary departure for the eight-cap Argentina international.

talkSPORT recently revealed how Chelsea had slapped a £42.5m asking price on the 22-year-old.

The Midlands are keen to bring in a replacement for Morgan Rogers, who is set to join the Blues in a deal worth £117million.

His switch to Stamford Bridge will only see Garnacho fall further down the pecking order, having already been placed on the transfer list - one year after joining from Manchester United in a £40m move.

Garnacho had been linked with Roma earlier in the window, but they failed with a loan offer to bring him to Italy.

That's Al folks?

They appear to have now switched their attention to West Ham's Crysencio Summerville, who had been on Villa's radar, with Al Hilal also in the running to sign the Netherlands international.

And in turn, Villa have formalised their interest in Garnacho, where they are able to offer him Champions League football.

talkSPORT told you on Tuesday how both Garnacho and Nicolas Jackson had been offered to Villa in the wake of their deal to sign Rogers.

It is also understood that as well as Garnacho, Unai Emery's men hold firm interest in PSG starlet Ibrahim Mbaye.

In what was a disappointing 2025/26 season for Garnacho, he scored just once from 24 Premier League outings.

3 Garnacho chipped in with one goal and four assists from 24 Premier League games in the 2025/26 season

Named just 14 times in a top-flight starting XI, the Red Devils academy graduate looks poised for a new adventure.

What has been said about Alejandro Garnacho?

Speaking on Garnacho's future earlier in July, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso confirmed that the forward is attracting interest.

And he refused to rule out the club standing in his way of a potential summer exit.

He said: "We have spoken with the sporting directors and there is interest in him from other clubs, let's see how it develops.

"Hopefully it finishes in the best possible way for all parties."

Meanwhile, Kevin Nolan has wondered why Villa would want to welcome Garnacho into their squad during his appearance in the talkSPORT studio on Tuesday.

3 Garnacho was left out of Argentina's World Cup squad following a poor campaign Credit: Getty

Questioning his professionalism, the ex-Newcastle midfielder said: "I don't know the kid personally, I don't know him at all.

"I'm just looking at him when I see him and what he's done at Manchester United and then going to Chelsea.

"He looks like a problem child, he looks like a problem if he's not playing, he'll throw his toys out of the pram if it's not going too well for him.

"I think if you've got him on board, and you've got your arm around him and everything else and if everything suits him, I think he's a real big and good player.

"But is he big enough for Unai Emery to sort of go, 'I'll take him because I'll be able to get the best out of him?'"

Sports.title: Liverpool midfielder set to join Arsenal youth stars in Slovakia and could face Yaya Toure
Sports.content:
Liverpool midfielder set to join Arsenal youth stars in Slovakia and could face Yaya Toure

Liverpool academy midfielder Tommy Pilling is reportedly closing in on joining the English football revolution in Slovakia.

The 21-year-old, who was in and around the first-team picture last season, was left out of the Reds' pre-season tour of the United States.

5 Tommy Pilling is set to join Slovakian club MFK Zemplin Michalovce Credit: Getty

Pilling, who trained under new Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola earlier this summer, has been on the Anfield books for 16 years.

However, he is expected to join MFK Zemplin Michalovce on a long-term deal in the coming days, according to the Liverpool Echo.

Who is Tommy Pilling?

Pilling progressed through the Reds academy since he was five years old, and looked on the cusp of a first-team breakthrough last season.

He played for the senior team in one of the two friendly victories against Athletic Bilbao at Anfield in August 2025 under Slot.

Pilling told the Liverpool website: "Even though it wasn't a competitive game, just the feeling of being at Anfield, being around the fans, warming up, sitting on the bench behind the coaches, listening, getting an insight into what the first-team players listen to before the game, how people are moving about before the game, what they're doing.

"To actually come on, I had a good 25 minutes too; it was just a moment to express myself, to show what I can do.

"I was nervous before the game, but warming up and stuff, it just felt natural. When the gaffer said, 'You're coming on', I was just focused and happy."

The boyhood Liverpool fan, who was born in St Helens, followed in the footsteps of his great-grandfather Jack Pilling, who played 118 times for the club between 1942-43 and 1945-46.

The Reds' No.70 was then part of Slot's matchday squad for the Carabao Cup ties with Southampton and Crystal Palace last autumn.

5 Pilling played for Liverpool's first-team in pre-season last summer but never made a competitive appearance Credit: Getty

5 The 21-year-old (right) was left out of the squad for their pre-season tour Credit: Getty

Liverpool squad for pre-season tour of USA *Further senior players to join later in tour after World Cup commitments Goalkeepers: Giorgi Mamardashvili, Freddie Woodman, Vítezslav Jaros, Harvey Davies, Bailey Hall Defenders: Joe Gomez, Jeremy Jacquet, Milos Kerkez, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Kostas Tsimikas, Jeremie Frimpong, Luke Chambers, Calvin Ramsay, Calum Scanlon, Ifeanyi Ndukwe Midfielders: Wataru Endo, Dominik Szoboszlai, Curtis Jones, Josh Abe, Trey Nyoni, Stefan Bajcetic, Kieran Morrison, Forwards: Federico Chiesa, Harvey Elliott, Hugo Ekitike, Lewis Koumas, Rio Ngumoha, Will Wright, Hall, Josh Sonni-Lambie,

Unfortunately for Pilling, he was unable to make his competitive bow for Liverpool despite training with the first-team stars several times.

Having entered the final year of his deal, the local lad is now closing in on his first career transfer in a move to the Slovak top-flight.

Who are MFK Zemplin Michalovce?

Anton Soltis' men, who finished fifth in the Slovak First Football League, have built up an English core in the past 18 months.

Zemplin’s squad already boasts two players who started at Arsenal: the first of which is midfielder Ben Cottrell.

The 24-year-old made his senior Gunners debut under Mikel Arteta in a 4-2 win over Dundalk in the 2020 Europa League group stage.

5 Slovakia's top-flight is the home of several English academy talents Credit: Getty

5 Kido Taylor-Hart trained with Arsenal's first-team before heading to Slovakia Credit: Getty

Cottrell was joined in Slovakia by fellow Hale End academy product Kido Taylor-Hart, who Arsenal released in the summer of 2024.

Zemplin also has further British links in Kai Brosnan, who was previously at Hemel Hempstead Town in the National League South.

Pilling could now join the trio in an early test away at Slovan Bratislava on August 29, who are managed by Yaya Toure.

The Manchester City legend was announced as the club's new head coach last month in what represents his first senior management job.

Sports.title: New Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa tipped to be sacked this season: ‘Could easily go wrong’
Sports.content:
New Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa tipped to be sacked this season: ‘Could easily go wrong’

Alvaro Arbeloa could fail to last a year in charge of Fulham - he arrives at Craven Cottage with huge pressure.

That's the view of ex-Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor, who believes the Spaniard has big shoes to fill having replaced Marco Silva.

2 Arbeloa won 18 of his 28 games at Real Madrid during his interim spell in the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty

Arbeloa was appointed by the Cottagers earlier this month on a three-year deal.

It's an immediate return to the dugout for the 43-year-old, who was replaced by Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid in June.

And it's also a move back to England for the 2010 World Cup winner, having enjoyed two separate stints playing in the Premier League.

A seven-year stretch at the Bernabeu was sandwiched between spells at Liverpool and West Ham, with the former right-back retiring after his ill-fated stay at the London Stadium.

But he is hoping for better days in the English capital this time around.

Managerial merry-go-round

Arbeloa is one of eight new managers brought in by Premier League clubs ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

That is the most amount of changes made in a summer in Premier League history.

Enzo Maresca has taken over Manchester City, Liverpool have brought in Andoni Iraola, Chelsea moved for Xabi Alonso with Olivier Glasner switching to Nottingham Forest.

Elsewhere, Bournemouth have appointed Marco Rose, Crystal Palace now have Pierre Sage in charge with Gary O'Neil joining Ipswich.

But it is the future of Arbeloa that Agbonlahor is worrying about, as he commented on their depleted squad.

2 Arbeloa will be looking to guide Fulham to a top half finish for the first time since 2023 Credit: Getty

Fulham have already seen Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez depart as free agents, while defender Issa Diop is set to sign for Ipswich in an £8.5million deal.

Speaking on the talkSPORT Breakfast show, co-host Jeff Stelling commented on teams that have a new manager at the helm.

Interjecting, Agbonlahor then stated: "Arbeloa, there's pressure on him."

To which Stelling replied by saying: "There's big pressure on Arbeloa, that is a punt, isn't it?"

Agbonlahor continued: "That could easily go wrong we'll see won't we this season.

"We talk about Pep [Guardiola], what did he get out of then Man City players, can Maresca do it?

"What did Marco Silva get out of those players at Fulham?

"Diop's leaving, Wilson's gone, more players might leave Fulham.

"Don't be surprised if Arbeloa doesn't last a season."

Fulham's recent Premier League history

Since winning the Championship in the 2021/22 term, Fulham haven't finished below 13th in each of their last four seasons in the top-flight.

Silva guided the club to tenth spot in the 2022/23 campaign, with Fulham ending in 13th the next season, followed by two consecutive 11th-placed finishes.

Despite finishing outside the top ten in May, the Cottagers were just one point off a Conference League spot in eighth - and two behind a Europa League place in seventh.

Sports.title: Uncapped teenager tipped to earn England call-up and be big player for Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Uncapped teenager tipped to earn England call-up and be big player for Thomas Tuchel

Fulham starlet Josh King has been backed to force his way into Thomas Tuchel's England plans.

Following the Three Lions' heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit against Argentina, the conversation has already shifted onto who could star for the national team at future major tournaments.

5 Josh King became a regular fixture in Fulham's starting XI in the 2025/26 campaign Credit: Getty

England now have a two-year wait until their next shot at glory at Euro 2028, which will be hosted on home soil in the UK and Ireland.

Beyond this, there are of course four more years until Tuchel's side can avenge this summer's World Cup heartache, as Spain, Morocco and Portugal host the 2030 edition.

And the Three Lions could have a much-changed starting XI by the time either tournament rolls around, with a number of England's crop set to be well into their thirties by then.

Captain Harry Kane turns 33 this month, and will be nearly 37 in 2030, while key players John Stones and Jordan Pickford will both be 36.

Meanwhile, there is also potential for young players on the periphery of the England squad to stake their claim for a senior call-up, as they look to become key players at future major tournaments.

King of the options

talkSPORT pundit and Aston Villa legend Agbonlahor focused on the latter on Tuesday's Breakfast Show, and he believes Fulham midfielder King is among the top prospects here.

The 19-year-old enjoyed a breakthrough season last term, forcing his way into Marco Silva's starting XI to make 15 Premier League starts.

An England Under-21 international, King's impressive displays were rewarded in the summer, as he was then selected as one of five extra players travelling with the England squad to their pre-World Cup training camp.

Outlining King's qualities, Agbonlahor said: “Before the World Cup there were a few players that were part of the squad that didn't quite make it, but they were training with the squad.

“And one of the players that stands out for me - who I really, really enjoyed watching last season - was Josh King.

5 King is already known to England boss Tuchel after joining his team's training camp in Florida ahead of the World Cup Credit: Getty

“He's 19 years of age, made 32 appearances last season in the Premier League, but he only got one goal and two assists.

“Whenever I watched him play, and every time he got into that number 10 position, he always finds space - like top players do.

"The amount of times he received that ball in that position and created his own space, but maybe the end product, or it's a pass or it's a finish, wasn't at the level.

“But that's what you expect of a 19-year-old. It's a big season for him and I just loved watching him."

Agbonlahor then insisted that Tuchel will no doubt be keeping tabs on the youngster going forward, who he believes could add to England's existing quality in attacking areas.

He added: "He's one that I'm sure Thomas Tuchel will have his eye on - very good player.”

“He kept Emile Smith-Rowe - who’s a talented player - on the bench most of the season, and forced himself into Marco Silva's plans.”

5 King has been capped six times by England at Under-21 level, scoring once Credit: Getty

He will now have a new manager to impress in Alvaro Arbeloa, who replaced Silva this summer.

'What we need'

It wasn't just King who Agbonlahor tipped to break into the England squad in the near future.

He also named Liverpool starlet Rio Ngumoha and Arsenal teenage duo Ethan Nwaneri and Max Dowman as those who should be targeting call-ups.

Alongside King, Ngumoha and Nwaneri was also selected among the Three Lions training players at their pre-World Cup camp, with the former dazzling on his international debut in a friendly win over New Zealand.

On Ngumoha, Agbonlahor began: “Put him in, 100 per cent, and I feel like someone like Noni Madueke who didn't perform [at the World Cup], if you look at Nwaneri, look at Dowman [instead].

“I mean Nwaneri is 19 years of age, went on loan to Marseille - maybe it didn't work out as well as he thought it would be.

“It's a massive season for 16-year-old Max Dowman. These players are going to be so hungry to play. Go out there and play their football and break into Thomas Tuchel's ideas.

5 Aged just 17, Rio Ngumoha impressed off the bench in England's pre-World Cup friendly against New Zealand, which was his senior debut Credit: Getty

5 Max Dowman has followed in Ethan Nwaneri's footsteps by becoming a first-team regular at Arsenal whilst still a teenager Credit: Getty

“Rio Ngumoha? I think he will get a lot more game time under Andoni Iraola [at Liverpool].

"I love the way he plays. Direct, doesn't care, will get the ball and go at you again. Relentless, that's what we need."

England are next in action against World Cup winners Spain on September 26 in a Nations League clash.

During the extended international break across September and October, Tuchel's side will also face Czech Republic twice and Croatia.

Sports.title: Ipswich have £10m bid for Daizen Maeda accepted by Celtic and Nicolas Jackson is keen on Aston Villa as Man United, Arsenal and Chelsea target Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Ipswich's £10m Daizen bid does trick

Ipswich Town have had a £10m bid for Celtic’s Daizen Maeda accepted. A deal worth £8m up front and £2m in add-ons has been agreed in principle.

Earlier this month the forward confirmed his wish to move to England .

‘Since I went to Celtic, I became interested in the Premier League,’ he told Japanese YouTube show Pivot. ‘I started watching a lot of Premier League games. I have a strong desire to play in the Premier League.'

The Tractor Boys have also completed their deal for Leicester winger Abdul Fatawu today, with manager Gary O'Neil saying of the 22-year-old: 'Abdul is a young player who has already gained good experience in the game and we’re excited to have him with us.

'He has strong physical and technical attributes, is comfortable on the ball and can test the opposition in one-on-one situations, so will provide us with good options within the squad.

'Having represented his country at the World Cup this summer, I know he is now looking forward to getting to work ahead of the Premier League season.'

Daizen Maeda played a big role for Japan at the World Cup this summer

Villa step up Garnacho talks

Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho.

After enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m sale, Villa have proposed a loan for the Argentine with obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Chelsea have been holding out for a permanent sale around £40m as Manchester United are also due a sell in percentage.

Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho

Roma have also offered a loan with options for Garnacho who was of interest to Villa before he left Manchester United last summer.

Villa remain keen to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and are monitoring developments with Crysencio Summerville at West Ham.

The Hammers have a £39m offer plus add ons on the table from Roma and have added interest from Al Hilal.

PFA free agent squad in action tonight

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Around 48 players have now joined the PFA pre-season camp where they train and play a series of friendlies to showcase their availability to clubs over the summer.

Former Manchester United and Port Vale keeper Ben Amos and ex-Ipswich Town striker Connor Wickham are among a growing band of players looking to earn contracts elsewhere.

Another friendly is planned at Tranmere Rovers on Friday.

The games can be viewed on the PFA's live YouTube stream.

Spurs agree to sell Lankshear to Middlesbrough

Tottenham have agreed to sell Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £14million potentially rising to £20m with add-ons.

There is also a 20 per cent sell on clause and Spurs have matching rights on any bids from other clubs in the future.

Striker Lankshear, 21, who was on loan at Oxford United last season, is expected for a medical later today.

Nicolas Jackson interested in Aston Villa move

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa to work with his former head coach Unai Emery again.

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa

Jackson's name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who is set to move to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117million and sign a six-year deal with the option of an extra year.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson under Emery, who had the striker at Villarreal. Chelsea have been taking their time to decide on the 25-year-old Senegal international's future.

With Jackson, Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro as Xabi Alonso's striker options currently, there is an acceptance inside of Chelsea that they need to reduce their numbers, especially while facing a season out of Europe.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and so not for sale. Delap is keen to have another season to prove himself after a disappointing campaign following his move from Ipswich, while Emegha has only just arrived this summer from their sister side Strasbourg. Guiu is expected to leave either permanently or on loan.

There remains a market for Jackson, who spent the last season on loan at Bayern Munich. Chelsea are believed to value him at £65m.

That is down on the £80m they were understood to be seeking last summer before sanctioning his temporary switch to Bayern. That came at a time when the relationship between Jackson and then-manager Enzo Maresca had broken down.

Chelsea's plan for Jackson was to have him return in pre-season so that Xabi Alonso could take a closer look at the scorer. Alonso said at his unveiling last week that Jackson was due to join them on their tour of Australia and Asia after his post-World Cup break.

However, sources close to Jackson have told Daily Mail Sport that they are seriously considering Villa as an option after his name was discussed during talks about Rogers. Alejandro Garnacho has also been linked with Villa, but the Argentinian is said to be prioritising a move to Italy.

KIERAN GILL

West Ham mulling over Roma's Summerville bid

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

As reported yesterday, Roma's latest bid of £39million plus add ons is a marginal increase and restructure on their second bid which was rejected.

Aston Villa have also been monitoring developments on the 24-year-old.

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign Crysencio Summerville

West Ham have enquired about Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor.

Ipswich seal deal for new goalkeeper

Ipswich have completed the signing of goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen from Volendam.

The fee is £4.25m with an initial £3.4m followed by £850,000 in add-ons.

The 22-year-old, who is seen as one for the future, has signed until 2031.

Ipswich have had a bid rejected for another goalkeeper, Kjell Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise.

As reported on Window Watch yesterday, Ipswich are close to sealing a £20m deal for Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with a further £3m in add-ons.

Ipswich are overhauling their goalkeeping department and discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop (right)

They are discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop and are negotiating with Celtic for versatile forward Daizen Maeda and free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita who is leaving Sporting Lisbon and had been close to joining Leeds United.

QPR snap up Lamptey

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal.

The 25-year-old has signed on a free transfer after leaving Serie A side Fiorentina.

Lamptey said: 'I like to get up and down, a lot of energy, a lot of fun. Hopefully I'll keep the fans on the edge of their seats.

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal

'I'm tough tackling, I love one-v-ones, defensive and attacking, I just love playing the game.'

Lamptey's Fiorentina contract was terminated by mutual consent in May after the full-back ruptured his cruciate just three weeks after joining the Italian side from Brighton.

Fiorentina paid £6m for the Ghanaian.

Sheffield United weigh up Matondo move

Sheffield United are continuing to evaluate winger Rabbi Matondo who has impressed during their training camp in Valencia.

The Wales international, who is free to leave SK Brann, is due to play in a behind closed doors friendly against Huddersfield Town today.

Matondo figured in the Blades friendly against Levante last week and Chris Wilder is expected to make a decision this week with the likes of Derby County and Middlesbrough also showing interest.

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield Wednesday close in on TENTH summer signing

Aston Villa forward Tommi O'Reilly is poised to become Sheffield Wednesday's 10th summer signing.

The 22-year-old, who impressed on loan at Crewe in League Two last season, is due to sign on loan again at Wednesday.

The Owls' young goalkeeper Logan Stretch, 19, has been loaned out to National League North side Buxton, who are managed by former Wednesday youth coach Jordan Broadbent.

Man City teenager joins Northampton

Manchester City striker Matty Warhurst has joined Northampton Town.

The prolific 19-year-old was keen to leave for first team football and had interest from a host of clubs in League One and League Two including Stockport County, Cambridge United, Leyton Orient and Swindon Town.

Warhurst, who turns 20 in September, has scored 61 goals in 97 games for various City sides in the last few seasons, including 36 goals in 41 games for the under-18s before adding 13 goals in 18 Premier League 2 appearances and eight goals in 11 FA Youth Cup games.

Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract.

Scott has two years remaining on his current deal and was offered fresh terms by the Cherries in March this year.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United all hold an interest in the 22-year-old, but Bournemouth's stance is that he is not for sale this summer - regardless of his contract situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands Bournemouth have not put a price or valuation on the Under-21 European Championship winner as they do not consider him for sale.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract at the club

Just last week, new Cherries boss Marco Rose told the media he was confident that in-demand Scott and Junior Kroupi would remain on the South Coast for their Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth's policy this summer is to keep hold of their best players for Europe - including Scott, Kroupi and winger Rayan - but it remains to be seen if substantial offers would test their resolve.

Scott played 39 times for Bournemouth last season and was key to securing European football for the first time in the club's history.

Thomas Tuchel awarded Scott his first international call-up last November, although he did not earn a cap.

The midfielder also travelled to the United States with the Three Lions before the World Cup to take part in their tournament preparation camp.

Even if Bournemouth could be persuaded to do business over Scott, it's understood that United would have to sell players to afford the £80m it would be likely to cost to prise him away from the Vitality Stadium.

The club want to sell top-earner Marcus Rashford following his loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, and would listen to offers for Joshua Zirkzee. Manuel Ugarte would also have been available, but the Uruguay midfielder sustained a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will spend much of next season recuperating at Carrington.

As it stands, United will struggle to sign Scott and Roma midfielder Manu Kone appears to be a more realistic option after United held talks with the Frenchman's camp.

BOBBY MANZI AND CHRIS WHEELER
