Sports.title: Premier League referee Anthony Taylor announces retirement aged 47 - with Englishman bowing out after officiating at this summer's World Cup
Sports.content:
Premier League referee Anthony Taylor announces retirement aged 47 - with Englishman bowing out after officiating at this summer's World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from refereeing aged 47 ending his career at the World Cup.

The Englishman's last match as a referee was eventual World Cup champions Spain's last-16 1-0 win over Portugal on July 6.

Taylor's career as an official saw him involved in 831 matches which spanned over two decades.

During that time he was a Premier League referee for 16 seasons, being the man in the middle on 432 occasions.

Aside from the Premier League, he officiated the 2024 Champions League final as Real Madrid beat Borussia Dortmund, the FA Cup final in 2017 and 2020, the 2015 League Cup final and the 2018 Championship play-off final.

As well as this summer's World Cup, he officiated the 2022 World Cup in Qatar as well as the 2020 and 2024 European Championships.

Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from refereeing, bowing out at the World Cup

Explaining why he is retiring, Taylor cited the demands of the job.

'Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant,' Taylor said in a statement.

'The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.

'I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants Gary and Adam, my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years. Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded.'

Howard Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, English football's professional refereeing body, said of Taylor: 'He's consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it's not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many.

'The professionalism he's shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.'

Sports.title: Aston Villa propose loan move with obligation to buy for Alejandro Garnacho - with Chelsea wanting £40m permanent deal
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho.

After enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m sale, Villa have proposed a loan for the Argentine with obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Chelsea have been holding out for a permanent sale around £40m as Manchester United are also due a sell-on percentage.

Roma have also offered a loan with options for Garnacho who was of interest to Villa before he left Manchester United last summer.

Villa remain keen to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and are monitoring developments with Crysencio Summerville at West Ham.

The Hammers have a £39m offer plus add-ons on the table from Roma and have added interest from Al Hilal.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister's father firmly denies Real Madrid talks amid speculation Liverpool star had 'offered himself' to Spanish giants
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister's father has firmly shut down speculation of a potential move for his son to Real Madrid, according to reports.

The Liverpool star has enjoyed a strong World Cup campaign with Argentina, reaching the final before defeat to winners Spain on Sunday afternoon.

But as Mac Allister prepares to return to his club after a well-deserved break, his father Carlos has been quick to stamp out suggestions that he is set for a new season away from Anfield.

Spanish media first hinted at a potential move this week, with Defensa Central claiming that Mac Allister and his representatives had offered him to Real Madrid.

But speaking to online outlet 365scores, the elder Mac Allister left no room for misinterpretation.

'We have not spoken with any official at Real Madrid,' his statement read. 'What is being circulated about us holding talks with Real Madrid is not true.

Alexis Mac Allister is not thought to be agitating for a move to Real Madrid, according to his father Carlos

'Mac Allister is still under contract for two seasons at Liverpool, and currently he will get some rest for a few days, and then return to play in the Premier League, and that is the current situation.'

Mac Allister has featured for the Merseyside club since his move from Brighton in 2023, but Real Madrid has had a sharp-elbowed summer in the market so far.

As well as prising former coach Jose Mourinho away from Benfica ahead of the World Cup, the Spanish giants inked a £60million deal to bring Marc Cucurella to the capital from Chelsea.

Mac Allister's team-mate Ibrahima Konate has also made the move to LaLiga with Los Blancos, departing Liverpool as a free agent.

Real Madrid have similarly secured former Manchester City midfielder Bernardo Silva, while Denzel Dumfries was tempted away from Inter Milan after the club activated his £17.1m release clause.

Carlos previously acted as his son's spokesperson in April 2025, when Real Madrid previously appeared to be circling the Premier League winner.

Mac Allister had given a vague response to a question posed by AS suggesting that he could see himself playing in Spain 'one day' due to the country's similarity to his own.

Then, Carlos squashed the potential for rumours to blossom saying: 'Alexis is very happy where he is.'

Mac Allister was among the 16 national team players who returned to Buenos Aires after losing their World Cup final, with missing team-mates opting to return to their clubs or begin their holidays from the USA or Europe.

Sports.title: A feast fit for a (Vi)king! Erling Haaland shows off huge birthday meal on holiday with girlfriend Isabel - as he gears up for Premier League return after Norway's World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
A feast fit for a (Vi)king! Erling Haaland shows off huge birthday meal on holiday with girlfriend Isabel - as he gears up for Premier League return after Norway's World Cup campaign

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Erling Haaland celebrated turning 26 in style on Tuesday as he showed off his huge birthday feast while holidaying after the World Cup.

The Manchester City star played a key role for Norway at this summer's tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, steering his country to their best ever World Cup finish before suffering defeat against England in the quarter-finals.

Haaland, aware that the new Premier League season is only a few weeks away, has opted to take a much-needed holiday after the World Cup, enjoying a relaxing getaway on the waves with his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen in Sardinia.

Reposting a picture shared to Isabel's Instagram on Tuesday, the birthday boy showed off the incredible feast he was about to tuck into as he celebrated turning 26.

Showing views of the ocean's waves in the background, the photo displayed a table boasting huge portions of barbecued meat on the bone, a mountain of sausages, pancakes, eggs, bagels, fruit and a tower of various cakes and pastries.

He then later posted an image of him relaxing on the waves while wearing a Viking helmet, posting on X: '26 years. Nice.'

Erling Haaland showed off his birthday feast on Tuesday while holidaying after the World Cup

Haaland then posted a picture of himself wearing a Viking helmet on his summer holiday

The Manchester City star pictured with his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen on Instagram

Haaland is renowned for having one of the most extreme diets in the Premier League, averaging a remarkable 6,000 calories per day to keep up his monstrous physique.

Cow hearts and livers can often be found on the City star's menu, as referenced in Haaland: The Big Decision - the documentary made around his £51m move to the Etihad in 2022.

'You other people don't eat this (heart and liver), but I am concerned with taking care of my body,' Haaland explained in the documentary. 'I think eating quality food that is as local as possible is the most important.

'Or the local cow eating grass right over there? I eat the heart and the liver.'

Regular items on his shopping list - as shown on his access-all-areas YouTube channel - also include gigantic barbecue steaks, raw honey, and milk, lots of milk. Haaland loves the stuff, especially raw milk, and he once described it as his 'magic potion'.

The Norwegian loves pairing his milk with a breakfast of eggs on sourdough and a cup of coffee with maple syrup at his six-bedroom mansion in Alderley Edge, Cheshire, which he shares with Isabel.

During the video, Haaland also showcased his love for fish. He ate a lunch of sea bass, asparagus, and egg fried rice before joining his team-mates on the pitch at the Etihad campus.

The upcoming 2026-27 season will mark Haaland's first season at the Etihad without Pep Guardiola, who decided to call time on his glittering Manchester City career at the end of last campaign.

Haaland's remarkable physique is maintained with a crazy 6,000-calorie-per-day diet

There's also plenty of milk in Haaland's diet, which he has called his 'magic potion' for success

Guardiola's former assistant Enzo Maresca, who parted ways with Chelsea in January, has taken over at the Etihad and will undoubtedly lean on Haaland's prowess in front of goal as he bids to win City a ninth Premier League title.

Since arriving in Manchester, Haaland has scored a staggering 162 goals in 198 games across all competitions, winning two Premier League titles, a Champions League, two FA Cups and a League Cup during that time.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal mocks Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with hilarious sign at Madrid's celebration parade after star's shameful violence at the World Cup final - as red carded villain claims they represented nation 'in best possible way'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain superstar Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with a punchy sign at the champions' World Cup celebrations in Madrid.

Two million supporters crowded the streets of the capital to welcome their heroes after they defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final.

But the immediate aftermath of the match was marred by the barbarous antics of Paredes, who attacked two Spain players.

He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before shoving over substitute Gavi, causing a large-scale melee in the middle of the pitch - and it's that second act to which Yamal's sign referred.

Yamal held up a sign which read: 'Velada del ano VII: Paredes vs Gavi'. The Velada del Ano is a celebrity boxing event in Spain, not unlike Misfits.

Argentina were widely condemned for their behaviour after losing the final - but they have maintained a siege mentality following the game.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was sent off in normal time, claimed that they had represented their nation in the 'best way possible'.

Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina's Leandro Paredes at celebrations in Madrid, holding up a sign referring to his altercation with Gavi after the World Cup final

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes was lambasted after the whistle for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground

He said: 'As time passes, you realize there is something much bigger than a result.

'For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

'It teaches that competing isn’t just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I’ll always cherish.

'I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

'Wearing my country’s shirt is the greatest honour of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I’m called upon to defend it.'

Defending the shirt with violence is another matter, though, and the BBC's piundits weren't impressed. Micah Richards said of Argentina's behaviour: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart had a similar opinion, saying: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Captain Rodri lifted the World Cup as Spain touched down in Madrid yesterday

Yamal carried his luggage, including an oversized Hermes Birkin bag, off the plane

Wayne Rooney also said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been against England in the semis.

Chelsea star Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, the first of which came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they were trigger-happy on the fouls with 24 - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Alan Shearer said: 'There's a way to lose. Too many times we've seen that reaction from them. They were trying to win free-kicks and their reaction after full time was terrible. The best team won. It's a result for football because of the way Spain have played.'

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of yesterday

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

The airplane arrived hours later as the city of Madrid readied a welcome home fit for heroes

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigious Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do.

'But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

Ffter lifting the trophy in front of a full house of their adoring fans, La Roja opted not to ring in their victory with a night of partying in the city that never sleeps.

Instead, Golden Ball winner Rodri got the party started in transit, leading a round of singing on the team bus as the jubilant players sped back to their hotel for a team meal, before moving on to Newark Airport.

Back at the hotel, noted wine connoisseur Marcos Llorente enjoyed a bottle of Chateau Rayas Chateauneuf-du-Pape Reserve 2014 - which costs £1,009 to uncork - in his room with team-mates Ferran Torres and Marc Pubil.

The stars then boarded the Airbus A350-941 waiting for them - clad in their team's livery - and took off shortly after 2am local time.

Spain's players landed at Madrid's Barajas Airport at 2.30pm local time, and stepped out onto the tarmac with the World Cup trophy held aloft.

Sports.title: Argentina star praised for defying his team-mates and watching Spain's World Cup trophy lift - amid heavy criticism of national team's disgraceful post-match conduct
Sports.content:
Argentina star praised for defying his team-mates and watching Spain's World Cup trophy lift - amid heavy criticism of national team's disgraceful post-match conduct

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina star Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez has won plaudits for appearing to be the only player to acknowledge Spain's World Cup trophy lift after suffering a 1-0 defeat on Sunday.

The Albiceleste were unable to retain the trophy after their barnstorming victory in 2022 and instead reacted poorly, with many of the players refusing to acknowledge Spain's win.

The team was captured turning their backs on captain Rodri accepting the trophy in a gesture widely deemed bitter by international spectators.

But for Lopez, who plays for Brazilian side Palmeiras, the decision to watch the ceremony unfold and Spain lift the trophy after gaining their second star has seen him singled out as an example to his team-mates.

'To face your defeat head-on, that is what it truly means to be an honourable person,' one commenter said on social media.

Another added: 'Showed character. Congratulations!'

Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez was the only Argentina player to watch Spain lift the World Cup

The Palmeiras star was singled out as an example to his team-mates, many of whom turned their backs on Spain

A third suggested: 'Flaco Lopez all alone showing more class than the entire squad. The others had already vanished before the anthem even started playing.'

'The only one who respects football and his country by not letting them be made a laughingstock,' one social media user said.

Argentina were outplayed in New York after forcing extra time against Luis de la Fuente's side, with Ferran Torres finally grabbing the only goal of the game in the second-half of extra time.

When the final whistle blew, tensions bubbled over, with Leandro Paredes one of Argentina stars embroiled in physical violence, lashing out at Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

FIFA have since opened an investigation into Argentina's full-time confrontation, with the roles of other players and officials also set to be scrutinised.

Nahuel Molina hit Rodri in the torso as he was running by, resulting in the midfielder squaring up to his rival.

That saw players from both teams pile into the melee, before Paredes threw punches.

Elsewhere, 53-year-old assistant coach Roberto Ayala was also caught landing a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo at full time.

In the aftermath of the ugly brawl, DAZN Spain claimed Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi complained to Rodri about La Roja's pre-match comments alluding to officiating concerns ahead of the final.

As well as turning their backs on their opponents some Argentineans descended into violence after the final whistle

The South Americans had benefitted from a series of questionable decisions heading into the showpiece event, with the Manchester City midfielder raising concerns before the final.

'You and (Spain team-mate Aymeric) Laporte. Both of you,' Otamendi said to Rodri.

'You spent the time crying and complaining about the referees, my friend. But you shouldn't have spoken before the match, you know that? Didn't you see what he said this week?'

Argentina's post-match conduct had earlier come under scrutiny in their semi-final against England, when unused substitute Valentin Barco celebrated Enzo Fernandez's equaliser by running towards the Three Lions' backline rather than joining his team-mates.

Barco is later thought to have said something in the direction of Jude Bellingham which prompted the Real Madrid star to smack him on the back of his head.

The Argentine national team later unfurled a banner repeating Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands, which has also seen FIFA open an investigation into their breach of the tournament's rules around political messaging.

Sports.title: THE ANALYST - Alex Scott: Why Man United and Arsenal are battling for £80m 'diamond' who's refused to sign new Bournemouth deal - how he dominates midfield despite slight frame, the attributes that wowed Mikel Arteta and United's advantage in race
Sports.content:
THE ANALYST - Alex Scott: Why Man United and Arsenal are battling for £80m 'diamond' who's refused to sign new Bournemouth deal - how he dominates midfield despite slight frame, the attributes that wowed Mikel Arteta and United's advantage in race

Read THE ANALYST only on DailyMail+ as we give you the ultimate lowdown on the world's biggest talents - and tell you how they would fit in at YOUR club

When it comes to recruitment at the highest level of the game, it is often the intangibles that set players apart.

Is he a good trainer? What happens when he is left out? Does he get on well with team-mates? Can he listen and take on board tactical information? How does he manage disappointment? And can he handle pressure?

In the case of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, who has turned down a new contract offer from the club, it’s his intangibles report card, just as much as his passing, dribbling and all-action play on the pitch, that has Manchester United, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur circling with intent this summer, with the player valued around £80million.

‘He’s an absolute diamond off the pitch. He’s really, really good and he's one that you'd just want around the group,’ Ian Foster, who managed Scott with England Under 19s and Under 20s, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘He's such a good kid, and I think he's still under the radar for me.’

Brian Tinnion chuckles when those comments are put to him. When he was Bristol City technical director he brought Scott to Ashton Gate from Guernsey FC, who play in the Isthmian League.

‘The best thing about him is his attitude,’ Tinnion explains. ‘His attitude to play, the attitude to training, and he was never one bit of bother from the minute he walked in the building until the minute we sold him to Bournemouth. He was the absolute dream young person to work with.’

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is being chased by Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham this summer

The former Bristol City man is now valued at around £80million

The intangibles weren’t always enough, however, and more concrete hurdles almost killed Scott’s career. His lack of height and physicality as a youngster saw Southampton cast him aside. He had a year at Bournemouth, fell out of love with the game and went back home to Guernsey, where he became their youngest ever player.

He decided to take one last swing at making it in England, with a trial at Bristol City. This was likely his last chance, and he had to take it.

‘We organised a friendly game for him against a London academy who wanted to play us,’ Tinnion says. ‘So Alex came across for the week and he scored a perfect hat-trick in 35 minutes – left foot, right foot, header. I'm like, “Wow, who's this lad?”. We'd seen and watched him, but watching him close up like this, he was outstanding.’

He rose to the occasion with England, too. It was Scott’s header, coming off the bench in a semi-final against Italy, that kept the Young Lions on their path to winning the Under 19s Euros in 2022. And it was Scott who started alongside Elliot Anderson in last summer’s Under 21s Euros final, helping to throw Germany completely off their game.

So, to answer the questions posed earlier: Is he a good trainer? Among the very best. What happens when he is left out? He often changes games at the highest level from the bench. Does he get on well with team-mates? Nobody has a bad word to say about him. Can he listen and take on board tactical information? Managers spoken to for this piece insist he can take on the most detailed of briefs.

What about handling disappointment? Well, after joining Bournemouth in 2023 for £25m, a knee injury restricted him to three games, then a year later he tore his meniscus. He broke his jaw on the eve of the Under 21s Euros, and came off injured and in tears in the final.

He bounced back in the season just gone to get Bournemouth into Europe. And though he didn’t quite make this summer’s World Cup squad, he was on Thomas Tuchel’s radar enough to join the Florida training camp.

And can he handle pressure? Without any hesitation, yes.

Scott and Elliot Anderson, who has completed a £116m move to Man City, were a superb pair in England's Under 21s Euros win last year

Scott (left) has impressed Thomas Tuchel to the point he was called up to England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida

Now to Scott’s appeal on the pitch. His versatility makes him an attractive target to many of the game’s elite clubs. Having first been deployed as a wing-back by Bristol City, Scott has moved inside, playing as a deeper-lying No 6, a box-to-box No 8, and an attack-minded No 10 just behind a striker.

Where Manchester United are targeting a rhythm-setting defensive midfielder to complement Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes, Arsenal are seeking ball-carriers to help get them up the pitch quicker in transition.

Deceptively strong, Scott showed last season what an impressive driver of the ball he is, with 21 per cent of his carries deemed to be progressive – stats providers define this as taking the ball at least five metres closer to the opposition goal. That was the fourth-highest mark of any defensive midfielder in Europe’s top five leagues last season.

Under Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth and Lee Carsley with England Under 21s, Scott has more recently been tasked with a deeper role, working as a rhythm disruptor. He did that to great effect, particularly alongside Anderson, one of his best friends in football, on international duty.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who values players who can play in multiple positions such as Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kai Havertz and any number of his centre backs who can also play at full back, got a first-hand example of Scott’s class in April, when Bournemouth came to the Emirates Stadium and played the Gunners off the park in a 2-1 victory, with Scott getting the winner.

‘He has played for us as a No 10, a No 8; today as a No 6 and he has added a lot of defensive work and a lot of duel-winning to the ability he has on the ball,’ Iraola explained after that match. ‘I’m very happy, because he is becoming a very, very complete player.’

For Foster, it is important that Scott continues to rotate through the roles he can play, rather than keeping him stuck in one position. ‘Whether it’s 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, I wouldn't pigeonhole Alex really in terms of a number on his back,’ he says. ‘I just think he can affect the game really positively. I think he's got really high levels of game understanding and he just knows what's required.

‘He's an old-fashioned all-around midfield player. If you would have asked what Paul Scholes and Roy Keane were, they were central midfield players and I think Alex is that. He can get up and down, he can hold midfield, he can burst into the box, he can score and create. He's an all-round, really, really good midfield player.’

Scott's ability to dribble through the midfield is of particular interest to Arsenal, who need players that can break down opposition defences

Scott's defensive ability is a lot better than his slight frame would make you expect

This summer transfer window will be defined by the market for central midfielders.

Anderson has sealed a British transfer record £116m move to Manchester City, Spurs spent a combined £185m on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, both Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea) and Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) would fetch enormous fees if they were allowed to leave.

And the stats show Scott has already vaulted himself into the conversation among the Premier League’s best midfielders, able to turn a match on his own.

He ranked third behind Anderson (80) and Guimaraes (75) for fouls won from central midfield last season.

He made more clearances than Arsenal pair Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi (both 78) and departed Manchester United anchor Casemiro (73) and ranked third for completed dribbles (29) among central midfielders, again behind Anderson (50) and Morgan Gibbs-White (30).

‘He’s very, very brave, in terms of taking the ball under the pressure,’ Foster adds. ‘He's got the ability as a midfield player to just beat you one-v-one, he's very creative.’

Coaches are also quick to point to Scott’s impact in both boxes, in terms of winning headers and duels at set-pieces, as an area of the game supporters often overlook due to his Jack Grealish-like frame and appearance.

But Scott’s situation, in Bournemouth’s view at least, is clear. He’s not for sale. With two years left on his deal, and new boss Marco Rose eager to build his whole project around Scott, Bournemouth have no appetite to sell, and maintain they are desperate to tie him down to a new deal that will increase his price tag - despite the midfielder rejecting fresh terms.

Scott scores the winner against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in April

Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’

That is unlikely to deter United, Arsenal or Chelsea. Scott’s step-sister Maya Le Tissier is captain of United’s women’s team. Her role in any pursuit may yet prove crucial.

United have already splashed on midfield reinforcements this summer, signing Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa via his £38m release clause alongside adding Andrey Santos in a £50m package from Chelsea.

But United remain in the market for a third midfielder and will be encouraged by Scott's decision not to sign a new contract at Bournemouth. That said, United would struggle to make a meaningful offer without a sale.

Arsenal, meanwhile, missed out on Morgan Rogers - who is set to join Chelsea in a £117m deal, topping the record Anderson set earlier this month - but are keen on Newcastle's Guimaraes.

Crystal Palace, West Ham and Tottenham, the team he grew up supporting, all looked at Scott in January 2023, before passing up and allowing Bournemouth to get him a few months later.

Scott is loved by Nigel Pearson, who gave him his debut at Bristol City; loved by Foster, and has a massive fan in Carsley. Iraola is smitten with him, and may yet push him up Liverpool’s shopping list, and Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’.

United, Arsenal and Chelsea know those footballing minds can’t all be wrong when it comes to the intangibles. So, let the bidding begin.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will both take part in warm-up fights later this week, and one boxing legend has revealed why fans should not be worried ahead of their clash later this year

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally face off (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are both expected to come away without a scratch in their warm-up fights, finally setting up a long-awaited showdown.

‌



That is according to boxing legend Teddy Atlas - who expects the heavyweight icons to 'wipe the floor' with their respective opponents. Joshua will make a sensational return to the ring on Saturday night - seven months on after being involved in a horrific car crash just days after knocking out Jake Paul.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion will take on unknown fighter Kristian Prenga over in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. But just over 24 hours before Joshua makes the walk to the ring, Fury is expected to have a tune-up fight of his own. The 'Gypsy King' will meet Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand.

‌



Providing both men win, they will meet later this year. The pair finally agreed to a fight earlier this year, and are expected to settle their 10-year feud in November. While Prenga has vowed to scupper those plans, Atlas is expecting a relatively easy night at the office for both Fury and 'AJ' later this week.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

In an interview with CanadaCasino, he said: "I think the warm-up fights are pretty much foregone conclusions. I’m not knocking anyone who gets in the ring, but in a practical sense, they are foregone conclusions. Wach is 46 years old and has been knocked out five times. With Joshua and Prenga, I think it is all up to Joshua and how long the fight goes. But we don’t know where Joshua is emotionally coming off that near-fatal car accident. We don’t know how that has impacted him. We saw how a car accident may have impacted Errol Spence.

"With Joshua, I definitely tell you it has impacted him. I just don’t know how much and how. If he is in a halfway decent place, I think he goes behind the jab, catches Prenga and the fight is over, maybe in two rounds. If he is not, maybe he does not do anything for a few rounds and allows Prenga to survive. But at the end of the day, there should only be one guy left standing, and it should be Joshua."

Anthony Joshua sent brutal warning ahead of boxing comeback READ MORE :

Barry Hearn gives clear verdict on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight collapsing READ MORE :

Fans are chomping at the bit to see both Joshua and Fury trade leather, but Atlas believes the fight has been made far too late, seeing as both men have lost multiple times over the last few years. "It’s definitely a money grab," he said. "Joshua is two fights on from being knocked out badly against Dubois, Fury has lost a couple of times to Usyk, and both of them have lost their most significant fights of recent times. There is no arguing that both of them have slippage in their performances and in their careers at this point in their lives. They are not spring chickens anymore. They have been in tough fights, and it shows.

Article continues below

"Ali and Frazier in Manila were too late. Their skills had been eroded, they had been diminished, but it became one of the great heavyweight fights because they were more available to each other than they would have been when their skills were sharper. The one thing that was not diminished was their character, their resolve, their determination and their championship qualities. So yes, Fury vs Joshua is late, and yes, it’s a money grab, but it still might give you some of that because they’re heavyweights.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved

The England legend was set to be a special guest at next season's opening game against his old club Liverpool at St James' Park on August 23 before he died from cancer

Toon fans pay tribute to Kevin Keegan

Kevin Keegan was planning an emotional return to his beloved Newcastle United before his tragic death from cancer.

‌



"King Kev" was set to be a special guest at next season's opening game against his old club Liverpool at St James' Park on August 23. He told an audience at his last appearance on Tyneside that he 'did not want a statue' like fellow Toon idols Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer. But he intended to see the "Toon army" one last time.

‌



His tragic death from cancer at 75 meant that he never got that chance. Lifelong fan Joe Black wore a Newcastle Utd shirt today which had been signed by Keegan during his personal appearance at the Tyne Theatre in Newcastle in May.

‌



View 7 Images Lifelong Newcastle United fan Joe Black with the shirt signed on his last appearance on Tyneside

He joined a stream of fans today at St James' Park who paid tribute, including his son, also Joe, 34, and his six-year-old grandson Joe. He said: "I am going to wear my shirt for the opening game of the season and then keep it and never wear it again.

"My dad was also called Joe and he was black and white daft. My first game was when I was five years old and I have been coming ever since and I am 69 now. Keegan was a hero, he was something else, and we will never forget him."

‌



Newcastle-born Carolyn Ridley, 63, also a lifelong fan, came to pay tribute and 'share stories' with supporters. He said: "He brought such great times, I still get goosebumps thinking about it. He lifted everything when he was a player and manager.

View 7 Images Kevin Keegan tributes at St James' Park (Image: Mirrorpix)

"We will never forget the excitement of his teams, he nearly won the league. But his football was just brilliant; I think he got the Geordies, and we got him and loved him. Every time you came here you knew you were going to see goals; he will be remembered for that and of course that TV rant."

‌



Keegan himself joked that people would remember his 'perm, his crash on TV's Superstars and his rant at Man Utd." Sir Alex Ferguson, the man famously on the other end of Keegan's "I'd love it, absolutely love it, if we beat them" tirade, said: "I had the utmost respect for him.

View 7 Images Newcastle United fan Carolyn Ridley came to pay her respects at St James' Park (Image: Mirrorpix)

"We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but I have to say the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic. He re-energised that club and brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism that great supporters can give. That's the job he did.

‌



"And he also brought three great players to the club: David Ginola, Faustino Asprilla, and Philippe Albert. I must say the challenges we had at that time were huge. It gave Newcastle - I think - their best ever team."

Fergie told Track Radio: "The best thing about him was that he held no grudges and I admired him for that." Schoolfriends Ross Hickson, 46, and Steven Porritt, of Gateshead, bumped into each other outside St James' Park.

View 7 Images Alex Ferguson said he had the 'utmost respect' for Kevin Keegan (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

‌



They shared memories of Keegan's heyday as both a player and manager. "I met him when I was 12 or 13 at the training ground," Steven, a floor layer, recalled.

"I was picking up the footballs and he said to me: 'We are £3m in debt, we can't afford to lose them'. Then he got me a ball which I got signed and took into school. He loved it up here and we loved him. I am 47 years old and could not stop crying when I heard he had died yesterday."

Ross, a courier, added: "For me, he is up there with Sir Bobby Robson as a legend of this club." Fans left floral tributes around the Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer statues at the ground.

‌



View 7 Images Shola Ameobi former Newcastle United player paid his respects to Kevin Keegan (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Former player Shola Ameobi and Newcastle Central MP Dame Chi Onwurah both came to pay their respects. One tribute read: "White roses for the Geordie from Yorkshire. You broke our hearts in 1974 but made up for it."

Another card read: 'Kevin Keegan, Angel of the North'. Others said that whatever tribute was offered 'would never be enough'. Chris Hughton, the former Toon manager, recalled Keegan's wonderful rapport with players.

‌



"He was an incredible coach. He was down to earth, charismatic, and always incredibly honest," he said. Lee Clark, now manager of Hartlepool United, played under Keegan in the 90s.

View 7 Images Fans have left tributes around the grounds of St James' Park in Newcastle (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

When he first passed his driving test, Keegan told him to take his new sports car back because he did not like the way Clark was driving it. He did the same again with Clark's next car. He said: "He was like the Pied Piper to the Geordie public. They adore him."

‌



The former BBC broadcaster Gary Richardson interviewed Keegan on many occasions. Richardson recalled completing one interview about Keegan's early life before explaining that he was returning to London. Keegan asked him to stay and they chatted for two hours.

"It was one of the greatest days of my life in broadcasting. And that is just because of the way that he was ," he added. Keegan told him that he was a 'lucky man' because all of his dreams had come true - winning the league with Liverpool, playing for England and Newcastle United, and working with the great Bill Shankly.

View 7 Images Keegan made 63 appearances for England, 31 of those as captain (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

‌



"Three days after joining Liverpool he came up to me and said 'you will play for England son," Keegan recalled. "And I never had any doubt about it because it was Bill Shankly telling me. And he did not mess around."

In a statement on behalf of Keegan's former Liverpool team mate and close friend Terry McDermott, his family said: "We are heartbroken by the loss of our dear friend, Kevin Keegan. Kevin was so much more than a teammate.

Article continues below

"He was a lifelong friend whose warmth, loyalty, humour and passion for football touched so many lives. The memories they shared, both on and off the pitch, will be treasured forever. Although Terry’s dementia means he is no longer able to express his feelings publicly, we know how much Kevin meant to him and how deeply this loss would have affected him.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with Jean, Laura, Sarah and all of Kevin’s family at this incredibly sad time. We hope they find comfort in the love and respect being shown for Kevin by so many people. Kevin was one of football’s true greats, but to Terry he was, above all, a cherished friend. He will be greatly missed and never forgotten."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked

Lionel Messi's Argentina speech has caused a stir with numerous conspiracy theories emerging after the World Cup final

View 2 Images Lionel Messi hinted at a pre-match issue for Argentina during the speech to his team-mates before the World Cup final (Image: TyC Sports)

Conspiracy theories over a potential issue distracting Argentina players in the World Cup final have been sparked after footage emerged of Lionel Messi's strange pre-match speech.

‌



Lionel Scaloni's side failed to lay a glove on Spain at MetLife Stadium on Sunday and though they defended valiantly, the 2022 champions did not muster a shot until the second half of extra-time. A number of theories have emerged over why their performance was so bad and the latest of those has hinted at a significant problem just before the match started.

‌



Fresh footage from inside the tunnel has supported those claims and also provided more evidence of Scaloni stating that things happened before the final. As the Argentina players emerge from their dressing room, Messi has been captured stating: "Come on, boys, let's forget what happened, as if nothing had happened."

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez and Enzo Fernandez are among those in the background of the video appearing visibly upset. The latter was sent off in the final knockings of normal time while Martinez went off injured during the first half.

The X account @arielipillo, which has 80,000 followers, has claimed that they were emotional and distracted because of unannounced anti-doping tests moments before the game started.

However, that post has been hit with a community note which clarifies that FIFA anti-doping controls are carried out after matches and not before.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Cameras also caught comments from Messi and Emiliano Martinez as the players headed back out for the second half.

Via Sport, Argentina's captain said "Come on, lads. Personality, people, personality. We've always had it, so why wouldn't we have it now? We have the personality to play. Martinez added: "With heart, lads. Let's move forward, not backward... Only cowards play backward.

‌



In addition to the strange behaviour, some Argentina players disgraced themselves with their conduct after losing to Spain. Leandro Parades was involved in a brawl with Gavi and Eric Garcia while Nahuel Molina and assistant coach Roberto Ayala appeared to throw punches.

View 2 Images TOPSHOT - Argentina's midfielder #05 Leandro Paredes (top) clashes with Spain's midfielder #09 Gavi during the 2026 World Cup football tournament final match between Spain and Argentina at the New York/New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford on July 19, 2026. (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images)

The former was among many to release statements following defeat in the final with Messi's public declaration particularly heartfelt.

‌



He wrote: “The pain is immense, it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also choose to hold on to all the good things, all matches we turned around by giving everything and moments that will remain in our memories forever.

“I will always remember the support of an entire country that, together with the work and effort of this group, brought us back once again among the best teams in the world. I also want to congratulate Spain on winning World Cup.”

“Today, it is difficult to appreciate what we achieved… but this group has really reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message. Once again, we managed to come together as a country and stand united, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

Sports.title: Grand National-winner’s training partnership to end as ally announces new venture
Sports.content:
Grand National-winner’s training partnership to end as ally announces new venture

After two and a half years together a restructure will result in Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole going their separate ways as trainers

View 2 Images Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole (left): going their separate ways

One of the most successful training partnerships since their introduction is to split.

‌



Grand National-winning trainer Dr Richard Newland announced two and half years ago that he was expanding his operation into the Flat and he was taking on Jamie Insole to help manage it. Newland tasted Aintree glory with Pineau De Re in 2014, while he also has a Cheltenham Festival winner on his CV thanks to the 2007 Coral Cup success of Burntoakboy.

‌



After starting training with only three horses in 2006 Newland sent out more than 500 winners and nearly 150 after teaming up with Insole at his state of the art yard in Droitwich, Worcestershire.

‌



Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch READ MORE :

Jockey William Buick banned for eight days after being blamed for causing horse stumble READ MORE :

Together they won the Lennox Stakes at Goodwood last year with Witness Stand while Dividend recorded two wins during the Dubai Carnival.

But from the end of August Insole is to establish a yard in Lambourn with his partner, Racing TV presenter Jess Stafford.

“Following recent reports and the decision to restructure the training operation at Urloxhey, I can confirm that my training partnership with Dr Richard Newland will come to an end next month,” Insole said in a statement.

‌



View 2 Images Hollie Doyle on Witness Stand with Jamie Insole (left): struck in the Lennox Stakes (Image: PA)

“I am immensely proud of what we have achieved over the past two and a half years. From a standing start I established and developed the Flat operation at Urloxhey alongside a fantastic and hardworking team, and together we have enjoyed some memorable successes.”

He continued: “I will always be grateful to Richard for giving me the opportunity to begin my training career within the partnership. Establishing yourself as a trainer in Britain is no easy task, and that opportunity provided an invaluable platform from which to build the Flat string from the ground up.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

“It has always been my ambition to establish my own training business and build an operation that reflects my own vision. Jess and I are now in the advanced stages of finalising a lease on a state-of-the-art yard in Lambourn, with excellent facilities and access to some of the best gallops in the country.

“Although the move to our new Lambourn base has always been planned for later this year, the partnership at Urloxhey will now come to an end beforehand, creating a short term period before I am able to begin training under my own licence.”

Article continues below

He added: “While this transition has arrived sooner than anticipated our focus is firmly on the future.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi snubs Argentina parade as he flies home separately from disgraced team-mates
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi snubs Argentina parade as he flies home separately from disgraced team-mates

Argentina's players are still reeling from their World Cup final defeat but that hasn't stopped them from hosting a bus parade which Lionel Messi snubbed

View 3 Images Argentina held a bus parade after their World Cup final defeat but Lionel Messi wasn't there (Image: Getty)

Lionel Messi flew back to Argentina separately from his international team-mates after their 1-0 World Cup final loss to Spain. Most of La Albiceleste's squad embarked on an open-top bus parade in Buenos Aires after landing, but 11 players, including Messi, did not make an appearance.

‌



Argentina's dreams of back-to-back World Cup titles were crushed by Luis de la Fuente's Spain on Sunday evening as La Roja lifted the trophy for just the second time in their history. Yet, the match itself was overshadowed by ill discipline.

‌



Some of Lionel Scaloni's squad were branded disgraceful on the back of their performance, during which Argentina failed to register a shot on target until extra time and Enzo Fernandez was sent off for two egregious bookable offences.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final READ MORE :

After the final whistle blew, scenes got even uglier, with Leandro Paredes seemingly throwing Spain's Gavi to the floor and Nahuel Molina appearing to punch opposition skipper Rodri. Argentina's players have since flown home, but 11 stars did not join the bulk of the squad in Buenos Aires and Messi embarked on a separate journey to his homeland altogether.

View 3 Images Manager Scaloni and 15 players took part in the greeting (Image: Getty)

‌



In the wake of their heavily criticised appearance in the final, manager Scaloni and 15 of his players landed at Ezeiza International Airport to a hero's welcome on Monday evening, regardless of the 1-0 defeat they had suffered.

After staff disembarked the plane, Argentine Football Association president Chiqui Tapia, manager Scaloni and veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi led the group across a red carpet before they boarded an open-top bus.

This vehicle travelled along major streets towards the AFA training centre in Buenos Aires. The 15 players will soon begin their holidays from the AFA base.

‌



But 11 stars did not travel with their team-mates. Rodrigo De Paul, Cristian Romero, Julian Alvarez, Geronimo Rulli, Juan Musso, Nico Paz, Giuliano Simeone, Lautaro Martinez, Molina and Fernandez remained in the United States.

It is likely they will embark on vacations from the US. Messi was the 11th player not to travel, though he did fly to Argentina. At 6:28am local time on Tuesday, he arrived at Islas Malvinas International Airport before heading to his home in Rosario.

View 3 Images Messi was emotional after defeat in New Jersey (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

After a stopover in Miami, Messi landed in his home country from New York and will rest with his family in the gated community of Kentucky in Funes. He too was greeted by hordes of fans upon arrival, but opted not to join his team-mates in Buenos Aires.

Messi will jet off to Miami to join his Inter Miami peers after enjoying sufficient rest in Rosario. His parents were unable to attend the World Cup due to his father Jorge's health issues.

Sports.title: Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection
Sports.content:
Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection

Manchester City have agreed to sign Arsenal teenager Mishel Nduka, after the youngster rejected a new deal that would've kept him at the Emirates

View 2 Images Man City have secured a deal to land one of Arsenal's teenage stars

Manchester City have reached an agreement to land Arsenal youngster Mishel Nduka, who turned down a new contract in north London.

‌



The young midfielder is expected to undergo a medical imminently before joining City on scholarship terms, which is likely to lead to a professional deal. Nduka is an England youth international and tipped for a big future.

‌



Nduka moved to Arsenal from Charlton Athletic in 2025 and played for Arsenal’s Under-18s. He also ran out for the club’s under-21 side in Premier League 2 but, despite the offer of a competitive long-term deal, he has chosen to move to Manchester, reports the Athletic.

‌



Nduka’s likely move to City comes after they completed the signing of 17-year-old Jeremy Monga from Leicester City this month. Arsenal were also keen but backed out when they believed the price being quoted was too high. City secured a deal which is worth £12.5m in total - £10m plus £2.5m in potential contingencies.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

City's greatest academy success has been Phil Foden, who continued to blossom under Pep Guardiola before eventually being named the PFA Player of the Year in 2024. Last season was a breakout campaign for Nico O'Reilly, who established himself as the team's first choice left-back.

Rico Lewis was another player to become a fixture in the first-team environment. Enzo Maresca has now come in to replace Guardiola and will be tasked with making use of the club's young talent, with Nduka now among those available to him.

‌



Nduka is not the only youth prospect that Arsenal have lost in recent years with Ayden Heaven moving to Manchester United last year. The centre-half went straight into the first-team squad at Old Trafford and played 18 times for the Red Devils last term.

View 2 Images Ayden Heaven left Arsenal for Man United last year (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

He had been on Arsenal's books since he was 13 and had made his senior debut in a Carabao Cup game, but Sky Sports claimed that he felt a route into the first-team was blocked off. Several players were ahead of him in the pecking order and the Gunners continued to sign players, forcing him into moving.

Article continues below

Heaven became the second young player to join United from Arsenal during that season after striker Chido Obi-Martin moved north in October.

Sports.title: Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch
Sports.content:
Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch

Christophe Soumillon was found to have ridden Puerto Rico in a way which benefitted stablemate Gstaad at Royal Ascot but an appeal panel was not satisfied it was intentional

View 2 Images Gstaad (left) was able to challenge along the far rail after Puerto Rico (obscured) was switched left early in the straight (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Aidan O’Brien is set to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in next week’s £1.2 million Sussex Stakes rematch between Bow Echo and Gstaad.

‌



After the second clash of the year between the 2,000 Guineas first and second in the St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot, Bow Echo confirmed his superiority by holding off Gstaad by a short head.

‌



But that wasn’t the whole story as jockey Christophe Soumillon, who was aboard Puerto Rico, received an eight-day ban for ‘riding in a manner to benefit’ stablemate Gstaad. The ten-time French champion took two glances over his shoulder as he moved Puerto Rico towards the middle the course entering the straight, causing slight inteference to another rival, which left space for Gstaad to make his challenge along the far rail.

‌



Jockey William Buick banned for eight days after being blamed for causing horse stumble READ MORE :

He appealed against the verdict but a disciplinary panel was satisfied he rode in a way which gave an advantage to Gstaad, adding, “For the avoidance of doubt, we are not satisfied that the Appellant intended so to do.” However the suspension was cut to five days.

Puerto Rico, a dual Group 1 winner under Soumillon last year, finished sixth at Ascot but is among the Ballydoyle entries for the July 29 showpiece in which the three-year-olds will race against older horses for the first time.

Confirming his plans for the Glorious Goodwood meeting in an interview with the racecourse, O'Brien said he was keen to run both Gstaad and Puerto Rico. He said: “Gstaad came out of Ascot very well and we’re looking forward to going there with him – we always thought it was a race that would suit him.

‌



View 2 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

“He obviously just failed at Ascot. Things didn’t go perfectly for us at Ascot, and maybe they didn’t for Bow Echo either.

“In the Guineas, we felt we were forced on. We were very forward and had to do our own donkey work, while Bow Echo had lovely cover and everything worked well for him.

‌



“Then we went to Ascot and felt that maybe it didn’t go 100 per cent for us either. Maybe the lads thought it didn’t go perfectly for Bow Echo, either.

“It’s going to be interesting. That’s what I think makes these races great. We’re looking forward to seeing what happens.”

Of Puerto Rico, O'Brien said: “Obviously, Ascot was a complete mess for him. He went forward, and I think he got taken on for the lead. It just all went out the window.

“We had planned on making the running with him. He won his two Group 1s making the running - it just didn’t work for him on the day.

“There was a snowball effect throughout the whole race when that happened, but that’s racing, and it doesn’t go right all the time.

“We’re very happy with his progress since, and we feel that we will see a different horse this time.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight

The former two-time heavyweight champion will return to the ring this weekend before taking on Tyson Fury in an all-British showdown later this year

View Image Anthony Joshua speaks ahead of his return to the ring (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Anthony Joshua has got another three years left in him before finally calling it a day.

‌



That is according to Matchroom founder Barry Hearn - who offered a rather glittering take ahead of the British brawler's return to the ring. The former two-time heavyweight champion will take on unknown heavyweight Kristian Prenga over in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night.

‌



Joshua has not fought since knocking out YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in the sixth round back in December. The 36-year-old had been due to fight again in February, but was forced to postpone his return after he was involved in a horrific car crash just days after his win over Paul.

‌



Many wondered whether Joshua would ever fight again, and even promoter Eddie Hearn had previously suggested that 2026 could be 'AJ's' last year in the ring. But according to Hearn's father, Barry, Joshua seems more motivated than ever.

‌



Anthony Joshua sent brutal warning ahead of boxing comeback READ MORE :

In an interview with Sky Sports, he said: "[Anthony Joshua] is in an amazing place at the moment. Obviously I’ve seen him since 2012, we got very close. He’s like a member of our family really. I don’t think I’ve seen him so motivated for the long term.

"As I say, some of that has been fuelled by that tragic accident, but he’s now talking about the next three years in the ring. It was a year ago we were talking about potentially two fights and then go off to a happy retirement.

"He’s very motivated, he feels good about himself, but boxing is a funny sport. It takes one decent punch from a big lad to knock out anyone in the world."

Article continues below

Barry Hearn gives clear verdict on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight collapsing READ MORE :

Providing Joshua comes away from his fight this weekend unscathed, he will then take on long-time rival Tyson Fury in November. 'AJ' was ringside for Fury's comeback win over Arslanbek Makhmudov back in April. The 'Gypsy King' quickly called out Joshua merely minutes after the contest, but the latter refused to engage in all of the theatrics.

However, just days later, the pair finally agreed to a fight and settling their decade-long feud. Like Joshua, Fury is also expected to fight this week. The Morecambe scrapper will take on veteran heavyweight Mariusz Wach on Friday night over in Thailand. Fury is putting the fight on for charity and will give the proceeds from the 1,500 tickets to local good causes.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
