Sports.title: Hamilton keeps F1 Belgian GP fourth-place finish as mechanic escapes unhurt
Sports.content:
The mechanic hit by Lewis Hamilton during Formula 1’s Belgian Grand Prix pitstop escaped without injury, Ferrari confirmed, with the team fined 30,000 euro for an unsafe release.

Hamilton came in under a virtual safety car on lap 20 to serve his only pitstop as well as a five-second hold for his role in the first-lap contact with George Russell.

After changing the tyres, a mechanic attempted to make a late front wing flap adjustment. But unbeknownst to the mechanic, the Briton had already been given the green light by the controller to depart from his box, leading to the mechanic being struck by the right-front of the car and falling to the ground.

Ferrari has since confirmed that the mechanic in question is doing perfectly fine and has not sustained any injuries, but Hamilton and the team still needed to visit the FIA race stewards for an alleged unsafe release.

The team has since been handed a 30,000 euro fine, 10,000 of which is suspended, with Hamilton keeping his fourth place in the result.

The FIA stewards' verdict read: "The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €30,000 of which €10,000 is suspended for 12 months on condition that the competitor does not commit a similar infringement in the meantime and on the further condition that within 14 days the competitor submits a report to the FIA regarding the incident and protocols introduced to mitigate the risk of such an incident occurring in the future."

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

The stewards didn't feel a sporting penalty was warranted because Hamilton immediately stopped and actually lost time because of the incident. However, given the safety nature of the incident they still felt a fine was warranted, as well as a commitment from Ferrari to review its pit crew communication and procedures.

"The team acknowledged that for Car 44 to have been released in these circumstances was unsafe and attributed the error to an inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic’s failure to notice the green light. The team committed to undertaking a review of their pit stop procedures to ensure an incident such as this will not be repeated."

Hamilton said the incident reminded him of Kimi Raikkonen injuring one of his mechanics at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix. "I'm looking at the lights, and I'm supposed to go when the car's dropping, and I went, and then I saw him to my right, and I stopped," he said. "All I could think at the time was back when Kimi did a leg. I'm just grateful that he didn't get hurt."

Sports.title: Lack of power left Russell “slower than a Formula 2 car” at start | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said the lack of power from his Mercedes at the start of the Belgian Grand Prix left him “slower than a Formula 2 car.”

He retired on the first lap of the race after tangling with Lewis Hamilton at Les Combes. Russell was passed by several drivers on the long run down the Kemmel straight which leads to the corner.

“I came out of turn one and I had no power,” Russell told Viaplay after the race. “I got to the top of Eau Rouge with zero percent battery and I was going slower than a Formula 2 car and I got overtaken by three drivers. It left me totally vulnerable.”

Russell has previously complained about differences in the power deployment between his car and that of team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who won the race.

“I’m getting used to this disappointment, unfortunately,” said Russell, who failed to score in a grand prix for the third time this year.

Antonelli said he has had similar problems with his power unit this season.

“It can happen,” he said. “Being honest, with George this weekend there was a slight loss, and sometimes you just don’t understand. I had the same in Australia, for example.”

The complexity of the new power units makes it difficult to tell how far the driver is influencing the energy delivery, said Antonelli. “It can be a little bit down to driving, but sometimes the system just does something a little bit different,” he explained.

“It’s very complicated. For the team, you have to appreciate the work, because the system is very complicated. Of course they’re trying to make things a bit easier, but sometimes it’s hard to get it perfect.

“Also, with the driving, sometimes, especially on tracks like this that are very energy-demanding, if you start driving differently, then for the system it’s a bit crazy. So it is tricky.

“But I have to agree that this weekend, for George, there was a slight issue. I’m sure it will be fixed for Budapest.”

Sports.title: Hamilton says Spa practice shunt compromised his race pace | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for the victory in the Belgian Grand Prix had he not crashed in third practice.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth at Spa-Francorchamps after an eventful grand prix. He collided with George Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap, which led to Russell’s retirement and a five second penalty being handed to Hamilton, before running into a Ferrari mechanic during a pit lane mishap.

Russell admitted after the accident that he saw the clash as a racing incident that both of them had contributed to. But Hamilton apologised for his part in the collision.

“Ultimately, I’m sorry for George because that obviously ended his race,” Hamilton told the official F1 channel. “But I do agree that it was a racing incident.

“It’s not like I went in aggressive and was misplaced or anything like that. I think it was just an unfortunate scenario, which happens in racing. Then I had damage as well, so I carried that through the race. It was a tough one. I’m hugely grateful for the points given the damage and given the crash yesterday.”

Hamilton had given his Ferrari mechanics a busy few hours on Saturday afternoon after crashing his car at the exit of the Fagnes chicane at the end of the final practice session, but his SF26 had been fixed in time for him to participate in qualifying. However, Hamilton believes that accident compromised his performance for the remainder of the weekend and his final result and he could have joined team mate Charles Leclerc in fighting for victory without the crash.

“Ultimately, it was not a good weekend from my side,” he said. “I think my race pace was strong today and I think without the damage, and probably without yesterday, I think we could have been fighting for the win today.

“Even with the damage I was challenging Charles [Leclerc]. It is what is, we move on, and hope we can have a better weekend next weekend.”

Sports.title: Rise from 21st to sixth “probably my best race” – Hadjar | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar described his performance in the Belgian Grand Prix as “probably my best race” for the team.

Hadjar started all the way down in 21st position on the grid after receiving a ‘back of the grid’ penalty for multiple power unit component infringements. However, he rose up the order through the race to finish in sixth place, extending his run of top six finishes to six races.

Hadjar pitted twice under the early Safety Car to satisfy his two tyre compound requirement, then ran two long stints on hard tyres after the restart to make his way up the order. The Red Bull driver said that long runs on the hard tyre had always been the intention, heading into a weekend where he knew he would be starting down the order.

“We knew that was part of the plan, starting nearly last, and we worked on it quite a lot through the free practice sessions,” he told Sky.

“Our one-lap pace was not the target and, today, it paid off. So I’m glad we really put the work in on the long runs. I think it really helped. And moving forwards, maybe change the approach, because it worked really well.”

After rejoining the track after his final pit stop, Hadjar was around 15 seconds adrift of team mate Max Verstappen ahead, but finished the race around 12 seconds behind the multiple world champion. Hadjar says he is very satisfied with the pace he showed during the race at Spa-Francorchamps.

“I think our one-lap pace, I showed what I needed to show,” he said. “Today I think is probably my best race.

“Race pace-wise. I’m right up there with the leaders, so I’m very glad with my first ten races. To be honest, I’m really looking forward to the race, because there are a lot of things we need to tidy up as a team – in a good way. I think there’s a lot more to come.”

Sports.title: Leclerc “confident I’ve made a step forward” after back-to-back podiums | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc believes he is finding form after taking second place in the Belgian Grand Prix and fighting Andrea Kimi Antonelli for the victory.

The Ferrari driver passed Max Verstappen and George Russell on the opening lap of the race to move into second behind Antonelli, then gained the lead of the race after pitting under a Virtual Safety Car.

He would later be caught and overtaken by Antonelli, but still finished second, just under two seconds adrift of the Mercedes driver. It was Leclerc’s second consecutive podium after winning the British Grand Prix in the last round following a start to the season where he seemed unable to match the performance of team mate Lewis Hamilton.

“I’m confident in saying that I made a step forward,” Leclerc said after the race. “Whether I’m at the level where I want to perform, not yet.

“There are still things in the car that I need to drive around. I cannot drive completely naturally, and that is slowing me down in some parts of the race. So, there are still things that I’ve got to work on in order to be better. But surely it was a step forward, and for that I’m happy. I’ll continue with the one-race-at-a-time approach because, with these cars, it’s very difficult to be confident that if one race weekend goes well, the other one will, because it relies on such small details. With what you do with your driving, it’s never a given that you get the same deployment from one lap to the other, and that’s maybe the frustrating bit about these cars.”

Leclerc admitted at the start of the weekend he expected to be “very far back, maybe to the extent of four or five tenths” a lap around Spa-Francorchamps.

“In qualifying, that was true, but in the race we were a bit closer than we thought,” Leclerc said. “So, it’s been positive.

“I think on two tracks which, on paper, were quite bad for us, we won and we finished second, with a little bit of luck, but still, I think it was a good effort from the team. On two tracks that didn’t fit our car particularly well, we’ve scored good points.”

Asked if he believed he could carry this momentum into next weekend’s race at the Hungaroring and be in contention for victory once more, Leclerc says it’s to difficult to be sure how good his team will be heading into any given weekend.

“We could be, but we could also not be, and we’ll never know until we go there,” he said. “I think it’s very difficult to predict the level of performance of every team.

“I recall very well what the overall feeling was before Monaco, and we arrived in Monaco and were under-performing compared to what everybody thought we would. So, I think we need to be cautious. We just need to do our homework, just like we do at every different track. I think what we did particularly well over these last two weekends was to really make sure that we maximised our package, and that’s the mentality we should keep for Budapest, without thinking about expectations.”

Sports.title: Wolff says Russell not alone in Mercedes power woes, was “team mistake” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff claims all Mercedes-powered cars were down on power during the Belgian Grand Prix.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli won the race for Mercedes, but team mate George Russell crashed out on the opening lap after contact with Lewis Hamilton at Les Combes.

Russell later said that while he felt the contact with the Ferrari driver was a racing incident, he implied that a battery deployment problem – which he had been complaining had been affecting his straight-line performance all weekend at Spa-Francorchamps – was more responsible for causing the clash. Wolff accepted that a power unit deployment problem had been a contributing factor.

“I think there’s two situations here,” he told Sky after the race. “First, the racing accident – that happened. Unfortunately, for us, we lost a lot of constructors points and, George, a lot of drivers’ points.

“George tried on the outside, braked late, and that corner should have been his, but it was a racing incident. These things can happen, whether you’re at the front, in the middle, or at the back of the pack. George had a tough weekend. Probably half of that can be attributed to the power unit, which wasn’t as good as it should have been in his car, and the other half perhaps to the driving.

“But we’re in this together. We all make mistakes. Today it was a team mistake on another day it’ll be a driver’s mistake. We just need to minimise those mistakes and support each other.”

Wolff says that Russell was not the only Mercedes-powered driver who was experiencing lower than expected power deployment during the Belgian Grand Prix.

“We had an issue on all Mercedes engines that we lacked the power out on the straights,” he admitted. “That bit him [Russell] badly and it goes one-hundred-percent on us.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We’re trying our best as a team. We have the most powerful power unit – we have a strong car that is capable of winning. Everybody gives their maximum to minimise their mistakes and still it happens – because we are humans at work. We let Kimi down at Silverstone where George got a podium – that was maybe better than the result should have been – one driver DNF’d in Canada, the other DNF’d in Barcelona. That’s a little bit the story of our season, here. It’s a technical sport, it’s a mechanical sport.

“I’m proud to be a part of the organisation at HPP and Mercedes Grand Prix. Those groups of people give it all they have and we came out with a product this year that is so strong and I’d rather fix the reliability than try to accelerate a slow engine or a slow car. We’re giving it one-hundred-percent and we need to give it one-hundred-percent, because we have lost a lot of points through reliability. We should be much further ahead than we are.”

Russell had been slower than than Antonelli throughout the weekend. Wolff suggested that Antonelli may have learned how to maximise the performance from the new-generation power units for 2026 compared to his more experienced team mate.

“I think, first of all, it’s very different and I think this is probably an advantage that Kimi has, because it reset for everyone,” he said.

“Then the components of energy harvesting and energy deployment plays a role. Even the way you go on the throttle – whether you give it full throttle or half throttle and when you lift off – can have consequences in terms of the energy delivery. And that’s another dimension that has been handed to the driving – some drivers may not like it, others may say ‘okay, we just need to get used to it’. But it’s another component that makes it more complex.”

Wolff said he would talk to Russell to console him following his latest setback in the championship, which has seen him drop to third in the standings behind Hamilton.

“I haven’t seen him yet, but it’s completely understandable that the moment you’re out of this race it’s so frustrating and the emotions boil. That’s why I completely understand. He has our one-hundred-percent support. We are trying to solve all the issues, he’s doing everything he can to get on top of his driving. So I haven’t spoken to him, but I’m going to try and put my arms around him.”

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Says Jeff Fenech Changes Tim Tszyu’s Mindset
Sports.content:
“I feel like if anything, the psychology of Tim with Fenech will be to fight more than flight,” Malignaggi said to The Punch Podcast. “I think if anything, if Fenech’s bringing anything to the table with Tim, it would be more of a mindset than anything else. Pedro Diaz is a very technical trainer, but it doesn’t seem like that’s what Tim needed. I think Tim needed more of the psychological stuff.”

Malignaggi said Fenech’s own fighting style is the reason he expects a more aggressive version of Tszyu on Saturday night. Instead of trying to overhaul Tszyu’s fundamentals in one camp, he sees the Australian great reinforcing an attacking mentality that fits the challenge posed by a returning Spence.

He did say that one technical adjustment he would like to see is that Tszyu’s left hook could become a bigger weapon against the southpaw.

Malignaggi expects Fenech to urge Tszyu to test Spence from the opening bell instead of allowing the former unified welterweight champion to ease back into competition after a three-year layoff.

“I would expect an aggressive Tim Tszyu,” Malignaggi said. “I don’t see how you can not start out this fight aggressively against Errol Spence when you consider what’s in front of you and the question marks about Errol.”

Malignaggi did say that Tszyu has been hurt early in previous fights, making that approach a calculated gamble. He still expects Fenech to press Tszyu into an aggressive start.

Looking ahead to fight night, Malignaggi said he isn’t expecting wholesale technical changes after one camp together.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson Crushes Carl Williams In 93 Seconds
Sports.content:
Williams had earned the opportunity the hard way. The 6-foot-4 challenger was the IBF’s #1 contender after victories over Trevor Berbick and other leading heavyweights. He had also gone the distance with former champion Larry Holmes, and his height, long reach and jab were considered his best weapons against Tyson’s relentless pressure.

Promoted by Don King and televised by HBO, the championship attracted approximately 11,000 fans to Convention Hall. Tyson reportedly earned about $5 million, while Williams received roughly $1.2 million. Ringside tickets sold for $500, although the event generated a much smaller gate than Tyson’s previous blockbuster title defenses.

Williams tried to establish his jab immediately while tying Tyson up whenever the champion closed the distance. Tyson continued stalking forward, slipping punches and waiting for an opening.

That opening arrived barely more than a minute into the fight. Williams fired another left jab, Tyson slipped outside it and answered with a crushing left hook that landed flush on the jaw. Williams crashed backward to the canvas. He beat referee Randy Neumann’s count but remained unsteady as he leaned against the ropes. After asking Williams if he was able to continue and receiving no convincing response, Neumann stopped the fight at 1:33 of the opening round.

The decision immediately drew boos from the Atlantic City crowd. Williams protested the stoppage, insisting he was able to continue, and his camp unsuccessfully sought a rematch. No second meeting ever took place.

The victory improved Tyson’s championship reign with one of the quickest heavyweight title fights in history. It also became the final successful defense of his undisputed championship before Buster Douglas ended his reign in Tokyo on February 11, 1990. Although the ending remains controversial, Tyson’s explosive left hook and the disputed stoppage have kept the fight among the most discussed moments of his championship career.

Sports.title: Roy Jones Jr. Says Errol Spence Takes Over Late Against Tim Tszyu
Sports.content:
Jones Jr. said Tszyu’s best opportunity comes in the opening rounds before Spence settles into his rhythm.

“Man, it’s a hard call, but I’m going with Errol. Hope Errol can withstand the early start that Tszyu is going to probably put up early because if you get past four or five rounds, Errol definitely is going to beat him because Errol, to me, is stronger later than anybody fighting. You get him past round six, and you got a problem in your hand. I don’t care who it is, especially if he ain’t beat up or nothing in the face. You get to round six, you got a problem because that’s when he starts to come alive. Ask Ugas. Ask Brook,” Jones Jr. said to Fight Hub TV.

Roy Jr. compared Spence’s relentless style to Marvin Hagler’s, arguing that constant pressure eventually wears opponents down. He also pointed out that Spence has more technical ability than many people remember from his amateur days, even though he has relied primarily on pressure as a professional.

The matchup remains a difficult one because Tszyu is naturally aggressive and has never been afraid to trade punches. That style may create entertaining early rounds, but it also plays into the kind of fight Spence has often thrived in if he can avoid taking too much punishment at the start.

Jones Jr. believes surviving the opening rounds is the key. If Errol reaches the middle rounds without absorbing significant damage, he expects the former unified welterweight champion to begin taking control with steady pressure and superior stamina.

A victory over Tszyu would put Spence back in the title picture at 154 pounds after a three-year absence from the ring. A loss would leave him facing another setback at a point in his career when every fight carries added significance.

Sports.title: Salvador Sanchez’s Final Triumph: The Classic Battle With Azumah Nelson
Sports.content:
The bout carried significant championship stakes. Sanchez defended both the WBC featherweight championship and The Ring featherweight championship for the 10th time. Already established as one of boxing’s premier pound-for-pound fighters, the Mexican star had built his reputation with victories over Hall of Famers Danny Lopez, Wilfredo Gomez, Juan LaPorte and Roberto Castanon.

Nelson came in as the WBC’s #10-ranked featherweight contender after accepting the fight as a late replacement. Largely unknown to American fans, the 24-year-old Ghanaian had never faced anyone close to Sanchez’s level, and most observers expected another successful title defense for the champion.

The unfamiliar challenger hurt attendance. Only 5,575 fans paid to attend the event, producing a modest gate of $129,244 despite Don King serving as promoter. Sanchez, as the champion and established attraction, earned the larger purse. Nelson also received the biggest payday of his young career, although the official purse figures were never publicly disclosed. Veteran referee Tony Perez worked the bout.

What unfolded surprised nearly everyone. Instead of being overwhelmed, Nelson attacked Sanchez from the opening bell with relentless pressure. He fired hooks, overhand rights and body punches, forcing the champion into one of the toughest fights of his title reign. Nelson captured several early rounds with his aggression and briefly had Sanchez backing toward the ropes, something rarely seen during the champion’s prime.

Sanchez began making the necessary adjustments. Beginning in the middle rounds, his timing became sharper. He started landing crisp counter left hooks, straight rights and punishing body shots that slowed Nelson’s relentless attack.

In the seventh round, Sanchez scored the fight’s lone knockdown with a sharp left hook, but Nelson beat the count and survived the remainder of the round.

Sanchez closed the fight by landing the sharper combinations and investing to the body, gradually breaking down Nelson’s offense before the 15th-round stoppage.

The conclusion arrived in the 15th and final round. Sanchez trapped Nelson along the ropes and unloaded a sustained barrage of hooks and body shots. Nelson remained upright but was no longer defending himself effectively. At 1:49 of Round 15, Perez stepped in and stopped the contest, awarding Sanchez a technical knockout after one of the finest performances of both men’s careers.

Following the fight, Sanchez praised Nelson’s toughness, later describing him as one of the strongest and most durable opponents he had faced. The fight proved career-defining for both men.

It became the final chapter of an extraordinary career for Salvador after his death on August 12, 1982, in a Porsche crash that deprived boxing of one of its brightest young champions. Many historians still rank him among the greatest featherweights in history despite his short career.

The defeat for Nelson became a launching point rather than a setback. The defeat raised Nelson’s profile, and he went on to win world titles in three weight classes before being inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

Over four decades later, Sanchez-Nelson has grown in stature. What appeared to be a routine title defense during the summer of 1982 is now remembered as one of the finest featherweight championship fights ever contested and the unforgettable final masterpiece of Salvador Sanchez’s career.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Taunts Keyshawn Davis After WBO Purse Bid Order
Sports.content:
“Anybody seen Keyshawn Davis?” Bill Haney posted on X.

The WBO’s order gives Devin Haney a commanding 75/25 purse split as champion if negotiations fail and the fight goes to a purse bid. Instead of celebrating a mandatory title shot, Team Davis suddenly finds itself staring at a brutal financial reality.

As champion, Haney is entitled to 75% of the winning purse bid and has little incentive to give ground while the mandatory process favors him.

The order also changes the conversation surrounding Haney’s options. Before the WBO stepped in, most of the attention was on a fight with Shakur Stevenson. Now the mandatory defense against Davis takes priority, and the July 27 purse bid deadline gives both sides limited time to reach an agreement.

If no deal is reached, the winning bidder will secure promotional rights for the fight under the WBO’s 75/25 split. That reality leaves Team Davis with an important decision. They can either reach terms before the deadline or allow the purse bid process to determine where and under what promoter the fight takes place.

Team Haney has little reason to blink before July 27. The WBO’s order already gives Devin Haney the financial advantage, leaving the pressure on Team Davis to decide its next move.

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco Looks Much Improved Against Immanuwel Aleem
Sports.content:
Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn told the media at the post-fight presser that Pacheco made a sensible decision choosing to wait for a title match, being that he had a new training team and Pacheco preferred to take the fight until he was ready at 100 percent.

Saturday night, a much-improved Pacheco boxed a much more technically sound fight by controlling the distance, utilizing his jab, and being defensively disciplined. Against Sadjo, Pacheco took a lot of punishment and also suffered the first knockdown of his professional career, but against Immanuwel Aleem (22-5-3, 14 KOs), he showed another level.

He landed 44.2 percent of his total punches, keeping Aleem at range with his jab. Immanuwel struggled to get on the inside and was offensively ineffective, finding minimal success connecting on only 24.1 percent of his total punches (Compubox).

WBC interim world super middleweight champion Lester Martinez (20-0-1, 16 KOs) fought Aleem to a close and hard-fought 12-round unanimous decision. Many believed he would be a much more challenging opponent for Diego, but he proved otherwise.

After the fight, Pacheco expressed to the media at the post-fight presser his desire to continue his progression and fight the best super middleweights in the world. He’d like fights against Jaime Munguia, Christian Mbilli, Hamzah Sheeraz, and Canelo Alvarez.

It’s only his first fight under Buddy, and his potential is limitless. He demonstrated Saturday night at the War Grounds he has the potential to challenge for a world title. Hearn said he hopes to have Pacheco fight at this venue again this year, around October or November, but will keep their options open if a big fight comes along.

Sports.title: Olympic Gold And Professional Glory: Champions Who Conquered Both
Sports.content:
Among the earliest examples was Frankie Genaro, who won Olympic flyweight gold in 1920 before claiming the NBA flyweight championship as a professional. The 1924 Games produced three future professional champions in Jackie Fields, Willie Smith, and Fidel LaBarba.

The post-war era continued the trend with Pascual Perez, Floyd Patterson, Nino Benvenuti, Joe Frazier, and George Foreman. Patterson became the youngest heavyweight champion in history at the time, while Foreman and Frazier carried their Olympic success into Hall of Fame careers.

The 1970s and 1980s produced another remarkable generation. Michael Spinks, Sugar Ray Leonard, Pernell Whitaker, Lennox Lewis, Ray Mercer, Henry Maske, Mark Breland, Meldrick Taylor, Frank Tate, Patrizio Oliva, Maurizio Stecca, Mate Parlov, Leo Randolph, Giovanni Parisi, and Kennedy McKinney all captured professional world titles after winning Olympic gold.

Oscar De La Hoya extended that tradition after the 1992 Barcelona Games, becoming one of boxing’s biggest attractions while winning titles in six weight classes.

The modern era has added Guillermo Rigondeaux, Andre Ward, Yuriorkis Gamboa, Vasiliy Lomachenko, Robeisy Ramirez, and Robson Conceição to the list. Ward retired undefeated after becoming the unified light heavyweight champion, while Lomachenko captured world titles in three weight classes after winning Olympic gold in both 2008 and 2012.

Not every Olympic champion reaches the top of the professional game, making this list a reminder of how difficult it is to dominate both amateur and professional boxing. While Olympic gold opens doors, history shows that only a relatively small percentage of champions have gone on to win recognized world titles in the paid ranks.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Admits Discipline Failed Him Before Steven Butler Fight
Sports.content:
“I feel like I was just getting by just because of my talent,” Berlanga said on Brian Custer’s channel. “What separated me from those guys was my dedication and my discipline. I always gave myself 50%. This camp has been different. The light switch turned on.”

What Berlanga isn’t saying is that what played a part in him being able to get by at only 50% is how he was managed. The early narrative was built on a shiny marketing gimmick: 16 straight first-round knockouts. Top Rank arguably spoon-fed him opponents selected specifically to keep the streak alive.

Once he stepped up into actual eight- and ten-rounders against basic step-up opponents like Demond Nicholson, Marcelo Coceres, Steve Rolls, and Roamer Alexis Angulo, the knockout power suddenly vanished. He was getting dropped, biting opponents out of frustration, and looking completely ordinary against basic journeymen.

Matchroom essentially bought into the hype to leverage his Puerto Rican fanbase in New York, giving him soft touches like Jason Quigley and Padraig McCrory to line him up for a massive payday against Canelo Alvarez.

When Berlanga finally stepped up to elite level, the reality caught up with him. Canelo Alvarez outclassed him across 12 rounds, dropping him along the way. Hamzah Sheeraz exposed the gap in level by stopping him inside five rounds.

Attributing his struggles entirely to “lack of discipline” or “giving 50%” is a classic promotional spin to protect a fighter’s brand. Lack of dedication may play a role, but the primary reason he looked invincible early on was careful matchmaking hiding serious technical limitations, limitations that got punished the second he stepped in with elite competition.

“I want to change the perspective of people,” Berlanga said. “I want to be talked about like Bam Rodriguez, Shakur Stevenson… that I got skill, IQ. I owe it to myself.”

Comparing himself to operators like Crawford, Shakur, or Bam is completely disconnected from who he is in the ring.

Those guys are elite, generational defensive technicians and sweet scientists with master-level footwork, ring vision, and distance control. Berlanga is an aggressive brawler who relies on raw athleticism, wild power, and intimidating his opponents. You do not wake up at 29 years old after a decade of fighting as a crude slugger and suddenly develop elite IQ, nuanced defense, or counter-punching instincts just because you worked hard in one training camp.

It is one thing when a fighter is just spouting promotional buzzwords to hype a fight, but it is another thing entirely when they genuinely convince themselves of it. In boxing, that kind of delusion is dangerous.

Berlanga spent years being told he was an unstoppable monster while blasting out overmatched opponents in one round. That level of early praise distorts a fighter’s self-image.

Now, facing the reality of his technical limits, his brain is reaching for the easiest explanation: “I just wasn’t trying hard enough.” Accepting that you just lacked effort is a lot easier on the ego than accepting that you simply do not have the natural ring IQ, reflexes, or skill ceiling of a Crawford or a Shakur. If it was just a lack of discipline, it means the talent is still there waiting to be unlocked.

Ghana News.title: ‘Abrogate the contract ,refund deducted funds’ – Sulemana Brimah tells NASPA
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA), Sulemana Brimah, has called on the leadership of the National Service Authority (NSA) to discontinue the ongoing capacity-building programme and refund deductions made from the allowances of national service personnel.

His comments come amid growing concerns among some national service personnel over deductions made from their monthly allowances, including a reported GH¢60 charge for capacity building.

In a Facebook post on Tuesday, July 21, Mr Brimah urged the NSA leadership to terminate the arrangement and expressed concerns over the circumstances surrounding the deductions.

"The leadership at the NSS/NSA should just end the so-called capacity whatever, abrogate the contract, and have the deducted funds refunded before the scheme gets into another wahala," he stated.

Mr Brimah also referred to findings from the forensic audit conducted following the National Service Scheme (NSS) scandal, raising concerns about activities undertaken in the name of the National Service Personnel Association (NASPA).

The forensic audit cited unsupported payments of GH¢9,276,535.00 to NASPA, indicating that significant payments were made to the association during the period.

According to the findings, there were no formal agreements or memoranda of understanding (MoUs) between the NSS and NASPA defining the terms, purpose, scope, and conditions under which the funds were transferred.

It also stated that there was no evidence of accountability or retirement of the funds by NASPA leadership to justify how the monies were applied.

NSA distances itself from deductions

The National Service Authority has, however, stated that it did not authorise any deductions from the allowances of national service personnel.

According to the Authority, the GH¢60 deduction for capacity building was a decision taken by the leadership of the National Service Personnel Association (NASPA), rather than the NSA.

The clarification follows complaints from some national service personnel over deductions from their meager monthly allowances.

Some personnel have argued that the monthly allowance of GH¢715 is already inadequate to meet basic needs such as transportation, feeding, and other essential expenses, adding that the deductions have further increased their financial burden.

Meanwhile, addressing the press on Tuesday, 21 July, the President of NASPA, Abdul Wahab Bala Mohammed, announced the immediate suspension of the Capacity Building Programme pending a comprehensive review.

The suspension follows public criticism of a GH¢60 deduction from the allowances of some service personnel, who argued that they were not adequately consulted before the deductions were made.

Ghana News.title: NASPA clarifies GH¢60 deduction, says fee was meant to be GH¢15 monthly
Ghana News.content:
The National Service Personnel Association (NASPA) has clarified that the GH¢60 deducted from the allowances of service personnel was not originally intended to be paid at once.

The suspension follows public criticism of a GH¢60 deduction from the allowances of some service personnel, who argued that they were not adequately consulted before the deductions were made.

Addressing a press conference in Accra on Tuesday, July 21, NASPA National President Abdul-Wahab Bala Mohammed said the association had initially considered the programme beneficial because of its potential to improve the employability of service personnel.

According to the association, the amount was meant to be spread over a four-month learning period, translating into a monthly contribution of GH¢15.

NASPA explained that the deduction was to cover part of the cost of a training programme introduced to provide service personnel with additional skills and prepare them for the job market.

However, the full GH¢60 deduction from the previous allowance generated concerns among personnel, with many questioning why the amount was taken at once instead of being divided across the four months.

The association acknowledged the concerns, noting that the financial commitment may not have been convenient for all service personnel.

NASPA said it subsequently engaged its newly elected regional executives and gathered feedback from personnel to better understand the issues surrounding the deduction and the level of consultation before the programme was implemented.

“Based on this progress, NASPA formally requested the National Service Authority to facilitate a reduction of GH¢60 to represent the duration of the training over a four-month learning period, that is, GH¢15 per month,” the association stated.

It added that management of the National Service Authority has since engaged NASPA over the concerns and frustrations expressed by personnel and the general public.

The association said further directives have been issued by the NSA management in response to the feedback received and in line with guidance from the sector minister and the board.

It has therefore suspended the capacity-building programme.

Ghana News.title: Flux Power & Automation launches smart energy management system to help Ghanaian businesses cut electricity costs
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian electrical engineering company Flux Power & Automation has launched a smart energy management system aimed at helping businesses and institutions monitor electricity consumption, reduce waste and improve energy efficiency.

The company has introduced Smappee Infinity, a technology developed by Belgian clean technology firm Smappee, to provide organisations with real-time information on how electricity is being used across their operations.

The launch comes as businesses continue to look for innovative ways to manage rising operational costs, with electricity remaining a major expense for many companies.

Chief Executive Officer of Flux Power & Automation, Ing. Kwasi Tetteh Akrobettoe, said the product was introduced to address a major challenge facing businesses — limited visibility into their energy consumption.

“Most businesses only see their electricity bill at the end of the month. They do not know which equipment is consuming excess power or where inefficiencies exist,” he said.

He explained that Smappee Infinity gives businesses the ability to track energy use in real time, identify areas of waste and make informed decisions to improve efficiency.

The system combines energy monitoring, remote control and automation features through a digital dashboard and mobile application. It allows users to monitor consumption patterns, control connected equipment and automate energy use based on operational needs.

According to Flux Power & Automation, the technology can be integrated with existing electrical systems, allowing businesses to improve energy management without replacing equipment such as air conditioners, refrigeration units and industrial machinery.

Targeting key sectors

The company says the product will support organisations across several sectors, including banking, hospitality, healthcare, manufacturing, mining, education, retail and real estate.

Flux Power & Automation believes better access to energy data will help companies reduce unnecessary consumption, lower electricity costs and improve overall business performance.

Before the official launch, Smappee Infinity was piloted at the Lakeside Estate Sales Office in Accra, where it was tested under local operating conditions.

Engineers from the Ghana Standards Authority assessed the installation process, after which the system received approval from the Authority.

Mr Akrobettoe said the successful pilot demonstrated the suitability of the technology for Ghana's business environment.

“Businesses looking to reduce operating costs, improve energy efficiency and lower their carbon footprint should see energy management as a strategic investment,” he said.

Founded in 2012, Flux Power & Automation provides electrical engineering, automation and energy management solutions for residential, commercial and industrial clients.

Through its partnership with Smappee, the company aims to expand access to intelligent energy management solutions and support Ghanaian businesses in making smarter energy decisions.

Ghana News.title: Consortium in talks to buy Liverpool minority stake
Ghana News.content:
A consortium led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia has expressed an interest in buying a minority stake in Liverpool.

Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal, was director and co-owner at QPR for 18 seasons but stepped down from the board and relinquished ownership of the club on Tuesday afternoon.

In a statement, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) told BBC Sport: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

BBC Sport understands that the deal has not yet been finalised with FSG.

If the investment was to proceed, it would follow a similar deal made in 2023, when FSG sold a minority stake in the Reds to global sports investment firm Dynasty for between £82m and £164m.

FSG purchased Liverpool in 2010 for £300m, when the club was on the verge of administration.

According to the Financial Times, a deal with the consortium led by Bhatia would value Liverpool at more than $6bn (£4.5bn).

Image caption,Liverpool finished fifth in the Premier League last season

Who is Amit Bhatia?

Amit Bhatia is a former investment banker who worked for Morgan Stanley on Wall Street before becoming an entrepreneur.

His investments include businesses in construction, real estate, and private equity.

The 46-year-old Londoner was awarded the young entrepreneur of the year award in 2013, and sits on the advisory board of the Saudi Arabian government's cultural affairs and international relations unit.

He was a director and co-owner of QPR before his unexpected departure on Tuesday, and a stand at Loftus Road bears his surname.

He married Vanisha Mittal Bhatia in 2004, in a six-day ceremony in France costing more than $55m (£41m), which was recognised by Guinness World Records as the most expensive of all-time.

Vanisha is the daughter of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, whose net worth has been estimated at more $30bn (£22bn).

Ghana News.title: NASPA suspends capacity building programme after concerns over allowance deductions
Ghana News.content:
The National Service Personnel Association (NASPA) has suspended its capacity-building programme following concerns from national service personnel over deductions made from their monthly allowances to fund the initiative.

The suspension follows public criticism of a GH¢60 deduction from the allowances of some service personnel, who argued that they were not adequately consulted before the deductions were made.

Addressing a press conference in Accra on Tuesday, July 21, NASPA National President Abdul-Wahab Bala Mohammed said the association had initially considered the programme beneficial because of its potential to improve the employability of service personnel.

Read Also: National Service Authority denies authorising allowance deductions, says NASPA approved GH¢60 charge

"We believe that the package represented value for money, especially considering the potential return on investment in terms of your future employability. However, we fully acknowledge that the financial commitment required may not have been reasonable for all service personnel."

He explained that following discussions, NASPA formally requested the National Service Authority (NSA) to reduce the amount to GH¢60, spread over a four-month period at GH¢15 per month.

"Based on this progress, NASPA formally requested the National Service Authority to facilitate a reduction of 60 Ghana cedis to represent the duration of the training over a four-month learning period, i.e. 15 cedis per month, to offset part of the programme costs already incurred, which was deducted in the last allowance."

Mr Mohammed said the association reviewed the programme after concerns over the deductions and the level of consultation intensified.

He said NASPA engaged its newly elected regional executives, gathered feedback from service personnel and held discussions with the management of the National Service Authority.

"As concerns about the programme intensified, particularly regarding the deductions and the level of consultation, we took our time to engage our newly elected regional executives, receive feedback from service personnel, as well as carefully review the issues that had been raised."

According to him, following the engagements and directives from the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment and the National Service Authority's governing board, the programme has been suspended.

"In response to the feedback from the service personnel and general public, and as well as in line with the sector minister's and board's directive, the management have issued this directive to NASPA."

"The capacity building programme, as currently structured, is hereby suspended with immediate effect, pending a comprehensive review of the programme for a decisive action to be taken, which is in line with our sector minister, the Minister of Youth Development and Empowerment, Honourable George Opare-Addo's directive."

Mr Mohammed assured service personnel that no further deductions would be made towards the programme while the review is underway.

"Again, we wish to assure every National Service person that there will be no further deductions on behalf of or in relation to the capacity building training."

He welcomed the decision to suspend the programme and thanked the ministry, the National Service Authority's board and management for responding to the concerns raised.

Ghana News.title: Global drug threats emerging rapidly through technology – NACOC D-G
Ghana News.content:
The Director-General of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, has warned that global drug trafficking networks are becoming increasingly sophisticated, exploiting technology and cyberspace to expand their illicit operations across borders.

Delivering the opening remarks at the Africa–South Asia Inter-Regional Workshop on “Strengthening Cooperation Against New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) and Synthetic Opioid Trafficking”, currently underway at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel in Accra, the Director-General noted that criminal organisations are taking advantage of vulnerabilities within countries to strengthen their operations.

“Ghana is experiencing a trend where these criminal networks are using cyberspace to trade in narcotics,” he stated, stressing the urgent need for stronger regional and international cooperation to counter the evolving threat.

Major General Mantey called on participating countries to deepen collaboration through the timely exchange of intelligence, best practices and coordinated enforcement efforts to dismantle transnational drug trafficking networks operating within Africa and South Asia.

The Ghana Law Enforcement advisor for the US Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs, Mr. Chip Duncan, in his remarks, also said: “The world is facing a drug threat that is moving faster than ever before,” adding that “traditionally, we dealt with plant-based drugs that followed predictable patterns. Today, we face a synthetic revolution”.

“Over 1,200 New psychoactive substances (NPS) have been identified globally. These are chemicals designed to mimic illegal drugs while evading current laws”. Mr. Duncan noted

He added that West Africa is already the world’s largest market for diverted tramadol, with over 180 tons seized every year. More alarming is the recent detection of nitazens, a synthetic opioid that can be 40 times stronger than heroin.

These substances, according to him, “don’t just fuel crime, they kill your citizens and devastate your communities “.

He further stressed that criminal networks are highly organized and tech-savvy, as they use maritime and air corridors to link South-Asia, particularly India and Sri Lanka, to East and West Africa, which creates a global trafficking chain that exploits weak points, limited lab capacities, outdated laws and porous borders.

The four-day workshop brings together experts and law enforcement agencies from across the two regions to strengthen partnerships, enhance real-time intelligence sharing and exchange experiences in addressing the growing threat posed by New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) and synthetic opioids.

The workshop is sponsored by the US Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) and is being facilitated in collaboration with the International Narcotics Control Board (NCB), with the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), and the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi conviction: History has been made; political protection for illegal miners over – Inusah Fuseini
Ghana News.content:
Former Tamale Central MP, Inusah Fuseini, says the conviction of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, signals the end of political protection for persons involved in illegal mining.

According to him, the 20-year prison sentence handed to Wontumi over illegal mining-related offences demonstrates that individuals engaged in galamsey can no longer rely on political connections to avoid accountability.

Speaking on JoyNews' The Pulse on Tuesday, July 21, Mr Fuseini said the development represents a significant moment in Ghana's fight against illegal mining.

"History has been made. Anybody engaged in illegal mining activities can no longer have political insurance in perpetuity. The political insurance obtained by Bernard Antwi Boasiako expired on the 7th of December 2024," Mr Fuseini stated.

He added "anybody who is engaged in illegal mining activities and associated with NDC should know that a time when his politicsal insurance will expire."

Mr Fuseini recalled that concerns about activities involving Akonta Mining Limited in the Samreboi concession were raised during the administration of former President Nana Akufo-Addo.

He said the then Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, Samuel Abu Jinapor, wrote to Akonta Mining after advice from the Minerals Commission, drawing attention to alleged illegal activities and requesting that the company desist.

According to him, the former President's subsequent comments appeared to exonerate Wontumi, a move he believes raised questions about leadership and accountability.

Mr Fuseini further urged President Mahama to use the momentum from the case to intensify the fight against illegal mining, arguing that galamsey has caused severe damage to Ghana's forests, water bodies and livelihoods.

He called for all persons involved in illegal mining, regardless of their political affiliation, to face accountability.

Ghana News.title: No sirens or police escorts without approval, Speaker Bagbin tells MPs
Ghana News.content:
Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has directed Members of Parliament and the Parliamentary Service to comply with a Cabinet directive regulating the use of police escort services and sirens on vehicles.

Addressing Parliament, Mr Bagbin said his office had received a communication from the Minister for the Interior outlining restrictions on the use of police resources, particularly escort services, as well as the installation and use of sirens.

He said the directive had been brought to the attention of lawmakers following a request from the Interior Ministry.

"Honourable members, according to the communication, Cabinet, in compliance with existing law, has requested, among other things, that no person shall install or use a siren on any official or private vehicle without the prior written authorisation of the minister responsible for the Interior," the Speaker said.

The directive also requires written approval from the Interior Minister or the Inspector General of Police, acting on behalf of the minister, before any individual can utilise police resources, including escort services.

Mr Bagbin explained that the Ghana Police Service had been mandated to enforce the directive by removing and seizing unauthorised sirens, discontinuing unauthorised police escort services and pursuing legal action where necessary.

The Speaker urged MPs to take note of the directive and ensure that their actions conform with the law.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: US eyes new tariffs as existing trade duties near expiration
World.content:
US Trade Rep Jamieson Greer hints at new tariffs on 60 trading partners as President Donald Trump’s temporary tariffs expire on Friday.

United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer says a new round of tariffs could be on the way as US President Donald Trump’s latest global duties are set to expire on Friday unless Congress acts.

“We expect to see some action soon,” Greer said on CNBC’s Squawk Box programme when asked if a new wave of tariffs could hit 60 different trading partners.

In February, the White House imposed tariffs under Section 122 of the US Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to levy tariffs of up to 10 percent for 150 days without congressional approval.

Those tariffs were imposed after the Supreme Court struck down Trump’s use of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) to impose his sweeping global tariffs, ruling that the president lacked the authority to do so.

The White House has prepared a new round of levies targeting countries over a range of allegations, including the failure to address forced labour.

“We expect to see some action soon,” Greer said in the interview, but he did not specify a timeline. He stressed that the new tariffs could cover a majority of US trade, fuelling increased tensions with trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union.

The announcement follows a new round of tariffs unveiled last week on Brazilian goods. The White House announced 25 percent duties on thousands of imports from the South American nation, ranging from sugar to steel.

Then on Monday, the White House announced a new 50 percent tariff on goods ranging from wine to cement, which will take effect in 30 days, alleging that Ottawa has subjected US products, including automobiles and dairy goods, to “discriminatory treatment”.



“President Trump is taking action to hold Canada accountable for its continued discrimination against and unreasonable and unequal treatment of US commerce that has burdened and disadvantaged hardworking Americans,” the White House said in a release on the heels of the announcement.

However, it is US consumers and businesses that bear most of the cost of Trump’s tariffs. Analysis by the Kiel Institute for the World Economy found that US importers and consumers shoulder 96 percent of the burden, while the nonpartisan Tax Foundation estimates that the tariffs will increase the average tax burden on US households by about $700.

US markets are in positive territory. The Nasdaq is up 0.8 percent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up by 0.6 percent, and the S&P 500 rose by 0.5 percent in midday trading.

World.title: Italy’s Meloni slams protesters following clashes in Bologna
World.content:
PM pledges probe into death of Moroccan man under police restraint, condemns violence as protests injure 56 officers.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has condemned demonstrators in Bologna, after protests over the death of a Moroccan man under police restraint left dozens of officers injured.

Speaking on Tuesday, the right-wing premier pledged that the death of Abderrahim Fakir would be investigated fairly, but accused overnight protests of seeking “confrontation” rather than “truth”.

The 42-year-old Fakir died on Sunday after police were called to deal with a man behaving aggressively and damaging a vehicle.

Protests broke out on Sunday night, and as they resumed on Monday evening in central Bologna, they clashed with police.

Demonstrators hurled firecrackers, bottles and chairs at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons. The Italian Coordination of Police Officers reported that 56 officers were injured.

“Those who chose to use this incident as a pretext to lay waste to the city, attack officers and spread violence … were not seeking the truth: they were seeking confrontation,” Meloni declared.

She added that “any responsibilities” must “be ascertained with the utmost rigour” and that the truth must be pursued “without prejudice and without leniency toward anyone”.

Footage of Fakir’s final moments, widely shared online, shows him face down while two officers restrain him and he calls for help and says he can not breathe before falling still.



The footage has drawn comparisons to the 2020 killing of George Floyd by United States police in Minneapolis.

Prosecutors have opened an investigation, reigniting debate in Italy over the use of force during arrests.

Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi said he had “full confidence” the inquiry would establish the facts, telling the daily Il Messaggero that officers deserve the same “presumption of innocence” as any other citizen.

The case has drawn reactions across the political spectrum.

Members of the populist right-wing governing coalition have defended the officers involved.

Opposition politicians have criticised the government for its handling of the incident and claimed that its policies promote violence.

Centre-left legislator Francesco Boccia warned against Italy adopting an “ICE model” of policing, referring to the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, which has been involved in several killings of protesters.

Lawyer Barbara Spinelli, who had met Fakir last year when he applied to renew his residency permit, told the ANSA news agency that he was “a very kind, well-educated, respectful person” who had worried about being expelled from Italy despite living there legally.

World.title: FIFA ‘destroying football’ for the World Cup, says Spanish football chief
World.content:
The president of the Spanish football league, Javier Tebas, has accused FIFA of acting “irresponsibly” following the announcement of discussions regarding a possible 64-team World Cup in 2030, in an interview with an Italian sports daily.

Tebas also said that FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s time was “over” in the interview published in La Gazzetta dello Sport on Tuesday.

He lamented the manner in which FIFA’s leadership is elected, terming it a system that is “fundamentally flawed”, which has allowed Infantino to lead football’s global governing body for a decade.

“The football industry is not just about the World Cup, however important it may be,” he said.

“They are destroying the football industry – which generates tens of thousands of jobs – for an event that lasts 40 days and involves only a minority of players.”

At the World Cup opening ceremony in June, Infantino mentioned “discussions about expanding to 64 teams” for the World Cup’s centenary in 2030, which will be cohosted primarily by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina also welcoming some matches.

“We have repeatedly expressed our concerns about the competition calendar. And now they want to organise a 64-team World Cup,” Tebas added, emphasising that “it is the domestic leagues that keep this sport alive”.

“We need fewer national teams and better protection for domestic football at all levels. They don’t realise this and are making decisions irresponsibly,” Tebas added.

FIFA has not responded to Al Jazeera’s request for a comment following the accusations levelled by La Liga’s Tebas.

World.title: Saudi condemns Houthi blockade: How will the rest of the world be impacted?
World.content:
Saudi Arabia has condemned the Houthi naval blockade that could impact oil flow to importers of Saudi oil.
